https://leadership.ng/russia-denies-usin.summary: The embassy also cited Russia’s record under the Chemical Weapons Convention, stating that the country completed the verified destruction of its declared chemical weapons stockpile in 2017 under the supervision of the OPCW Technical Secretariat. Beyond the battlefield allegations, Russia accused Ukrainian forces of targeting chemical-industrial facilities containing hazardous substances, including the Azot and Metafrax plants in the Perm region on September 11.
https://leadership.ng/russia-denies-usin.summary_zh: 大使馆还援引了俄罗斯在《禁止化学武器公约》下的履约记录，称该国已于2017年在禁止化学武器组织技术秘书处的监督下完成对已申报化学武器库存的核验销毁。除战场相关指控外，俄罗斯还指责乌克兰军队袭击存放危险物质的化工设施，包括9月11日位于彼尔姆地区的Azot和Metafrax工厂。
https://leadership.ng/russia-denies-usin.body: The denial followed a recent publication by Ukraine’s Ambassador to Nigeria, Ivan Kholostenko, who alleged that 14,009 incidents involving chemical substances were recorded between February 2023 and September 2026. Kholostenko also claimed that Ukrainian servicemen sought medical attention in 6,021 cases after experiencing symptoms of chemical exposure of varying severity. However, the Russian Embassy in Abuja, in a statement on Sunday, described the allegations as a “chemistry of double standards,” accusing Kyiv of using statistics to portray Russia as guilty without presenting sufficient evidence. The Russian Mission also questioned the consistency of Ukraine’s figures, citing a report by Ukraine’s Permanent Representative to the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (OPCW), Andriy Kostin, who reportedly presented 3,632 cases involving symptoms of chemical injury on October 8, 2026. “While Kholostenko claims that 6,021 Ukrainian servicemen sought medical assistance following chemical exposure, his colleague Andriy Kostin, Ukraine’s Permanent Representative to the OPCW, reported 3,632 cases involving symptoms of chemical injury on October 8, 2026,” the statement said. Russia categorically rejected the allegations, insisting that riot control agents were not issued to its armed forces and that their use was not part of its battlefield tactics. The embassy also cited Russia’s record under the Chemical Weapons Convention, stating that the country completed the verified destruction of its declared chemical weapons stockpile in 2017 under the supervision of the OPCW Technical Secretariat. It said Russia had consistently advocated for the depoliticisation of the organisation and its restoration as an impartial technical body responsible for ensuring compliance with the convention. The Russian Mission further accused Ukrainian forces of using toxic chemicals, claiming that Moscow had repeatedly submitted laboratory findings, photographs of recovered munitions and other evidence to the OPCW. It also alleged that Western-manufactured chemical devices and supplies of toxic substances and precursors, including CS, CR and BZ agents, had been provided to Ukraine. According to the embassy, investigations had exposed the involvement of foreign suppliers in providing Ukrainian forces with hazardous chemical materials. It criticised what it described as the limited attention given to these allegations by Ukraine’s Western allies, arguing that evidence should be examined impartially, regardless of which party it implicates. The embassy also questioned the OPCW’s handling of technical assistance requests, claiming that Ukraine had received three technical assistance visits while Russia’s corresponding request remained under consultation. It argued that the situation raised questions about whether the Chemical Weapons Convention was being applied equally to all member states. Beyond the battlefield allegations, Russia accused Ukrainian forces of targeting chemical-industrial facilities containing hazardous substances, including the Azot and Metafrax plants in the Perm region on September 11. The embassy warned that attacks on such facilities could trigger toxic releases, environmental disasters and civilian casualties. It also alleged that Ukraine could stage chemical incidents to implicate Russia, particularly as Ukrainian forces faced mounting difficulties on the battlefield. Addressing the OPCW’s findings, the Russian Mission acknowledged that the organisation had confirmed the presence of CS in certain samples collected in Ukraine. However, it cited a statement attributed to the OPCW Director-General on October 6, arguing that laboratory analysis alone did not establish the use of riot control agents as a method of warfare. The embassy further maintained that the organisation had not attributed Ukraine’s 14,009 alleged incidents to Russia, accusing the Ukrainian ambassador of presenting allegations as established facts. It also criticised NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte over remarks it said encouraged attributing incidents to Russia when responsibility was considered highly likely. The Russian Mission argued that such an approach undermined the principles of impartial investigation and evidence-based attribution in international affairs. It accused Kyiv and its Western allies of attempting to draw the OPCW into geopolitical disputes, insisting that the organisation should uphold the Chemical Weapons Convention rather than endorse politically motivated accusations. “Impressive numbers are no substitute for convincing evidence, and repeating an allegation does not make it true,” the embassy stated. The Russian Mission said it would continue presenting what it described as evidence of Ukrainian violations and pressing for the convention to be applied equally to all states parties. It also urged the OPCW to maintain its independence and credibility, warning against its use as an instrument for advancing the geopolitical interests of individual governments. The embassy concluded that preserving the independence of international institutions was particularly important for Nigeria and other countries committed to multilateralism. It accused Kyiv and its Western allies of combining allegations, selective evidence and political pressure in an attempt to influence the OPCW’s findings. We’ve got the edge. https://leadership.ng/russia-denies-usin.title_zh: 俄罗斯否认对乌克兰军队使用化学武器
https://leadership.ng/russia-denies-usin.body_zh: 这一否认是在乌克兰驻尼日利亚大使伊万·霍洛斯坚科最近发表的一篇文章之后提出的，他声称2023年2月至2026年9月期间记录了14009起涉及化学物质的事件。霍洛斯坚科还声称，乌克兰军人因出现不同程度化学接触症状而在6021起病例中寻求医疗救助。然而，俄罗斯驻阿布贾大使馆在周日的一份声明中将这些指控描述为“双重标准的化学反应”，指责基辅利用统计数据将俄罗斯描绘成有罪一方，却没有提供充分证据。俄罗斯使团还质疑乌克兰数据的连贯性，援引乌克兰常驻禁止化学武器组织代表安德烈·科斯京的一份报告，据称他在2026年10月8日提交了3632起涉及化学伤害症状的病例。“虽然霍洛斯坚科声称6021名乌克兰军人因化学接触后寻求医疗帮助，但他的同事、乌克兰常驻禁止化学武器组织代表安德烈·科斯京在2026年10月8日报告了3632起涉及化学伤害症状的病例，”声明说。俄罗斯断然拒绝这些指控，坚持认为其武装部队没有配备防暴控制剂，而且其战场战术中不包括使用此类物质。大使馆还援引俄罗斯在《化学武器公约》下的记录，指出该国在禁止化学武器组织技术秘书处监督下于2017年完成了对其申报化学武器库存的核实销毁。它表示俄罗斯一贯主张该组织去政治化，并恢复其作为确保遵守公约的中立技术机构的地位。俄罗斯使团进一步指责乌克兰部队使用有毒化学物质，声称莫斯科已多次向禁止化学武器组织提交实验室结果、回收弹药的照片和其他证据。它还指称西方制造的化学装置以及有毒物质和前体（包括CS、CR和BZ剂）已被提供给乌克兰。据大使馆称，调查已揭露外国供应商参与向乌克兰部队提供危险化学材料。它批评乌克兰西方盟友对这些指控给予的关注有限，认为证据应得到公正审查，无论它牵涉哪一方。大使馆还质疑禁止化学武器组织对技术援助请求的处理，声称乌克兰已收到三次技术援助访问，而俄罗斯相应的请求仍处于磋商中。它认为这种情况引发了关于《化学武器公约》是否平等适用于所有成员国的问题。除了战场指控之外，俄罗斯还指责乌克兰部队针对含有危险物质的化工设施，包括9月11日位于彼尔姆地区的Azot和Metafrax工厂。大使馆警告说，对此类设施的袭击可能引发有毒物质释放、环境灾难和平民伤亡。它还指称乌克兰可能策划化学事件来牵连俄罗斯，特别是随着乌克兰部队在战场上面临越来越大的困难。在谈到禁止化学武器组织的调查结果时，俄罗斯使团承认该组织已确认在乌克兰收集的某些样本中存在CS。然而，它援引据称是禁止化学武器组织总干事在10月6日发表的声明，认为仅凭实验室分析无法确定将防暴控制剂用作战争方法。大使馆进一步坚持认为，该组织并未将乌克兰声称的14009起事件归咎于俄罗斯，指责乌克兰大使将指控当作既定事实呈现。它还批评北约秘书长马克·吕特发表的言论，称这些言论鼓励在认为责任极有可能时将事件归咎于俄罗斯。俄罗斯使团认为这种做法破坏了国际事务中公正调查和基于证据归因的原则。它指责基辅及其西方盟友试图将禁止化学武器组织拖入地缘政治争端，坚持认为该组织应维护《化学武器公约》，而不是支持出于政治动机的指控。“令人印象深刻的数字不能替代令人信服的证据，重复指控并不能使其成为事实，”大使馆指出。俄罗斯使团表示，它将继续提交其所描述的乌克兰违反行为的证据，并敦促公约平等适用于所有缔约国。它还敦促禁止化学武器组织保持其独立性和公信力，警告不要将其用作推进个别政府地缘政治利益的工具。大使馆最后表示，维护国际机构的独立性对尼日利亚和其他致力于多边主义的国家尤为重要。它指责基辅及其西方盟友将指控、选择性证据和政治压力结合起来，试图影响禁止化学武器组织的调查结果。我们拥有优势。获取实时报道、突发独家新闻和独家视角，直接发送到您的手机。不要满足于陈旧新闻。加入LEADERSHIP NEWS的WhatsApp，获取24/7更新→

https://billygraham.org/decision-magazin.title: ‘An Absolute Human Tragedy’: Christian Genocide in Nigeria
https://billygraham.org/decision-magazin.summary: Written by: Jerry Pierce In 2002, the year Islamic terrorist group Boko Haram was founded in northeast Nigeria, a band of jihadists attacked a Christian church in the region, burning the building to the ground and murdering multiple members, including the pastor.
https://billygraham.org/decision-magazin.summary_zh: 作者：杰里·皮尔斯 2002年，也就是伊斯兰恐怖组织博科哈拉姆在尼日利亚东北部成立的那一年，一伙圣战分子袭击了该地区的一座基督教教堂，将建筑焚烧殆尽，并杀害多名成员，其中包括牧师。
https://billygraham.org/decision-magazin.body: Written by: Jerry Pierce In 2002, the year Islamic terrorist group Boko Haram was founded in northeast Nigeria, a band of jihadists attacked a Christian church in the region, burning the building to the ground and murdering multiple members, including the pastor. The attack was a shocking precursor to what’s transpired in the years since as Boko Haram, which aims to implement strict Sharia law across all of Nigeria—including in the Christian South—began to spread its murderous ideology. More than a decade later, terrorists struck the same church, which had rebuilt and continued to meet. This time, machete-wielding jihadists beheaded the widow of the late pastor and killed the youngest of her five children. Then last April, on Good Friday, militants hit the same church yet again, setting it ablaze as part of a larger round of deadly attacks on Easter weekend across Nigeria’s North and Middle Belt. The pastor—who as a child had lived through his father’s murder, then his mother’s beheading and his youngest sibling’s death—survived the attack, and the congregation, with help from a Nigeria-based ministry, has been able to salvage much of the church building and reopen. But many Christians living in the Muslim-majority North, especially in rural areas, are not as fortunate. Of the victims who survive, thousands end up in camps for internally displaced persons (IDPs) or hiding in forests, where many die from injuries, disease, lack of clean water or malnutrition. Multiple sources working among displaced Christians in northern Nigeria told Decision similar stories of sustained, systematic violence by jihadists toward Christian churches and communities, often while government security forces wait nearby until the attacks cease before responding. There is also a government narrative often repeated by the international community and some press agencies that the violence stems mostly from “complex” disputes between Muslim herders and Christian farmers and that no genocide exists. In fact, the Nigerian government spent $9 million in the last year to hire Washington, D.C., lobbying firm DCI Group to help boost its image inside the Beltway. And it has been trumpeting a few instances this year where it rescued Christian captives and cooperated with U.S. military interventions, including one that eradicated the Islamic State’s global No. 2 leader. Yet with Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) operating in Nigeria’s northwest, Boko Haram in the northeast, and both groups radicalizing and arming young, uneducated Fulani herdsmen to wreak havoc, the Nigerian government’s narrative is hard to square with the statistics and reports from aid workers. Life for the Christian minority in the North is a contrast to the Christian South. In northern Nigeria, 12 states have Sharia written into their civil codes. Muslims caught converting to Christ from Islam face possible death sentences. Even liberal atheist comedian Bill Maher—unlike most of the American mainstream media—has noticed. “I’m not a Christian, but they are systematically killing the Christians in Nigeria,” he said on his HBO show while discussing the jihadist elements in Nigeria, adding, “They are literally attempting to wipe out the Christian population of an entire country. Where are the kids protesting this?” “The fact that this issue has not gotten on people’s radar, it’s pretty amazing,” Maher noted. In just the first six months of 2026, 2,500 Nigerian Christians had been murdered, 2,800 abducted, 800 forced to convert to Islam, and 300 churches destroyed. By Sept. 8, the number of dead had swelled to more than 4,200. “Every morning I get a report from our teams,” said Brad Brandon, a former U.S. pastor who leads a ministry called Across Nigeria. In a late September phone interview, he told Decision , “I think there were 30 people that have been killed so far this week. It’s ridiculous how many people are being slaughtered and nothing is being done.” Since 2009, the death toll for Christians has been staggering: Estimates range from 80,000 martyrs on the low end, upward to 130,000. Another 12 million have been displaced by the violence in those 17 years, according to statistics cited by CeCe Heil, who was appointed by Senate Majority Leader John Thune in May to a term on the U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom. Heil, an attorney with the American Center for Law and Justice, which has long championed the plight of Nigeria’s Christians, acknowledges that land and ethnic disputes happen, but they are a fraction of the conflict. Brandon echoed Heil’s assessment, as did the leader of a Nigerian-led non-governmental organization (NGO) that has been helping thousands of orphans, widows and displaced people find practical and spiritual hope for more than 17 years. “In the large majority of attacks,” said the NGO leader, who asked that her name be withheld, “Christians are targeted, and we can prove that by data. They live in fear, but they also walk in courage. They are not prone to run away because of their faith.” In 12 years, Brandon’s shoes have stood on dirt clods from freshly dug graves more times than he wishes to count. One recent example, he said, was an attack in June in the northwest Nigerian settlement of Larabar Zango. “When we got there, 14 people had been massacred, two pregnant women and a 4-year-old boy among the victims. And by the way, that wasn’t a farming community.” Brandon said many people are surprised to learn that his ministry works among both Christian communities and some Fulani clans in the North. He said while young, radicalized Fulani males commit much of the violence, especially in Nigeria’s Middle Belt, most of Nigeria’s 17 million Fulani people, who are about 95% Muslim, are largely illiterate and not ideological. On the other hand, the radicalized Fulani responsible for much of the violence number about 30,000—fewer than half a percent of the Fulani ethnic group. But those 30,000, supplied with AK-47s and dirt bikes by Boko Haram and ISWAP, are largely undeterred by security forces and often paid for each act of terrorism. In October 2025, the Trump State Department restored Country of Particular Concern (CPC) status to Nigeria after the Biden administration removed it in 2021. CPCs represent the world’s most severe violators of human rights. The CPC label limits Nigeria’s trade and financial transactions with U.S.-based entities. Annually, the State Department is mandated by Congress to review the status of CPC nations. Nigeria’s was due to be reviewed in October. Nigeria is Africa’s most populous nation and largest economy, with sizable gold and oil reserves and home to four of the continent’s largest airlines. The CPC designation matters to leaders in the capital city of Abuja. “Don’t be fooled,” Brandon warned. “If there’s anything the Nigerian government has perfected the art of, it is to put up window dressing and make everything look like they’ve done what they’ve been asked to do.” Brandon and the NGO leader both told Decision that the government’s efforts to quell the violence are largely a ruse. “The security forces take the videos and show the soldiers who are on the scene dealing with the situation. But they don’t show up until hours after the attack,” Brandon said. “In my own personal experience, those security forces were just 20 minutes down the road.” Even worse, Brandon said he has repeatedly heard of Nigerian forces watching as Boko Haram soldiers arrived to destroy Christian communities. The NGO leader corroborated Brandon’s claim. On Capitol Hill, Rep. Riley Moore (R-W.Va.), a freshman congressman whom Trump tapped along with Oklahoma Republican Rep. Tom Cole to lead an investigation into the Nigerian genocide last October, said his Christian faith drives him to pray for Nigeria daily. “It is an absolute human tragedy over there,” Moore told Decision . “But please keep praying. I believe in the power of prayer. And raise awareness. Talk to your members of Congress.” If the terrorism continues unabated, Moore said, it could destabilize the entire African continent. “Left unchecked, northern Nigeria could become a new caliphate and a major base for global terrorist operations, and that would pose direct national security risks to the United States,” he warned. But even amid unspeakable heartbreak, the Gospel message can’t be stymied. Brandon said Across Nigeria has led more than 7,000 Fulani to faith in Christ since 2014, often by building trust with local chieftains through digging water wells and providing education and basic medical care. https://billygraham.org/decision-magazin.title_zh: “一场彻头彻尾的人类悲剧”：尼日利亚基督徒遭种族灭绝
https://billygraham.org/decision-magazin.body_zh:
撰文：杰里·皮尔斯

2002年，也就是伊斯兰恐怖组织“博科圣地”成立于尼日利亚东北部的同一年，一伙圣战分子袭击了当地一座基督教教堂，纵火将建筑夷为平地，并杀害多名成员，其中包括牧师。这次袭击是此后一系列事件的惊人前奏：“博科圣地”企图在整个尼日利亚——包括基督徒为主的南部——实施严格的伊斯兰教法，并开始散布其杀人的意识形态。十多年后，恐怖分子再次袭击同一座教堂；这座教堂已重建并继续举行聚会。这一次，手持砍刀的圣战分子斩首了已故牧师的遗孀，并杀死她5个孩子中最年幼的一个。去年4月，耶稣受难日，武装分子又一次袭击这座教堂，纵火将其烧毁；这是尼日利亚北部和中部地区复活节周末更大规模致命袭击的一部分。牧师小时候曾目睹父亲被杀，随后又经历母亲被斩首、幼弟死亡，却在这场袭击中幸存；在一家总部位于尼日利亚的事工机构帮助下，会众抢救出了教堂建筑的大部分，并重新开放。

但生活在穆斯林占多数的北部、尤其是农村地区的许多基督徒就没有这么幸运。在幸存受害者中，数千人最终进入境内流离失所者营地，或躲进森林，许多人因伤势、疾病、缺乏清洁水源或营养不良而死亡。多名在尼日利亚北部流离失所基督徒中开展工作的消息人士向《Decision》讲述了类似情况：圣战分子持续、系统性地针对基督教教堂和社区实施暴力，而政府安全部队往往在附近等待，直到袭击停止后才作出反应。国际社会和某些新闻机构经常重复政府的一套说法，称暴力主要源于穆斯林牧民与基督徒农民之间的“复杂”纠纷，并不存在种族灭绝。事实上，尼日利亚政府去年花费900万美元，雇用位于华盛顿特区的游说机构DCI Group，帮助改善其在华盛顿政治圈中的形象。今年，该政府还大肆宣扬了几起营救基督徒俘虏以及配合美国军事干预的案例，其中包括一次消灭“伊斯兰国”全球二号头目的行动。然而，“伊斯兰国西非省”（ISWAP）在尼日利亚西北部活动，“博科圣地”在东北部活动，两组织还在使年轻、未受教育的富拉尼牧民激进化并武装他们，以制造浩劫。在这种情况下，尼日利亚政府的说法很难与救援人员的统计和报告相吻合。

北部基督徒少数群体的生活与基督徒占多数的南部形成鲜明反差。在尼日利亚北部，12个州已将伊斯兰教法写入民法体系。穆斯林若被发现在脱离伊斯兰教后改信基督教，可能面临死刑判决。就连持自由主义无神论立场的喜剧演员比尔·马赫——与大多数美国主流媒体不同——也注意到了这一点。他说：“我不是基督徒，但他们正在有系统地杀害尼日利亚的基督徒。”他在HBO节目中讨论尼日利亚的圣战分子时补充道：“他们实际上正试图消灭整个国家的基督徒人口。孩子们在哪里抗议这件事？”马赫指出：“这个问题竟然还没有引起人们的注意，实在太令人震惊了。”

仅在2026年前6个月，就有2,500名尼日利亚基督徒遇害、2,800人遭绑架、800人被迫改信伊斯兰教，300座教堂被毁。截至9月8日，死亡人数已增至4,200多人。曾任美国牧师、现领导一个名为“Across Nigeria”的事工机构的布拉德·布兰登说：“每天早上，我都会收到我们团队提交的报告。”9月下旬接受《Decision》电话采访时，他说：“我认为截至本周，已有30人被杀。这么多人遭到屠杀，却什么都没做，实在荒唐。”

自2009年以来，基督徒死亡人数触目惊心：估计数字从低端的8万名殉道者到高端的13万人不等。据CeCe Heil援引的统计数据，在这17年的暴力中，另有1,200万人被迫流离失所。Heil于5月获参议院多数党领袖约翰·图恩任命，出任美国国际宗教自由委员会任期成员。Heil是American Center for Law and Justice的律师；该机构长期为尼日利亚基督徒的困境奔走。她承认，土地和族群纠纷确实存在，但这些冲突只占整体冲突的一小部分。布兰登赞同Heil的评估，一个由尼日利亚人领导、帮助数千名孤儿、寡妇和流离失所者寻找现实与精神希望的非政府组织的负责人也持相同看法。这名负责人要求不公开姓名。她表示：“在绝大多数袭击中，基督徒都是目标，我们可以用数据证明这一点。他们生活在恐惧中，但也勇敢前行。他们不会因为自己的信仰而逃逃。”

12年来，布兰登多少次站在新挖坟墓的土块上，连他自己都不愿去数。他说，最近的一个例子是6月发生在尼日利亚西北部聚居地拉拉巴尔赞戈的一次袭击。“我们赶到时，14人已被屠杀，遇害者中有两名孕妇和一个4岁男孩。顺便说一句，那并不是一个农业社区。”

布兰登说，许多人得知他的事工机构同时服务于基督徒社区和北部一些富拉尼宗族后，都感到惊讶。他说，虽然实施大量暴力的主要是年轻、激进化富拉尼男子，特别是在尼日利亚中部地区，但尼日利亚1,700万富拉尼人中的大多数——约95%为穆斯林——基本不识字，也没有意识形态倾向。另一方面，为大量暴力负责的激进化富拉尼人约有3万人，不到富拉尼族群人口的0.5%。然而，这3万人获得“博科圣地”和ISWAP提供的AK-47突击步枪和越野摩托车，几乎不受安全部队威慑，而且往往每实施一次恐怖活动都能获得报酬。

2025年10月，特朗普政府的国务院恢复了将尼日利亚列为“特别关注国家”（CPC）的地位，而拜登政府曾于2021年取消这一 designation。CPC代表世界上最严重侵犯人权的国家。CPC标签限制尼日利亚与美国境内实体之间的贸易和金融交易。国务院每年都须依据国会要求，审查CPC国家的地位。尼日利亚的审查时间原定在10月。尼日利亚是非洲人口最多、经济规模最大的国家，拥有可观的黄金和石油储量，非洲四大航空公司中有四家总部设于此。CPC designation对首都阿布贾的领导人而言十分重要。

布兰登警告说：“别被骗了。如果尼日利亚政府有什么特别精通，那就是粉饰门面，让一切看起来都像是他们完成了别人要求他们做的事。”布兰登和上述非政府组织负责人都告诉《Decision》，政府遏制暴力的努力在很大程度上只是幌子。布兰登说：“安全部队会拍摄视频，展示士兵在现场处理情况。但袭击过去好几个小时，他们才出现。”他说：“就我个人经历而言，安全部队当时其实只在20分钟路程之外。”更糟的是，布兰登说，他多次听说尼日利亚安全部队眼睁睁看着“博科圣地”成员赶到并摧毁基督徒社区。非政府组织负责人证实了布兰登的说法。

在美国国会山，特朗普于去年10月与俄克拉何马州共和党众议员汤姆·科尔一起任命新任众议员赖利·摩尔（西弗吉尼亚州共和党）领导对尼日利亚种族灭绝的调查。摩尔告诉《Decision》，自己的基督徒信仰促使他每天为尼日利亚祈祷：“那里是一场彻头彻尾的人类悲剧。但请继续祈祷。我相信祈祷的力量。还要提高关注度，与你们的国会议员沟通。”

摩尔说，如果恐怖主义持续不受遏制，可能会破坏整个非洲大陆的稳定。他警告说：“如果不加控制，尼日利亚北部可能成为一个新的哈里发国，并成为全球恐怖行动的主要基地，那将对美国构成直接的国家安全威胁。”然而，即便遭遇难以言喻的悲痛，福音信息仍无法被遏止。布兰登说，自2014年以来，“Across Nigeria”已带领7,000多名富拉尼人信奉基督；该机构常通过打井、 提供教育和基本医疗服务，与当地酋长建立信任。上图：尼日利亚每年因信仰而遇害的基督徒人数，超过其他所有国家的总和

https://www.tvcnews.tv/police-rescue-11-.summary: The Nigeria Police Force has reported a series of operational successes across six states in the last 48 hours, including the rescue of 11 abducted persons, the arrest of suspects linked to criminal activities and the recovery of livestock, motorcycles and firearms.

https://www.tvcnews.tv/police-rescue-11-.body: The Nigeria Police Force has reported a series of operational successes across six states in the last 48 hours, including the rescue of 11 abducted persons, the arrest of suspects linked to criminal activities and the recovery of livestock, motorcycles and firearms. In a statement signed by the Force Public…... The Nigeria Police Force has reported a series of operational successes across six states in the last 48 hours, including the rescue of 11 abducted persons, the arrest of suspects linked to criminal activities and the recovery of livestock, motorcycles and firearms. In a statement signed by the Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Ani Iniedu, the Police said five elderly women abducted by armed bandits while harvesting beans on a farm in Dansadau, Maru Local Government Area of Zamfara State, were rescued unhurt following a confrontation between the assailants and security operatives. The incident occurred on October 29, 2026, at about 12:30 p.m., when the bandits attacked the farm and killed a 35-year-old farmer before abducting the women. Police tactical teams, supported by local vigilantes, pursued the attackers and engaged them in a gun duel, forcing them to abandon the victims and flee. The Police said bush-combing and tracking operations were ongoing to apprehend the fleeing suspects. In Niger State, a joint security operation involving the Police, military, Department of State Services, special hunters and local vigilantes rescued six farmers abducted from Mahangi Village, via Pandogari, in Rafi Local Government Area. The operation, conducted on October 29, led security operatives to the bandits’ hideout, where the victims were successfully rescued. They were taken to the police division for profiling ahead of their reunion with their families. Meanwhile, joint security forces in Kebbi State repelled an attack by suspected Lakurawa members on Ribah Town in Danko Wasagu Local Government Area. The attackers reportedly struck at about 8:15 p.m. on October 30 after an earlier attempt to block Rambo Junction was foiled by security operatives. They later regrouped and opened fire from different directions but were engaged and repelled by the joint forces. In Kano State, Police operatives arrested five suspects allegedly linked to the harbouring of criminals during an operation targeting individuals connected to the kidnapping of Alhaji Abdu Fanka, the APC chairman of Rogo Local Government Area. The Police Anti-Kidnapping Squad reportedly stormed the residence of the suspects, but the principal suspects escaped after raising an alarm. Operatives, however, arrested five persons and recovered 48 cows, 43 sheep and two Bajaj Boxer motorcycles during the operation. In Katsina State, tactical teams foiled an attempted bandit attack on Karofi Village in Dutsin-Ma Local Government Area. The Police said operatives responded to a distress call at about 11:27 p.m. on October 29 and intercepted the attackers, engaging them in a gun duel that forced them to retreat into the bush. No casualties were recorded among security personnel or civilians, while joint patrols and bush-combing operations continued. In Lagos State, Police operatives arrested a 28-year-old suspected cultist identified as Ojo/Ojomu Bolanle, popularly known as “Burna”, following an armed robbery and shooting at Desa Bus Stop, Ibeju-Lekki. The incident occurred on October 31 at about 11:30 a.m., when operatives responded to an ongoing robbery involving a Point of Sale operator, Ibrahim Adewale Moronfade, who was shot and later died. A search conducted after the arrest led to the recovery of a locally made pistol, an expended cartridge and charms. The Police also said the stolen handbag and other property were traced to the robbery. The Force said investigations into the incidents were ongoing, with the relevant State Criminal Investigation Departments handling the cases in the affected states
https://www.tvcnews.tv/police-rescue-11-.title_zh: 警方在6个州解救了11名被绑架妇女和农民，并逮捕嫌疑人
https://www.tvcnews.tv/police-rescue-11-.body_zh: 尼日利亚警察部队在过去48小时内报告了横跨6个州的一系列行动成果，包括营救11名被绑架人员、逮捕与犯罪活动有关的嫌疑人，以及追回牲畜、摩托车和枪支。在由警察部队公共关系官CSP Ani Iniedu签署的声明中，警察表示，赞法拉州马鲁地方政府区Dansadau一处农场发生武装匪徒袭击时，5名正在收获豆子的年长妇女遭绑架；在袭击者与安全人员对峙后，这5人获救且未受伤。事件发生于2026年10月29日约中午12时30分，当时匪徒袭击农场并杀死一名35岁农民，随后绑架这些妇女。在当地民兵支援下，警察战术小组追击袭击者并与其交火，迫使他们弃下受害者逃离。警察称，搜山和追踪行动仍在继续，以缉捕在逃嫌疑人。在尼日尔州，警察、军方、国家安全局、特别猎手和当地民兵联合开展安全行动，从拉菲地方政府区经Pandogari前往Mahangi Village，营救6名遭绑架的农民。这次行动于10月29日展开，安全人员追至匪徒藏身处，成功救出受害者，随后将他们送往警察分局登记建档，以便与家人团聚。与此同时，Kebbi州联合安全部队击退了疑似Lakurawa成员对Danko Wasagu地方政府区Ribah Town的袭击。据报道，袭击者于10月30日约晚上8时15分发动袭击，此前他们企图封锁Rambo Junction，但被安全人员挫败。他们随后重新集结，从不同方向开火，但遭到联合部队迎击并被击退。在Kano州，警察人员在一次针对与绑架Rogo地方政府区APC主席Alhaji Abdu Fanka有关人员的行动中，逮捕了5名涉嫌窝藏罪犯的嫌疑人。据报道，警察反绑架小组突袭嫌疑人住所，但主要嫌疑人在发出警报后逃脱。不过，行动人员仍逮捕了5人，并追回48头牛、43只羊和2辆Bajaj Boxer摩托车。在Katsina州，战术小组挫败了匪徒对Dutsin-Ma地方政府区Karofi Village的袭击企图。警察称，行动人员于10月29日约晚上11时27分接到求救电话后迅速响应，截住袭击者并与其交火，迫使他们撤入丛林。安全人员和平民均无人员伤亡，联合巡逻和搜山行动仍在继续。在Lagos州，警察人员于Ibeju-Lekki的Desa Bus Stop发生武装抢劫和枪击事件后，逮捕了一名28岁的疑似邪教成员，此人名为Ojo/Ojomu Bolanle，俗称“Burna”。事件发生于10月31日上午约11时30分，行动人员赶到时，一起涉及销售终端运营商Ibrahim Adewale Moronfade的抢劫仍在进行；Ibrahim Adewale Moronfade中枪后死亡。逮捕行动结束后展开的搜查发现并追回一把本地制造的手枪、一枚击发过的弹壳和数件护身符。警察还表示，已追回抢劫案中失窃的手提包及其他财物。警察部队称，对这些事件的调查仍在进行，受影响各州的相关州刑事调查部门正在处理案件……

https://leadership.ng/500-calabar-market.title: 500 Calabar Market Women Receive N50,000 Each From Tinubu’s Wife
https://leadership.ng/500-calabar-market.summary: The beneficiaries received the financial assistance during a market outreach organised by the First Lady through Dr Betta Edu, which attracted more than 5,000 women from different markets across the city. Beyond the cash grants, the women received gift items, including deep freezers, blenders, toasters and luxury dresses.
https://leadership.ng/500-calabar-market.summary_zh: 受益者通过第一夫人委托贝塔·埃杜博士组织的巡回宣传活动领取了这笔经济援助，活动吸引了全市不同市场的5000多名女性参加。除了现金补助，这些女性还获得了包括深冷柜、搅拌机、烤面包机和奢华连衣裙在内的礼品。
https://leadership.ng/500-calabar-market.body: The beneficiaries received the financial assistance during a market outreach organised by the First Lady through Dr Betta Edu, which attracted more than 5,000 women from different markets across the city. Edu said the intervention was intended to help small-scale traders replenish their stocks, expand their businesses and improve their ability to support their families. “For many of the beneficiaries who struggle to keep a business of N10,000 alive, it can mean fresh stock, a bigger business, renewed hope and another opportunity to provide for her family,” she said. Beyond the cash grants, the women received gift items, including deep freezers, blenders, toasters and luxury dresses. Some participants also won financial grants through a dance competition organised at the event. The outreach, however, also served as a political mobilisation exercise for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu and Cross River State Governor Bassey Otu, as participants danced, celebrated and offered prayers for the President. One of the beneficiaries, Mrs Hogan Bassey, who won a deep freezer, expressed appreciation to the President and the First Lady. “God bless you, Mr President. Cross River will vote for you and Sweet Prince,” she said, referring to Governor Otu. Edu, who is the Co-Director of the Women Mobilisation Directorate of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, urged the women to mobilise support for the party ahead of the next election. Unlock these with Subscription Published - November 01, 2026 10:07 pm IST - GELEPHU (BHUTAN) Bhutan King Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuk on Sunday (November 1, 2026) dedicated one of the 108 Buddhist stupas erected in a nine-hour construction feat to Prime Minister Narendra Modi as a mark of appreciation for India’s support for the country’s ambitious Gelephu Mindfulness City (GMC) project. About 40,000 trained volunteers built the 108 Jangchub Chortens in what could be a potentially record-breaking royal initiative to lay the spiritual foundation of the planned city. About 240 km south-southeast of Bhutan’s capital, Thimphu, Gelephu borders Assam’s Chirang district. King Wangchuk envisions the city as a spirituality-driven global economic hub. The King, other members of the royal family, top officials and foreign dignitaries faced Chorten Number 79 from the ceremonial ground as thousands of people around chanted a six-syllable Tibetan Buddhist mantra a billion times while the volunteers completed the mission between 3 a.m. and 12 noon. About two hours later, the focus shifted to Chorten Number 76, which the King dedicated to Mr. Modi “as an enduring symbol” of his “profound appreciation” for the latter’s “unwavering commitment and India’s steadfast support for the realisation” of GMC. Bhutanese officials said the number was chosen because Mr. Modi turned 76 more than a month ago. Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju, who represented India for ‘Project 108’, thanked the King for dedicating Chorten 76 to Mr. Modi. “This remarkable milestone is an enduring symbol of the deep spiritual and civilisational bonds between our two nations,” he said, congratulating Bhutan on the achievement. Each 15 metres tall and 108 metres apart, the Jangchub Chortens, or Buddhist stupas, stand in a single meandering file along the Mau Chhu River, Gelephu’s lifeline. Built with steel and other improvised building materials, they mark a departure from the traditional use of stone and earth. Addressing the people after the completion of Project 108, King Wangchuk said he had been worried that the construction of 108 stupas in a single day might not succeed. “People from every walk of life and every generation came together to make this possible,” he said, underscoring the Bhutanese collective spirit and ability to achieve “anything impossible”. He said the same spirit would help Bhutan overcome natural calamities, economic crises, and other challenges. The King also expressed gratitude to Bhutan’s patrons, sponsors, supporters, and well-wishers. “Prime Minister Modi and the government of India have been enormously supportive of Bhutan and of the vision of Gelephu Mindfulness City,” he said. https://www.thehindu.com/news/internatio.body_zh:
订阅账户还可使用 Premium Stories、Editorials、Opinions 等内容。订阅即可解锁这些内容。发布于 - 2026年11月01日 晚上10:07 IST - GELEPHU（BHUTAN）

Bhutan 国王 Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuk 于星期日（2026年11月1日）将108座佛教佛塔中的一座献给总理 Narendra Modi，以表彰 India 对该国雄心勃勃的 Gelephu Mindfulness City（GMC）项目的支持。这108座佛塔是在一项历时9小时的施工壮举中建成的。约40,000名经过培训的志愿者建成了108座 Jangchub Chorten；这项有望打破纪录的王室倡议为规划中的城市奠定了精神基础。

Gelephu 位于 Bhutan 首都 Thimphu 南偏东约240公里处，与 Assam 的 Chirang 区接壤。Wangchuk 国王设想将该城市打造为由精神力量驱动的全球经济中心。

在仪式场地上，Wangchuk 国王、王室其他成员、高级官员和外国政要面向第79号 Chorten；周围数千人在志愿者于上午3点至中午12点完成任务的期间，吟诵六字藏传佛教真言十亿遍。

约两小时后，活动焦点转向第76号 Chorten。Wangchuk 国王将其献给 Modi 先生，“作为一项长久的象征”，以表达对后者“不渝的承诺”以及“India 对实现 GMC 的坚定支持”的“深切感谢”。来自 Bhutan 的官员表示，选择76这个数字，是因为 Modi 先生在一个月多前年满76岁。

代表 India 参加“Project 108”的议会事务部长 Kiren Rijiju 感谢国王将第76号 Chorten 献给 Modi 先生说。“这一非凡里程碑是两国之间深厚精神纽带和文明纽带的恒久象征，”他说，并祝贺 Bhutan 取得这一成就。

每座 Jangchub Chorten（即佛教佛塔）高15米，彼此相距108米，沿 Gelephu 的生命线 Mau Chhu River 蜿蜒排成一线。这些佛塔以钢材及其他权宜使用的建筑材料建成，与传统使用石材和泥土的做法有所不同。

“Project 108”完成后，Wangchuk 国王向民众讲话时说，他此前担心一天建成108座佛塔可能无法成功。“来自各行各业、各代的人携手合作，使这一切成为可能，”他说，强调了 Bhutan 的集体精神以及实现“任何看似不可能之事”的能力。他说，同样的精神将帮助 Bhutan 克服自然灾害、经济危机和其他挑战。

国王还向 Bhutan 的资助者、赞助者、支持者和祝福者表示感谢。“Modi 总理和 India 政府一直大力支持 Bhutan，也大力支持 Gelephu Mindfulness City 的愿景，”他说。

Unlock these with Subscription Thousands of protesters from across the country, representing political parties, youth organisations, women’s groups and farmers’ bodies, gathered at Minto Road in Delhi on Sunday (November 1, 2026) ahead of the INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan, seeking to strengthen the campaign against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Chalo Dilli protests: Follow LIVE updates from the Opposition rally on November 1, 2026 Ahead of the arrival of Opposition leaders, including Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, protesters raised slogans of “vote chori” and demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the rollback of the SIR exercise. Among those assembling at Minto Road were members of the Indian Youth Congress, Samajwadi Party, Rashtriya Janata Dal, National Students’ Union of India, Krantikari Yuva Sangathan and the All India Students’ Federation, among other groups. The gathering also drew citizens (independent of parties) who said the coming together of various parties and the public had given the protests greater strength after several demonstrations against the SIR in recent weeks. “You can break one stick easily, but if you bundle 10 sticks together, they cannot be broken. Today’s protest symbolises that bundle of sticks,” said Tejender, an IT employee who had arrived with his wife from Gurugram. When asked why he had joined the demonstration on a Sunday afternoon, he said, “We are doing this for a better future for our children. The education system is in a bad state, healthcare facilities are lacking, and there are concerns over the misappropriation of votes. Our country has so many problems that need to be addressed. It is high time we all came together,” he said. Mr. Tejender said the SIR exercise has disproportionately affected people who lacked the resources or awareness to navigate the documentation process. “I am educated and was able to produce all the required documents, but a large section of the population is either uneducated or unaware of the process and is being targeted by the SIR of electoral rolls. Who will fight for them?” he asked. Participants also said that the past protests ensured that fear of demonstrations was gradually receding. “The earlier protests were a struggle by the youth and they have helped remove the fear of the police from people’s minds. I was scared earlier, many political parties were scared too. But after a series of consistent protests, that fear is no longer there,” said Anil S. Raj, an advocate who had attended previous demonstrations against the SIR. Participants said earlier demonstrations had largely taken place in silos, with different groups raising concerns over the SIR separately. The INDIA bloc rally, they said, offered an opportunity to bring these voices together and build a broader movement. “Now, so many people are joining the protests, including leaders from different political parties. This will send a strong message,” J.C. Yadav, another advocate who joined the protests said. With an intravenous cannula on her left arm, Azka, a Delhi-based cafe owner who had spent the past week admitted to Guru Teg Bahadur Hospital with typhoid, also arrived for the protest. Unable to attend earlier protests because of her illness, she said she did not want to miss Sunday’s (November 1, 2026) gathering. “I could not attend the earlier protests because I was unwell. Today, I did not want to miss this one. I am here simply to support the people of our country who are fighting against the government’s wrongdoings,” she said. Ms. Azka said her mother had strictly advised her against attending the rally because of her health. However, she decided to make the journey to Minto Road, joking that she would return to hospital the next day if her condition worsened. “I have never shut my cafe on a Sunday because the footfall is higher on weekends. But today, I wanted to be at the protest. Everyone needs to stand together to show the government that it cannot simply do whatever it wants,” she said. 来自全国各地的数千名抗议者汇聚在明托路，聚集于德里于2026年11月1日星期日举行集会，他们来自不同政党、青年组织、女性团体和农民组织。集会在拉姆利拉广场举行INDIA联盟大规模集会之前，旨在加强反对选民名册特别集中修订（SIR）的竞选活动。

“前往德里”抗议活动：关注2026年11月1日反对党集会的实时报道

在包括人民院反对党领袖拉胡尔·甘地在内的反对党领导人抵达前，抗议者高举写有“偷窃选票”的标语，要求首席选举专员贾内什·库马尔辞职，并要求撤回选民名册SIR行动。

聚集在明托路的人士包括印度青年大会、社会民主党、印度人民达尔党、印度全国学生联盟、革命青年联盟以及全印学生联合会成员及其他团体成员。

此次集会还吸引了许多不属于任何政党的公民参加。他们表示，近几周多次反对SIR的示威活动之后，各党派与公众携手行动，使这次抗议拥有了更强力量。

IT员工特真德尔与妻子从古尔冈赶来参加集会。他说：“一根棍子很容易折断，但如果把10根棍子捆在一起，就无法折断。今天的抗议象征着那捆棍子。”当被问及为何在星期日下午参加示威时，他说：“我们这样做是为了给孩子们一个更美好的未来。教育体系状况糟糕，医疗设施不足，选票被挪用也令人担忧。我们的国家有太多问题需要解决。现在是我们所有人团结起来的的时候了。”

特真德尔先生说，SIR行动对缺乏资源或不了解文件申报流程的人群造成了不成比例的影响。他说：“我受过教育，能够提供所有所需文件，但很大一部分人口要么没有受过教育，要么不了解相关流程，正在成为选民名册SIR行动的目标。谁来为他们发声？”

参与者还表示，过去的抗议活动已使人们对示威的恐惧逐渐消退。曾参加此前反对SIR示威的律师阿尼尔·S·拉杰说：“早先的抗议是青年争取权益的斗争，它们帮助消除了人们对警察的恐惧。我以前很害怕，许多政党也很害怕。但经过一系列持续不断的抗议，这种恐惧已经不复存在。”

参与者表示，此前各次示威大多各自为政，不同团体分别就SIR表达关切。他们说，INDIA联盟的集会提供了把这些声音联合起来、建立更广泛运动的机会。

另一名参加抗议的律师J.C.亚达夫说：“现在有这么多人在参加抗议，包括来自不同政党的领导人。这将传递出有力信息。”

阿兹卡是一名常驻德里的咖啡馆老板。过去一周，她因患伤寒被收治在古尔·泰格·巴哈杜尔医院，左臂上仍留有静脉留置针，但她也赶来参加抗议。由于身体不适，她此前无法参加抗议活动。她表示，不想错过2026年11月1日星期日的集会。

她说：“我之前身体不适，无法参加早先的抗议。今天，我不想错过这一场。我来这里只是为了支持我们国家那些反对政府不当行为的人。”

阿兹卡女士说，母亲曾因她的健康状况严词劝阻她参加集会。不过，她仍决定前往明托路，并开玩笑说如果身体状况恶化，第二天就返回医院。

她说：“我从未在星期日关掉过咖啡馆，因为周末客流量更大。但今天，我想参加抗议。所有人都需要团结起来，向政府表明它不能想做什么就做什么。”

http://www.africanews.com/2026/11/01/in-.body: On the sand of Lomé Beach, Anthony Yao Sodjinê warms up for a match. The sport he's preparing for - sambo - began in the USSR and takes its name from a Russian expression meaning "unarmed self-defense." Now, a new partnership between Togo and Russia is giving the discipline a foothold in West Africa. Anthony came to sambo from judo, and the transition was deliberate. "I decided to take up competitive sambo to test myself, to see how it would turn out in life," he says. In three years, he has already competed in four African tournaments. His personal journey now sits inside a broader partnership between Togo and Russia, with sports as the channel. The Togolese Sambo Federation has been organizing demonstrations in Lomé since June 2024. The Africa Initiative Cup is in its first edition. The groundwork was laid earlier: in April 2023, the Russian and Togolese sports ministers signed a memorandum of cooperation covering school and mass sports, infrastructure, and training. "Our mission here is to develop this type of sport in Togo, as part of cultural and sports exchanges, as well as training exchanges," says Andrey Belogonov, representative of Africa Initiative and organizer of the Africa Initiative Cup. "Today, our federations may be invited by the Russian Federation to participate in sports initiatives and international competitions," says Gneny Tchagbele, representative of Togo's Ministry of Youth and Sports. Despite the progress, sambo remains relatively unknown in Togo compared with sports like football. But the nascent partnership between Lomé and Moscow could earn it the visibility it needs
http://www.africanews.com/2026/11/01/in-.title_zh: 在洛美，苏联时代的运动庆祝多哥与俄罗斯的友谊
http://www.africanews.com/2026/11/01/in-.body_zh: 在洛美海滩的沙地上，Anthony Yao Sodjinê正在为一场比赛热身。他准备参加的项目——桑博——起源于苏联，其名称源自一个意为“无器械自卫”的俄语表达。如今，多哥与俄罗斯之间的一项新合作正在让这项运动在西非扎根。Anthony此前练习柔道，后来有意转向桑博。他说：“我决定开始参加竞技桑博，检验自己，看看人生会因此发生怎样的变化。”三年来，他已经参加了4场非洲赛事。他的个人经历如今成为多哥与俄罗斯更广泛合作的一部分，体育是双方开展合作的渠道。自2024年6月以来，多哥桑博联合会一直在洛美组织表演赛。非洲倡议杯正在举办首届赛事。此前，双方已奠定基础：2023年4月，俄罗斯与多哥体育部长签署了一份合作备忘录，涵盖学校体育和大众体育、基础设施以及培训。非洲倡议代表、非洲倡议杯组织者Andrey Belogonov说：“我们此行的使命是在多哥发展这类项目，作为文化和体育交流以及培训交流的一部分。”多哥青年与体育部代表Gneny Tchagbele说：“如今，我们的各联合会可能会受俄罗斯联邦邀请，参与体育项目和国际赛事。”尽管取得了进展，与足球等项目相比，桑博在多哥仍然相对鲜为人知。不过，洛美与莫斯科之间这项初具规模的合作，或许能为桑博赢得它所需要的知名度

https://www.yna.co.kr/view/akr2026110200.body: (부에노스아이레스=연합뉴스) 김선정 통신원 = 레오 14세 교황이 39년 만에 아르헨티나를 방문한다. 폐암 수술로 순방 취소 가능성까지 제기됐으나 일정이 예정대로 확정되면서 아르헨티나 전역에서 약 700만명이 교황 방문 행사에 참여할 것으로 예상된다. 8일부터 11일까지 이어지는 이번 방문에서 교황이 빈곤과 사회적 불평등, 취약계층 보호 문제에 대해 어떤 메시지를 내놓을지에도 관심이 쏠린다. 2023년 12월 취임 이후 고강도 긴축정책을 추진해온 하비에르 밀레이 아르헨티나 대통령은 교황의 방문을 환영하고 있지만, 연금 수급자와 장애인 지원 문제를 둘러싼 정부와 가톨릭교회의 시각차가 다시 부각될 가능성도 있다. 교황의 아르헨티나 방문은 1987년 요한 바오로 2세 이후 39년 만이다. 아르헨티나 출신인 프란치스코 교황은 2013년 즉위 이후 12년간 재임하면서도 고국을 방문하지 못했다. 이번 방문은 교황의 건강 문제로 취소 우려가 제기되기도 했다. 레오 14세는 지난달 13일 폐선암으로 오른쪽 폐 하엽을 절제하는 수술을 받았다. 그러나 회복 상태를 확인한 의료진이 해외 순방에 의학적 장애가 없다고 판단하면서 일정이 확정됐다. 교황은 오는 6일부터 17일까지 우루과이, 아르헨티나, 페루 등 남미 3개국을 방문한다. 아르헨티나 방문 기간 가장 큰 행사는 11일 부에노스아이레스주 루한 대성당에서 열리는 미사다. 이 행사에만 300만∼400만명이 모일 것으로 예상되며, 수도권과 코르도바주 등 다른 지역의 행사까지 포함하면 전체 방문 기간 약 700만명이 교황을 맞이할 것으로 전망된다. 교황은 9일에는 부에노스아이레스주 클레이폴레에 위치한 장애인 복지시설을 찾는다. 400여명의 장애인이 생활하는 이 시설은 정부의 장애인 지원 예산과 복지 서비스 축소 논란이 이어지는 가운데 주목받는 방문 장소다. 레오 14세는 그동안 빈곤층과 소외계층 보호, 사회적 연대와 공동선의 중요성을 강조해왔다. 이번 방문에서도 화합과 사회정의, 사회적 약자에 대한 관심을 촉구하는 메시지를 낼 것이라는 관측이 나온다. 밀레이 대통령과 가톨릭교회의 관계도 관심사다. 밀레이는 대선 후보 시절 프란치스코 교황을 '악마의 지상 대리인' 등으로 부르며 강하게 비난했다. 그러나 2024년 2월 바티칸에서 프란치스코 교황과 만나 포옹하고 대화를 나누면서 관계 개선에 나섰다. 아르헨티나에서는 연금 수급자와 장애인 등 취약계층의 생활 여건이 악화했다는 비판이 이어지고 있고, 장애인 지원 예산과 복지 서비스 문제를 놓고 가톨릭교회와 복지단체의 우려도 꾸준히 제기돼왔다. 현지 언론은 밀레이 정부가 39년 만의 교황의 아르헨티나 방문을 정권의 외교적 성과로 부각할 수 있다는 점에서 환영하면서도, 교황이 빈곤, 일자리 부족, 사회적 약자와 관련한 현안을 직접 언급할 경우 정부의 긴축경제 정책에 대한 비판에 커질 수 있다는 점에 우려하고 있다고 전했다. 제보는 카카오톡 okjebo <저작권자(c) 연합뉴스, 무단 전재-재배포, AI 학습 및 활용 금지> 2026/11/02 01:24 송고 2026년11월02일 01시24분 송고 (부에노스아이레스=AFP 연합뉴스) 한 시민이 아르헨티나 부에노스아이레스주 라 마탄사에서 고(故) 프란치스코 교황(왼쪽)과 레오 14세 교황(오른쪽)을 묘사한 벽화를 배경으로 걷고 있다. 레오 14세 교황은 오는 8일(현지시간)부터 11일까지 아르헨티나를 방문한다. 2026.11.2 (바티칸=AFP 연합뉴스) 교황 레오 14세가 1일(현지시간) 바티칸 산피에트로 광장을 내려다보는 교황청 창문에 서서 신자들에게 축복을 기원하고 있다. 2026.11.2
https://www.yna.co.kr/view/akr2026110200.title_zh: 39年来首次踏上阿根廷土地……政府对社会正义的呼吁触动敏感神经
https://www.yna.co.kr/view/akr2026110200.body_zh: （布宜诺斯艾利斯=韩联社）记者金善政报道=教宗利奥14世将于39年后访问阿根廷。因接受肺癌手术，其访阿行程一度面临取消可能，但目前已确认按计划进行，预计将有约700万人参加阿根廷境内迎接教宗的各项活动。外界关注在11月8日至11日举行的此次访问中，教宗将就贫困、社会不平等和弱势群体保护等问题传达何种信息。2023年12月就任以来，阿根廷总统哈维尔·米莱一直推行力度较大的紧缩政策，并对教宗访问表示欢迎，但围绕养老金领取者和残疾人支持问题，政府与天主教会之间的分歧可能再度浮现。这是教宗自1987年访问阿根廷、继约翰·保罗二世之后时隔39年再次到访。阿根廷出生的方济各教宗自2013年即位、在位12年期间始终未能回到祖国。此次访问也曾因教皇健康问题而引发取消担忧。利奥14世上月13日接受切除右肺下叶的肺鳞癌手术，但医疗团队确认其恢复情况良好，判断海外访问不存在医学障碍，因此行程最终确定。教宗将于本月6日至17日访问乌拉圭、阿根廷和秘鲁等南美3国。此次访问阿根廷期间规模最大的活动将于11日在布宜诺斯艾利斯省鲁汉大教堂举行，预计仅这场弥撒就会吸引300万至400万人参加；若计入首都圈和科尔多瓦省等其他地区的活动，预计整个访问期间将有约700万人迎接教宗。教宗还将在9日探访位于布宜诺斯艾利斯省克莱波莱的一所残疾人福利设施。这家设施约有400名残疾人居住，在政府削减残疾人支持预算和福利服务的争议持续之际，此次探访格外引人关注。利奥14世一直以来强调保护贫困和边缘群体，并重视社会团结与共同善。此次访问中，预计他将发表敦促社会和解、伸张社会正义以及关注社会弱者的信息。教宗与米莱总统之间的关系同样受到关注。米莱在大选候选人期间曾称方济各教宗为“魔鬼在世上的代理人”等，予以猛烈抨击；但2024年2月在梵蒂冈与方济各教宗会面、拥抱并交谈后，双方关系有所改善。在阿根廷，针对养老金领取者和残疾人等弱势群体生活状况恶化的批评持续不断，天主教会和福利团体也经常就残疾人支持预算及福利服务问题表达担忧。当地媒体对米莱政府表示欢迎，认为其可以借此突出39年来教宗访问阿根廷这一外交成果；但媒体同时担忧，若教宗直接提及贫困、就业不足和社会弱者等现实问题，访问可能演变为对政府紧缩经济政策的批评。图片说明：（布宜诺斯艾利斯=法新社 韩联社）一名市民走过一幅描绘已故方济各教宗（左）和教宗利奥14世（右）的壁画。教宗利奥14世将于当地时间8日至11日访问阿根廷。2026年11月2日。（梵蒂冈=法新社 韩联社）教宗利奥14世于当地时间1日站在梵蒂冈圣彼得广场的教皇宫窗口，为信徒祈祷并送上祝福。2026年11月2日。

https://www.myjoyonline.com/harmful-peer.body: The Vice-Chancellor of the Presbyterian University, Ghana (PUG), Prof. John Ofosu-Anim, has urged newly admitted students to prioritise healthy academic networking over harmful relationships. Prof. Ofosu-Anim warned that wrong relationships and networks remain a major cause of failure among university students, stressing that PUG will not compromise on discipline. Speaking during the matriculation ceremony for the 2025/2026 academic year, he explained that the university environment exposes students to freedom and diverse choices, and that the kind of friends and networks they build on campus will largely determine their success or failure. According to him, many students lose focus and fail not because they lack ability, but because they associate with peers who negatively influence their values, discipline, and academic commitment. Prof. Ofosu-Anim reiterated the university's commitment to producing graduates who are academically excellent, morally upright, and ready to contribute meaningfully to national development. He said the university's motto, "Discipline in Leadership," must reflect in the conduct of all students as the institution trains future leaders for the public health sector and other fields. The Presbyterian University, Ghana, matriculated a total of 720 postgraduate students into various faculties of the university. The ceremony was held in three phases from October 9th to 24th, 2026, at the university's Akuapem and Asante Akyem Agogo campuses. The fresh students have been enrolled to pursue various postgraduate programmes, including MPhil and M.Ed in Educational Studies, MA Guidance and Counselling, MA International Development, MSc Environmental Health and Sanitation, MSc Natural Resources Management, MSc ICT Management, MPhil Nursing, MSc Nursing, and Master of Public Health. Of the total, 385 students were admitted to the Master of Public Health (MPH) programme, a milestone since the programme was introduced. The Vice-Chancellor explained that the MPH programme was introduced to build human capacity in public health following the global shortage of professionals exposed by the COVID-19 pandemic. He urged students to use their large numbers as an opportunity for collaboration, peer support, and knowledge sharing, rather than isolation, noting that academic networking is key to success at the postgraduate level. Prof. Ofosu-Anim further advised them to uphold hard work, integrity, and faith in God, in line with the values of a Presbyterian university. The Dean of the Faculty of Medical Sciences, Nana Osei Akomeah Prince, disclosed that the Master of Public Health programme has trained about 600 students in the last five years. According to him, tracer studies conducted on graduates show that most are currently serving in key areas of the health sector, including the Ministry of Health, local and international non-governmental organisations (NGOs), health directorates, and consultancy services. He explained that the programme is designed mainly for professionals who are already working and need advanced knowledge to enhance their practice. He noted that PUG's MPH programme places a strong emphasis on practical training, equipping students with both theoretical and practical competencies that are immediately applicable at their workplaces. He said the location of the Asante Akyem Agogo Campus, which offers the MPH programme, in a semi-rural area provides a unique advantage for students to engage directly with communities, diagnose community health problems, and design interventions to address them. "The university and the campus are based in a semi-rural area, and it gives us the opportunity to enter into the various communities, assess them, and try to bring interventions that will help the communities. When you come here, you have all the necessary tools in terms of learning, and you carry along a lot of experience because of what we do here," he stated. He expressed confidence that the continuous growth in enrolment for the MPH programme reflects the quality and relevance of the training being offered by the university
https://www.myjoyonline.com/harmful-peer.title_zh: 加纳 Presbyterian University 副校长警告新生：大学中有害的同伴关系会导致学业失败
https://www.myjoyonline.com/harmful-peer.body_zh: 加纳长老会大学（PUG）校长约翰·奥福苏-阿尼姆教授敦促新录取的学生优先建立有助于学业的健康人脉，而不是有害的人际关系。奥福苏-阿尼姆教授警告说，不当的人际关系和社交圈仍是大学生学业失败的主要原因之一，并强调PUG在纪律问题上绝不妥协。在2025/2026学年 matriculation 典礼上，他指出，大学环境让学生享有自由并面对多种选择，而他们在校园建立何种朋友关系和人脉，将在很大程度上决定其成功或失败。据他介绍，许多学生失去专注并遭遇失败，并非因为能力不足，而是因为他们与会对自身价值观、纪律和学业投入产生负面影响的同辈交往。奥福苏-阿尼姆教授重申，该大学致力于培养学业优秀、道德端正并能为国家发展作出切实贡献的毕业生。他说，大学的校训“领导力体现在纪律中”必须体现在所有学生的行为中，因为该校正在为公共卫生领域及其他领域培养未来的领导者。加纳长老会大学共有720名研究生被录取进入大学旗下各学院注册就读。典礼于2026年10月9日至24日分三个阶段举行，地点分别为大学位于阿夸佩姆和阿桑特阿克奥戈的校区。新生已注册修读多个研究生课程，包括教育研究MPhil和M.Ed、指导与咨询MA、国际发展MA、环境卫生与环境卫生管理MSc、自然资源管理MSc、ICT管理MSc、护理学MPhil、护理学MSc以及公共卫生硕士课程。在录取总数中，有385名学生被公共卫生硕士（MPH）课程录取，这是该课程设立以来的重要里程碑。校长 explained，COVID-19疫情暴露出全球专业人员短缺问题后，设立MPH课程旨在提升公共卫生领域的人力能力。他敦促学生利用人数众多这一优势开展合作、同伴支持和知识共享，而不是各自孤立，并指出，学术人脉是研究生阶段取得成功的关键。奥福苏-阿尼姆教授还建议他们秉持勤奋、诚信和对上帝的信仰，这与加纳长老会大学的价值观一致。医学科学学院院长纳纳·奥塞·阿科梅阿王子披露，公共卫生硕士课程在过去五年间培养了约600名学生。据他介绍，针对毕业生开展的追踪研究显示，目前大多数人正在卫生部门的关键岗位任职，包括卫生部、国内外非政府组织（NGO）、卫生主管机构以及咨询服务机构。他 explained，该课程主要面向已经在岗工作、需要通过进阶知识提升专业实践能力的人员。他指出，PUG的MPH课程高度重视实践培训，使学生同时掌握理论能力和实践能力，并能立即应用于工作场所。他说，提供MPH课程的阿桑特阿克奥戈校区位于半农村地区，这一独特优势让学生能够直接接触社区、诊断社区健康问题，并设计干预措施加以解决。他表示：“大学和校区位于半农村地区，这让我们有机会走进各个社区、评估社区情况，并尝试推出能够帮助社区的干预措施。来到这里后，你们将拥有学习所需的全部工具，而且会从我们这里所做的工作中积累大量经验。”他相信，MPH课程入学人数的持续增长反映了该大学所提供培训的质量和相关性

https://www.myjoyonline.com/constitution.title: Constitutional reforms need a roadmap to survive changes in government
https://www.myjoyonline.com/constitution.summary: Director of Policy Engagement and Partnerships at the Ghana Center for Democratic Development (CDD-Ghana), Dr Kojo Pumpuni Asante, has called for a statutory roadmap to guide the implementation of Ghana’s proposed constitutional reforms beyond changes in government.
https://www.myjoyonline.com/constitution.summary_zh: 加纳民主发展中心（CDD-Ghana）政策参与与合作主任 Kojo Pumpuni Asante 博士呼吁制定法定路线图，以指导加纳拟议宪法改革的实施，确保改革不仅限于政府换届。
https://www.myjoyonline.com/constitution.body: Director of Policy Engagement and Partnerships at the Ghana Center for Democratic Development (CDD-Ghana), Dr Kojo Pumpuni Asante, has called for a statutory roadmap to guide the implementation of Ghana’s proposed constitutional reforms beyond changes in government. He said the legitimacy and long-term success of the reform process would depend not only on legal and political decisions but also on ensuring that citizens feel genuinely involved in shaping the outcome. Speaking on JoyNews’ The Law on Sunday, November 1, during a discussion on the work of the Constitutional Review Committee (CRC), bridging political divides and the way forward, Dr Asante stressed the importance of what he described as “process guarantees”. “I think the process guarantees are very important,” he said. Referencing comments by former Chief Justice Sophia Akuffo, Dr Asante said constitutional reform should not be treated solely as an exercise for legal scholars and politicians. “Justice Sophia Akuffo, I think, recently said something similar about this as not just a process about law, legal scholars and politics, but it's about the legitimacy of the process,” he noted. According to him, whatever decisions emerge from the reform process must be accepted and believed in by Ghanaians. “Whatever we come to a conclusion on, it has to be believed and accepted by the people,” he said. He warned that reforms could fail to produce the desired results if citizens do not feel they have been adequately involved in the process. “So if the people don't feel part of it, don't feel that they have contributed to it, you pass legislation and it will not deliver the desired result,” he stated. Dr Asante said one of the most important safeguards required for the reform process is what he described as a Roadmap and Implementation Act. He explained that the proposed legislation should track the various actions and reforms arising from the constitutional review process and provide a statutory framework for their implementation. “We believe that one of the first things we have to do is to pass a Roadmap and Implementation Act that basically tracks all of the different actions and reforms that we want to undertake, but they'll do it by statute,” he said. According to Dr Asante, such a framework would help protect the reform process and ensure its continuity beyond the tenure of the current government. “So that it gives us the security that if we go past 2028 into another regime, into a different transition, that we are able to still carry out the reforms,” he explained. He noted that the reforms would take place at different levels, including constitutional amendments, statutory changes and subsequent legislation, making it unrealistic to expect all of them to be completed within a short period. “Because there are many levels of reform. Some are constitutional, some are statutory, some are subsequent legislation,” he said. Dr Asante also cautioned against rushing the entire reform agenda and putting unnecessary pressure on the process. “There is no way, with our election also coming, that you'll be able to execute all of this properly. So we shouldn't put ourselves in a corner with all that pressure and make sure that we put a framework in place that allows us to continue working on some of these reforms,” he added
https://www.myjoyonline.com/constitution.title_zh: 宪法改革需要一份路线图，才能经受政府更迭
https://www.myjoyonline.com/constitution.body_zh: Ghana Center for Democratic Development（CDD-Ghana）政策参与与合作事务主任 Kojo Pumpuni Asante 博士呼吁制定法定路线图，以指导加纳拟议宪法改革的实施，确保改革超越政府更迭并持续推进。他说，改革程序的合法性与长期成功，不仅取决于法律和政治决定，也取决于确保公民真正参与塑造改革结果。11月1日，在 JoyNews 的《The Law on Sunday》节目中讨论 Constitutional Review Committee（CRC）的工作、弥合政治分歧和未来方向时，Asante 博士强调了他所称的“程序保障”的重要性。他说：“我认为，程序保障非常重要。”提及前首席法官 Sophia Akuffo 的看法时，Asante 博士表示，宪法改革不应仅仅被当作法律学者和政治人士的工作。他指出：“我想，Sophia Akuffo 大法官最近就此发表过类似看法，认为这不只是涉及法律、法律学者和政治的程序，而是关乎程序的合法性。”据他所说，改革程序最终形成的任何决定，都必须让加纳人相信并接受。他说：“无论我们最终得出什么结论，都必须让人民相信并接受。”他警告，如果公民没有感到自己充分参与了改革程序，改革可能无法产生预期结果。他表示：“如果人民感觉不到自己是其中一分子，感觉不到自己曾为改革作出贡献，那么即使通过了法律，也不会产生预期结果。”Asante 博士说，改革程序所需的最重要保障之一，就是他所说的《Roadmap and Implementation Act》。他解释说，拟议立法应跟踪宪法审查程序产生的各项行动和改革，并为其实施提供法定框架。他说：“我们认为，首先必须做的一件事，就是通过一部《Roadmap and Implementation Act》，基本上将我们希望开展的所有不同行动和改革纳入跟踪，并通过成文法予以落实。”据 Asante 博士 Such a framework would help protect the reform process and ensure its continuity beyond the tenure of the current government. “这样就能为我们提供保障：即使越过2028年，进入另一个政权、经历不同的交接，我们仍然能够继续推行改革。”他指出，改革将在不同层面进行，包括宪法修正、成文法修改和后续立法，因此指望在短期内完成所有改革并不现实。他说：“因为改革涉及多个层面，有些属于宪法层面，有些属于成文法层面，有些则需要后续立法。”Asante 博士还警告，不要急于推进整个改革议程，也不要给改革程序施加不必要的压力。他补充说：“随着选举临近，我们根本不可能把所有这些工作妥善完成。因此，我们不应在所有这些压力下把自己逼入死角，而应确保建立一套框架，让我们能够继续推进其中一些改革。”

Mr. Gandhi was speaking at the INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan, which saw participation from across the country, with crowds spilling beyond the ground’s boundaries and marching with drums and waving flags. Many trailed Mr. Gandhi and other leaders as they drove to the venue in an open-top vehicle. Congress general secretary (organisation) K.C. Venugopal, without quantifying the number of participants, in a post on X, said, “The scale of today’s uprising has never before been seen in Delhi.” Responding to Home Minister Amit Shah’s recent remarks that Prime Minister Narendra Modi is “not going anywhere”, Mr. Gandhi said that neither the Prime Minister nor the Home Minister would be allowed to “go anywhere” even if they wanted to. “Amit Shah said Narendra Modi is not going anywhere... even if he wants to go, we will not let him. Narendra Modi ji and Amit Shah ji , understand this: after Gyanesh Kumar, we will stand against you. And don’t forget that for the vote chori (vote theft) you have done, there will be legal action against you and Narendra Modi,” he said to a roaring crowd. Other leaders also expressed similar views. Former Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Akhilesh Yadav described the crowd at Ramlila Maidan as the “Haldighati of democracy”, which he said indicated that change is in the offing. “Those who came to power through U.P. will be ousted from there. And ‘U.P. wallahs (people)’, who are good at welcoming, are better at giving send-offs,” he said. Former West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee described the SIR as “special intensive relief” for the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and said Bengal has been a victim of it. Mr. Gandhi’s 18-minute-long speech combined aggressive posturing towards the government with a preview of what he described as a post-Modi vision of India that would replace the politics of hatred with the politics of harmony. He said “ vote chori ” has been happening for years, claiming several Assembly elections, including those in Madhya Pradesh, Haryana, Chhattisgarh, and Maharashtra, were stolen through the “addition” and “deletion” of voters. The 2024 mandate for the Modi government, he alleged, was “illegal”. After the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, Mr. Gandhi said 130 million voters were removed, which amounted to 15% of the total electorate, or one in every seven voters. He pointed out that the difference in vote share between the BJP-led coalition and the INDIA bloc in the 2024 elections was three percentage points. “This is not an ordinary theft; it is not someone stealing something small from a shop... This is a theft of every citizen’s voice and expression. In legal parlance, this is called a ‘rarest of rare’ case; this is called treason,” Mr. Gandhi said, alleging that Mr. Modi and Mr. Shah would not have become Prime Minister and Home Minister without Gyanesh Kumar. Using the metaphor of “ Shiv ji ki baraat ”, where all kinds of creatures are allowed to participate, Mr. Gandhi said India has to be inclusive, where a farmer enjoys the fruits of his labour and where a student studying for 18 hours gets employment. Naming industrialist Gautam Adani, Mr. Gandhi said the Opposition will not allow all resources to be owned by a single person. “The first step to bring the nation back on track is to remove Gyanesh Kumar,” he said. While focusing his attack on Mr. Modi, Mr. Shah, and Mr. Kumar, Mr. Gandhi also drew a distinction between “us and them”, saying that despite everything, “we do not hate them”. “Narendra Modi ji , Amit Shah ji , Gyanesh Kumar ji , you have attacked the country’s soul, our constitution, our democracy; we are not willing to accept this,” he said, adding that none of the three is his enemy. He underlined that the voice of every individual Indian was more important to him than religion. “We have to erase hatred. Narendra Modi, Amit Shah, and the RSS have spread hatred. It is hurting the nation and our nation’s soul,” he said, adding that the country is screaming for love, stressing the need for a politics of harmony instead of hatred. The rally was attended by senior Opposition leaders, including Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, Congress Parliamentary Party Chairperson Sonia Gandhi, National Conference patriarch Farooq Abdullah, PDP leader Mehbooba Mufti, CPI(M) general secretary M.A. Baby, CPI general secretary D. https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/p.body_zh:

人民院反对党领袖拉胡尔·甘地指控首席选举专员贾内什·库马尔窃取公民的声音，称其犯下“叛国罪”，并表示库马尔将被免职、锒铛入狱。甘地是在拉姆利拉广场举行的INDIA联盟集会上发表上述言论的。活动吸引了全国各地民众参加，人群挤出了场地边界，敲着鼓、挥舞着旗帜前往集会。许多人与甘地及其他领导人乘坐敞篷车前往会场。

国大党组织事务总书记K.C.维努戈帕尔没有说明参加人数，但在X上发帖称：“今天这场起义的规模，在德里前所未有。”

针对内政部长阿米特·沙阿近期有关总理纳伦德拉·莫迪“哪儿也不会去”的言论，甘地表示，即使总理和内政部长想去，他们也不会被允许“去任何地方”。

他对欢呼的人群说：“阿米特·沙阿说纳伦德拉·莫迪哪儿也不会去……就算他想去，我们也不会让他去。纳伦德拉·莫迪和阿米特·沙阿，请听清楚：继贾内什·库马尔之后，我们也会与你们对抗。别忘了，你们窃取选票的行为将面临法律行动，纳伦德拉·莫迪也一样。”

其他领导人也表达了类似看法。北方邦前首席部长阿克ilesh·亚达夫把拉姆利拉广场的人群称为“民主的哈尔迪加蒂”，并表示，这预示着变革即将到来。他说：“那些借北方邦上台的人将被赶下台。而那些善于欢迎他人的‘北方邦人’，更擅长送人离开。”

西孟加拉邦前首席部长马马塔·班纳杰称，特别 intensive relief是人民党的“特别紧急救济”，并称孟加拉国一直是其受害者。

甘地发表了18分钟的讲话，将对政府的强硬姿态与他所称的“后莫迪印度愿景”结合起来，称这一愿景将以和谐政治取代仇恨政治。他说，多年来一直存在“窃取选票”的行为，并声称包括中央邦、哈里亚纳邦、恰蒂斯加尔邦和马哈拉施特拉邦在内的多次议会选举，都是通过“增加”和“删除”选民而遭到窃取的。他指控，2024年授予莫迪政府的授权“非法”。

甘地表示，2024年人民院选举后有1.3亿选民被剔除，占全部选民的15%，也就是每7名选民中就有1人被剔除。他指出，2024年选举中，人民党领导的联盟与INDIA联盟之间的得票率相差3个百分点。

他说：“这不是普通的盗窃，不是有人从商店里偷走小东西……这是对每位公民声音和表达的盗窃。用法律术语来说，这叫作‘极其罕见’案件；这就是叛国。”甘地指控，如果没有贾内什·库马尔，莫迪和沙阿就不会成为总理和内政部长。

甘地借用“Shiv ji ki baraat”的比喻——各种生物都可以参与其中——表示印度必须具有包容性，让农民享受劳动成果，也让学习18个小时的学生获得就业。

甘地点名工业家高塔姆·阿达尼，称反对派不会允许所有资源都被一个人拥有。他说：“让国家重回正轨的第一步，就是撤换贾内什·库马尔。”

甘地虽然把攻击重点放在莫迪、沙阿和库马尔身上，但也区分了“我们与他们”，称尽管发生了这一切，“我们并不仇恨他们”。

他说：“纳伦德拉·莫迪、阿米特·沙阿、贾内什·库马尔，你们伤害了国家的灵魂、我们的宪法和我们的民主；我们不愿接受这一点。”他补充说，这三人中没有一个是他的敌人。他强调，对每一名印度人的声音而言，宗教都不及它重要。

他说：“我们必须消除仇恨。纳伦德拉·莫迪、阿米特·沙阿和RSS散播了仇恨。这正在伤害国家和我们国家的灵魂。”他补充称，国家正在呼喊爱，并强调需要以和谐政治取代仇恨政治。

出席集会的反对派高层领导人包括国大党主席马利卡琼·卡尔格、国大党议会党主席索尼娅·甘地、国民会议党元老法鲁克·阿卜杜拉、PDP领导人梅赫布巴·穆夫提、CPI(M)总书记M.A.贝比、CPI总书记D.拉贾、CPI(ML)总书记迪潘卡尔·巴塔查里亚、Shiv Sena (UBT)的桑杰·拉乌特、NCP (SP)的苏普里娅·苏莱等。

https://dailytrust.com/sultan-confers-tr.body: The Sultan of Sokoto, Alhaji Muhammadu Sa’ad Abubakar III, has conferred traditional titles on two of his sons, a renowned philanthropist, an Islamic scholar and other prominent personalities. The two sons, Abubakar Sadiq Abubakar and Shehu Usman Abubakar, were turbaned as Sarkin Dawaki Tsakar Gida and Fagachin Sokoto, respectively, at a colourful ceremony held in Sokoto on Sunday. Also turbaned were renowned philanthropist and Islamic scholar, Alhaji Murtala Abdulkadir Dan’iya, as Dallatun Sokoto, and Prof. Mansur Ibrahim as Danmasanin Sokoto. Others included Alhaji Abubakar Hussain as Sarkin Bai; Alhaji Aminu Isa-Buhari as Danmalikin Sokoto; Prof. Ishaq Oloyede as Kuliyan Sokoto; Dr Peter Igoh as Kakakin Daular Usmaniyya and Hon Almustapha Rabah as Bauran Sokoto. Others were Dr Balarabe Kakale as Wakilin Makarantar Daular Usmaniyya; Alhaji Bello Abbas; Alhaji Gandi Umar as Sarkin Galmar Sarkin Musulmi; and Alhaji Abdulqadir Bello-Jeli as Sarkin Fulotin Sokoto. Speaking at the ceremony, the Sultan said the traditional titles were conferred on the recipients based on merit, their contributions to society and the recognition of their individual achievements. The monarch urged the newly turbaned title holders to regard their appointments as a call to greater service, commitment and responsibility, rather than merely as symbols of honour. He also encouraged them to use their positions to promote peace, unity, religious tolerance and the development of the Sokoto Caliphate and the country at large. Speaking to journalists after his turbaning, Dan’iya expressed appreciation to the Sultan for finding him worthy of the traditional title of Dallatun Sokoto. He described the honour as a great privilege and recognition, pledging to continue contributing to the development of society, particularly in the areas of philanthropy, religious activities and support for the less privileged. The ceremony attracted prominent personalities from within and outside the country, including the Speaker of the House of Representatives, Rt. Hon. Tajudeen Abbas, among other dignitaries. https://www.myjoyonline.com/climate-chan.summary_zh: 夸梅·恩克鲁马科技大学（KNUST）气候研究员伊诺克·贝萨博士，对加纳气候变化传播中存在的缺口表示担忧，称许多人只有在亲身经历其影响后才会意识到这场危机。据他所说，气候传播在很大程度上未能以让广泛民众产生共鸣且易于理解的方式触达他们。
https://www.myjoyonline.com/climate-chan.body: A climate researcher at the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST), Dr Enoch Bessah, has raised concerns about gaps in climate change communication in Ghana, saying that many people only become aware of the crisis after experiencing its effects directly. According to him, climate communication has largely failed to reach the wider population in ways that make the issue relatable and easy to understand. Dr Bessah, who leads Climate Change and Ecosystem Services Monitoring at the DIPPER Lab, KNUST, made the remarks during the first panel discussion at the Climate x Culture Summit. The Climate x Culture Summit was held under the theme “ Designing Sustainable Creative Experiences for Africa, ” and brought together voices to explore the intersection of climate action, culture and creativity. Responding to concerns about whether climate change is being communicated effectively to the Ghanaian public, Dr Bessah answered in the negative. “I will say no. Since the majority are still in the dark and they only get to know it when they are hit with the impact, then we are not doing well,” he said. He attributed the challenge partly to a disconnect between scientists and the broader public, noting that important scientific research often fails to reach as many people as messages communicated through popular culture and creative platforms. “Unfortunately, it is because of this disparity between we the scientists and those that are actually heard,” he explained. Dr Bessah said a climate change song by a popular musician such as Okyeame Kwame could potentially reach far more people within a year than a scientific article published in an academic journal. “Assuming that Okyeame Kwame has a music which is on climate change, just in a year, the number of people who know about it will be more than my article that has been in the journal for so many years that you don't even know that it is there,” he said. He stressed that climate change awareness in Ghana appears to be highest among people whose livelihoods are directly affected by changing weather patterns and environmental conditions. “For instance, the farmer, because he knows that a little change in what will happen in the season will affect him or her, is more conscious of it,” he noted. He added that construction workers are also likely to be conscious of changing weather conditions because unexpected changes can directly affect their work. However, Dr Bessah expressed concern that many people whose daily activities contribute to environmental problems may not fully understand the consequences of their actions. He cited indiscriminate waste disposal as an example, explaining that people may not realise that dumping waste on the streets can worsen flooding and increase the impact of even relatively short periods of rainfall. “The rest that are actually contributing to the things that are affecting the climate, they don't know that leaving waste on the street would actually increase the impact of little rains that lasted for one hour,” he said. Dr Bessah concluded that Ghana must broaden the channels through which climate change is communicated, particularly by embracing culture, creativity and other forms of communication that can reach ordinary citizens. “We are not doing well because we have limited the media of this climate change communication,” he stated
https://www.myjoyonline.com/climate-chan.title_zh: 气候变化传播未能触达许多加纳人，与创意工作者合作至关重要
https://www.myjoyonline.com/climate-chan.body_zh: 夸梅·恩克鲁玛科技大学（KNUST）气候研究员Enoch Bessah博士对加纳气候变化传播中存在的缺口表示担忧，称许多人只有在直接经历危机影响后才会意识到其存在。他认为，气候传播在很大程度上未能以让公众产生共鸣且易于理解的方式触达更广泛的人群。领导KNUST旗下DIPPER实验室气候变化与生态系统服务监测工作的Bessah博士，是在“气候×文化”峰会首次小组讨论期间发表上述言论的。“气候×文化”峰会以“为非洲设计可持续的创意体验”为主题，汇聚多方声音，探索气候行动、文化与创造力之间的交叉领域。针对气候变化是否得到有效传播给加纳公众的疑问，Bessah博士给出了否定的回答。他说：“我会说没有。由于大多数人仍处于黑暗中，只有在受到冲击、亲身经历其影响时才会知道这件事，因此我们的工作做得不够好。”他将这一挑战部分归因于科学家与更广泛公众之间的脱节，并指出，重要的科学研究往往不如通过流行文化和创意平台传播的信息那样广为人知。他解释道：“遗憾的是，这源于我们这些科学家与真正被听到的人之间的这种落差。”Bessah博士表示，Okyeame Kwame等知名音乐人创作的一首气候变化歌曲，在一年内触达的人数可能远多于一篇刊登在学术期刊上的科学文章。他说：“假设Okyeame Kwame有一首关于气候变化的歌曲，那么仅仅一年时间，知道它的人就会比我的文章更多。我的文章在期刊上刊登了这么多年，你们甚至不知道它就在那里。”他强调，加纳气候变化意识最强的人群，似乎是那些生计直接受到天气模式和环境条件变化影响的人。他指出：“例如农民，因为他们知道当季情况稍有变化就会影响自己，所以对这个问题有更深的认识。”他补充说，建筑工人也可能更加留意不断变化的天气状况，因为意外变化会直接影响他们的工作。然而，Bessah博士担忧，许多日常活动会加剧环境问题的人，可能并未充分理解自身行为带来的后果。他以乱扔垃圾为例解释说，人们可能没有意识到，在街道上倾倒垃圾会加剧洪涝，并放大即便持续时间相对较短的降雨所造成的影响。他说：“其他真正正在促成那些影响气候之问题的人，并不知道把垃圾丢在街上实际上会加重持续一小时的小雨带来的影响。”Bessah博士总结称，加纳必须拓宽气候变化的传播渠道，尤其是借助文化、创造力以及其他能够触达普通公民的传播形式。他表示：“我们做得不够好，因为我们限制了气候变化传播的媒体渠道。”

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/01/t.body: The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council (APC-PCC) has said that President Bola Tinubu has not deviated from the 2023 campaign pledge to fix electricity. It added that the administration’s quest to fix the electricity market and power sector is ongoing work. Alake recalled that at a meeting with members of the Organised Private Sector (OPS) in Lagos ahead of the 2023 elections, then candidate Tinubu promised to tackle systemic problems in the power sector and end estimated billing. His exact words, according to Alake: “Whichever way, by all means necessary, you will have electricity, and you will not pay for estimated bills anymore. A promise made will be a promise kept. If I don’t keep the promise and I come for a second term, don’t vote for me, unless I give you adequate reasons why I couldn’t deliver. The spokesperson listed measures taken by the administration to fix the sector including the signing of the Electricity Act, 2023 on June 9, within two weeks in office, liberalising the sector and allowing states to participate in generation, distribution and transmission. Lagos, Enugu, Abia, Ekiti, Oyo, Kaduna and Niger have set up their own regulatory agencies. He recalled taking on over N6 trillion legacy debt accumulated from 2015 to 2025 and creating a N4 trillion bond programme to settle verified debts to 21 Gencos and Discos. Alake noted that the first and second tranches have raised over N1.2 trillion. He added: “Launching the Presidential Metering Initiative to close the over 7 million metering gap, with over 1.5 million customers metered in the last three years. Alake also mentioned the Rural Electrification Agency connecting universities, hospitals and rural communities to solar power, plans to modernise the Osogbo Grid Control Centre built over 60 years ago and build an East-West super grid. Alake noted: “Fixing the electricity market and power sector is ongoing work. President Tinubu has not deviated an inch from his commitment. https://www.premiumtimesng.com/features-.summary: Convocation Lecture delivered at Augustine University, Epe, By Bishop Matthew Hassan KUKAH, CON, Bishop, Catholic Diocese of Sokoto on October 29, 2026.
