https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/more.summary_zh: 卡塔萨州政府将扬卡拉地区法斯卡里地方政府辖区发生的暴力事件归因于对一场穆卢德游行活动的争议，并否认有报道将该事件与州长迪科·拉达的竞选集会联系起来。他说，这起事件与法斯卡里举行的蒂努布—迪科竞选集会毫无关系。州长参观了该地区领主的宫殿，并视察了地方政府秘书处和议事厅的翻修工程，随后出席了竞选集会。
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/more.body: The Katsina State Government has attributed violence in Yankara, Faskari Local Government Area, to a disagreement over a Maulud procession, denying reports linking the incident to Governor Dikko Radda’s campaign rally. Two vehicles were reportedly burnt and several people injured during the disturbance. In a statement on Saturday, the governor’s Chief Press Secretary, Ibrahim Kaula Mohammed, said participants in the religious procession disagreed with security personnel over designated routes, causing confusion along a public street. He said the incident had no connection with the Tinubu-Dikko campaign rally in Faskari. LEADERSHIP newspaper reported that suspected hoodlums burnt two vehicles, including one belonging to the Musa Adamu Network (MAN), a political association. Several people were reportedly injured, while shops were damaged. Nura Yandaki, chairman of the association’s caucus, told the newspaper that he was travelling with 11 other members to the governor’s rally when the disturbance occurred. He said trouble began around a Maulud procession before suspected hoodlums attacked passing vehicles. Mr Yandaki said members of his delegation escaped unharmed, but their vehicle was destroyed. An unnamed local government official also told LEADERSHIP that two vehicles were burnt and several people injured while residents and political supporters awaited the governor’s arrival. The government’s statement did not address the reported attacks on vehicles carrying people travelling to the rally. Mr Mohammed said Governor Radda passed safely through Yankara on his way to Faskari. The governor visited the district head’s palace and inspected renovation works at the local government secretariat and council chambers before attending the campaign rally. The government called on security agencies to investigate the violence and establish what happened. It also urged media organisations and social media users to verify information before publication and appealed to residents to remain calm and avoid spreading unverified reports
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/more.title_zh: 卡蒂纳州政府否认暴力事件与拉达斯竞选集会有关
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/more.body_zh: 卡塔萨州政府将扬卡拉地区法斯卡里地方政府辖区发生的暴力事件归因于双方对庆祝先知穆罕默德诞辰活动游行路线存在分歧，并否认有报道将该事件与州长迪科·拉达的竞选集会联系起来。据报道，骚乱期间有2辆汽车被烧毁，另有数人受伤。州长首席新闻秘书易卜拉欣·考拉·穆罕默德星期六发表声明称，宗教游行参与者与安全人员就指定路线发生争执，导致一条公共街道陷入混乱。他说，这起事件与提努布和迪科在法斯卡里举行的竞选集会毫无关系。《LEADERSHIP》报报道称，疑似流氓烧毁2辆汽车，其中包括政治组织穆萨·阿达穆网络（MUSА ADAMU NETWORK，简称MAN）的一辆车。据报道，数人受伤，多家商店遭到破坏。该组织议员团主席努拉·扬达基告诉该报，骚乱发生时，他正与另外11名成员前往州长的集会。他说，麻烦始于庆祝先知穆罕默德诞辰活动的游行，随后疑似流氓袭击了途经车辆。扬达基先生说，他所在代表团的成员均安然无恙，但其车辆被毁。一名未具名的地方政府官员也告诉《LEADERSHIP》，2辆汽车被烧毁，数人受伤，当时居民和政治支持者正在等待州长抵达。州政府的声明没有回应有关乘坐车辆前往集会的人群遭袭的报道。穆罕默德先生说，拉达州长前往法斯卡里的途中安全经过扬卡拉。州长视察了该地区酋长的宫殿，并查看了地方政府秘书处和议事厅的翻修工程，随后出席竞选集会。州政府呼吁安全机构调查暴力事件并查明真相，还敦促媒体机构和社交媒体用户在发布信息前加以核实，并呼吁居民保持冷静，避免传播未经证实的消息。

https://leadership.ng/sokoto-2027-adc-da.title: Sokoto 2027: ADC Dares Govt Over Campaign Flag-off, Alleges Intimidation
https://leadership.ng/sokoto-2027-adc-da.summary: The party alleged a sustained pattern of attacks on its members, including gunshots at the airport, assault on women supporters and vandalisation of its campaign office. Goronyo said the ADC had formally notified the state government of its decision to flag off its presidential campaign in Sokoto, initially slated for October 31, but the government replied expressing disagreement.
https://leadership.ng/sokoto-2027-adc-da.summary_zh: 该党指控其成员持续遭到袭击，包括机场枪击、针对女性支持者的殴打以及竞选办公室遭破坏。戈罗尼奥表示，ADC已正式通知索科托州政府，决定为在索科托启动总统竞选举行旗式启动仪式，原定于10月31日举行，但政府回复表示不同意。
https://leadership.ng/sokoto-2027-adc-da.body: The party alleged a sustained pattern of attacks on its members, including gunshots at the airport, assault on women supporters and vandalisation of its campaign office. Addressing a press conference at the party headquarters in Sokoto on Sunday, the state chairman, Alhaji Bello Muhammad Goronyo, said the party would remain peaceful and law-abiding but would not surrender its constitutional right to organise political activities. He called on the Nigeria Police Force, the Department of State Services (DSS) and the state government to investigate the attacks, including the assault on its governorship candidate on October 30. “We demand protection for our candidate and supporters, accountability for those responsible, and an end to any use of state-backed security outfits to restrict lawful political activity,” he said. Goronyo said the ADC had formally notified the state government of its decision to flag off its presidential campaign in Sokoto, initially slated for October 31, but the government replied expressing disagreement. “The government replied by stating its disagreement with the flag-off. That reply raises serious concern about the government’s commitment to political pluralism, freedom of association and the right of opposition parties to hold lawful political activities,” he said. He alleged that the attacks were not isolated but a sustained pattern, which he linked to the release from prison of two men associated with political thuggery, reportedly by the state government. The party identified one Aliyu K.C. and his associates as being connected to the attacks. “On Wednesday, October 28, 2026, our women were attacked during a peaceful solidarity march. Participants were injured, their mobile phones were snatched, their clothing was torn, and their vehicles and other property were vandalised,” he said. He said on the same day, the ADC state campaign office was attacked, with windows and doors smashed, property looted and three motorcycles destroyed, while billboards, posters and other campaign materials were destroyed across the state. Goronyo further alleged that hotels booked for the flag-off cancelled reservations under pressure from the state government, while government-owned hotels claimed they were fully booked. “Government-owned hotels reportedly stopped accepting guests on the claim that their rooms were fully booked. We have received reports that hotel operators were threatened with consequences, including the demolition of their properties, if they refused to comply. “We are seeking written confirmation of these reports. If established, they would represent a serious abuse of public authority,” he said. “Who authorised their release, under what legal process, and what safeguards were put in place? Release from prison must never be treated as a licence to intimidate citizens, and political connections must not place anyone beyond accountability,” he asked. Goronyo said the party’s governorship candidate, Manir Muhammad Dan’iya (Walin Sokoto), was attacked at the Sultan Abubakar III International Airport, Sokoto, on Friday, by personnel of the Sokoto Marshals and Sokoto Community Guards. He said his vehicles were smashed and gunshots were fired, while two DSS personnel attached to the candidate were reportedly detained. “The authorities must establish who authorised the operation, what instructions were issued, who discharged firearms and under what authority, and why DSS officers assigned to a political candidate were detained by state security personnel. “Responsibility must not stop at the personnel at the scene: anyone who authorised, directed, sponsored or facilitated unlawful conduct must also be investigated,” he said. He said the party had also received reports that personnel of the two state-owned security outfits had been instructed to prevent ADC supporters from entering Sokoto ahead of the flag-off. “We consider this allegation extremely serious. If confirmed, the instruction would violate the constitutional rights of citizens to freedom of movement, peaceful assembly and political association. “No governor, political party or security commander has the authority to restrict citizens from entering a state because of their political affiliation,” he said. He said residents were entitled to question the state’s security priorities when communities still face banditry and kidnapping. “The ADC is a peaceful political party committed to democratic principles, political tolerance, constitutional freedoms and the rule of law. Our commitment to peace must never be mistaken for weakness or surrender of our constitutional rights. “We will not be intimidated, silenced or forced out of the democratic space through violence, threats or politically motivated harassment,” he declared. He called for a thorough investigation into the gunshots, destruction of vehicles, detention of DSS personnel, alleged involvement of Aliyu K.C. and his associates, threat to hotel operators and denial of venue, as well as protection for ADC candidates, leaders and supporters. He also urged all state-owned security outfits to remain politically neutral and not be deployed for partisan activities. We’ve got the edge. https://leadership.ng/sokoto-2027-adc-da.title_zh: 索科托2027：人民民主大会党就竞选活动升旗挑战政府
https://leadership.ng/sokoto-2027-adc-da.body_zh: 该党指控其成员持续遭到袭击，包括有人在机场开枪、殴打女性支持者以及破坏其竞选办公室。该党州主席兼Alhaji Bello Muhammad Goronyo周日在索科托党总部举行的新闻发布会上表示，该党将继续保持和平并遵守法律，但不会放弃组织政治活动的宪法权利。他呼吁尼日利亚警察部队、国家安全局（DSS）和州政府调查这些袭击，包括10月30日对其州长候选人的殴打。他说：“我们要求保护我们的候选人和支持者，追究肇事者的责任，并制止任何利用国家支持的安全机构限制合法政治活动的行为。”Goronyo表示，ADC已正式通知州政府，决定在索科托启动其总统竞选活动，原定于10月31日举行，但政府回复称不同意举行该活动。他说：“政府回复表示不同意启动竞选活动。这一回复引发了对政府是否致力于政治多元、结社自由以及反对党举行合法政治活动权利的严重关切。”他称，这些袭击并非孤立事件，而是一种持续模式，并将矛头指向据称由州政府从监狱释放的两名与政治暴力有关的人员。该党确认Aliyu K.C.及其同伙与这些袭击有关。Goronyo说：“2026年10月28日星期三，我们的女性支持者在一次和平声援游行中遭到袭击。参加者受伤，手机被抢，衣服被撕破，车辆及其他财产遭到破坏。”他说，同一天，ADC州竞选办公室也遭到袭击，窗户和门被砸，财物被洗劫，3辆摩托车被毁，同时全州范围内的广告牌、海报及其他竞选材料也遭到破坏。Goronyo进一步指控，为竞选启动活动预订的酒店在州政府施压下取消预订，而政府所属酒店则声称房间已被订满。他说：“据报道，政府所属酒店以房间已满为由停止接待客人。我们收到报告称，如果酒店经营者拒绝配合，就可能遭到包括拆除其在内的各种后果。我们正在寻求这些报告的书面确认。如果情况属实，将构成对公共权力的严重滥用。”他质问道：“是谁授权释放他们，采用了什么法律程序，又采取了哪些保障措施？服刑人员获释绝不能被视为恐吓公民的许可证，政治关系也绝不能让任何人免于问责。”Goronyo表示，该党州长候选人Manir Muhammad Dan’iya（Walin Sokoto）周五在索科托Sultan Abubakar III国际机场遭到Sokoto Marshals和Sokoto Community Guards人员袭击。他说，候选人的车辆被砸，枪声响起，而据报道，随行候选人的2名DSS人员被拘留。他说：“当局必须查明是谁授权此次行动，下达了哪些指示，谁在何种权限下开枪，以及为何负责政治候选人的DSS人员会被州安全人员拘留。责任调查不能止于现场人员：任何授权、指示、资助或协助违法行为的个人也必须接受调查。”他还说，该党收到报告称，两支州属安全机构的人员已接到指示，要阻止ADC支持者在竞选启动活动前进入索科托。他说：“我们认为这一指控极其严重。如果得到证实，该指示将侵犯公民自由迁徙、和平集会和政治结社的宪法权利。没有任何州长、政党或安全指挥官有权仅因公民的政治立场而限制他们进入一个州。”他表示，在各社区仍面临武装劫匪和绑架活动的情况下，州居民有权质疑州政府的安全优先事项。他说：“ADC是一个坚持民主原则、政治包容、宪法自由和法治的和平政党。我们对和平的承诺绝不能被误认为软弱，也不能被视为放弃宪法权利。我们不会因暴力、威胁或出于政治动机的骚扰而受到恐吓、噤声或被迫退出民主空间。”他呼吁对枪击、车辆被毁、DSS人员被拘留、Aliyu K.C.及其同伙涉嫌参与袭击、威胁酒店经营者以及拒绝提供场地等事件展开全面调查，并保护ADC候选人、领导人和支持者。他还敦促所有州属安全机构保持政治中立，不得被用于党派活动。我们掌握独家优势。获取实时报道、独家内幕消息和独家角度，直接发送到您的手机。不要满足于过时新闻。加入LEADERSHIP NEWS的WhatsApp，随时随地获取全天候更新 →

Yusuf, in an exclusive interview with LEADERSHIP, recalled the administration’s earlier claims of empowering vulnerable Nigerians through grants, arguing that the latest N50,000 initiative raised questions about the implementation and accountability of previous interventions. He also referenced the proposed N70,000 transportation allowance for workers, which he claimed had been rejected by workers, describing the various relief announcements as attempts to win public support ahead of the elections. According to him, Nigerians are already determined to vote the Tinubu administration out of power and elect the APM’s proposed candidate, Engr. Seyi Makinde, whom he said had demonstrated achievements during his administration in Oyo State. The APM spokesperson also questioned the government’s decision to introduce another cash relief programme despite unresolved concerns surrounding the N-Power scheme and outstanding allowances allegedly owed to beneficiaries. He specifically accused the government of failing to pay six months of outstanding allowances to N-Power beneficiaries, while also recalling controversies surrounding the Ministry of Humanitarian Affairs that preceded the removal of its former minister. Yusuf described the situation as ironic, questioning why the administration was announcing another financial support programme when previous social intervention commitments had allegedly not been fully addressed. He further expressed concern over Nigerians enrolling for the N50,000 grant, particularly given what he described as the government’s previous claims that similar grants had already been distributed. The APM spokesperson, however, advised Nigerians not to reject the proposed financial assistance but to remain conscious of their voting rights and make independent decisions at the ballot. “My advice, let them collect the money and vote wisely,” he said. Yusuf alleged that the cash relief initiative was an attempt by the ruling government to retain power while leaving the underlying economic challenges facing Nigerians unresolved. He maintained that the country needed sustainable economic policies capable of reducing poverty and improving living conditions rather than temporary financial incentives introduced ahead of elections. The APM insisted that Nigerians should assess political parties and candidates based on their records, policies and capacity to address the country’s economic challenges as the 2027 general elections approach. https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/foreignaffa.body: U.S. President Donald Trump has said the United States would talk to North Korea if it is found to be behind the theft of more than $6 billion from Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange. Trump made the remarks at his Mar-a-Lago estate in Palm Beach, Florida, on Saturday after the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) said North Korea was responsible for the theft of virtual assets from Binance on or about Oct. 29. "I'm not concerned. We're learning about it," he said. "We don't know if it's North Korea, but if it is, we'll talk to North Korea about it." In a cyber alert, the FBI identified the North Korean cyber operation as "TraderTraitor," a name previously associated with cryptocurrency thefts carried out by North Korean hackers. The agency said it had observed the hackers converting stolen assets primarily into Ethereum, a major cryptocurrency, in cooperation with the U.S. Secret Service and the Internal Revenue Service's Criminal Investigation division. The FBI warned that the hackers were expected to further launder the stolen assets through decentralized finance platforms and cryptocurrency exchange services that allow users to quickly swap one digital asset for another. The three U.S. agencies urged cryptocurrency exchanges, blockchain operators, analytics firms and other virtual asset service providers to block transactions involving digital wallet addresses used by the North Korean hackers to launder the stolen funds. The FBI's announcement follows an assessment by U.S. blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs, which earlier attributed the estimated $6.36 billion Binance theft to TraderTraitor. Trump's remarks come amid persistent speculation over the possibility of renewed diplomacy between Trump and North Korean leader Kim Jong-un. Trump and Kim met three times during Trump's first presidential term. U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Saturday that Trump remains open to talks with Kim if Pyongyang is willing to discuss issues of concern to Washington and its allies, though no meeting has been scheduled

https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/foreignaffa.body: WASHINGTON — U.S. President Donald Trump remains open to talks with North Korean leader Kim Jong-un if Pyongyang is willing to discuss issues of concern to Washington and its allies, but no meeting has been scheduled, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Saturday. Rubio made the remarks during a press conference following a Group of 20 (G20) foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta. "I think the president's perspective is, if North Korea and Kim Jong-un is prepared to talk with the United States about issues that are of concern to us and of concern to our allies, like South Korea, he would be open to doing it," Rubio said. "Nothing has been scheduled. I do not have anything to announce in regards to that today," he added. His remarks came amid persistent speculations over the possibility of renewed diplomacy between Trump and Kim, who held three meetings during Trump's first presidential term. The comments also followed trilateral talks among Rubio and his South Korean and Japanese counterparts in Atlanta on Friday, during which the three top diplomats reaffirmed their commitment to the complete denuclearization of North Korea. "The president doesn't view talks, doesn't view meeting with someone as a concession." Rubio said. "I know in traditional foreign policy, meeting with someone or inviting someone to something is viewed as a concession that somehow legitimizes them." Asked of recent U.S. visa refusal or delay cases involving South Korean legislators, Rubio said the two countries will "work through" the issue on a bilateral basis. "I think there was one particular visa individual, that there was an issue about regarding behavior, perhaps a couple decades ago. But we'll work through that at a bilateral basis," the secretary said. Rep. Jin Sung-joon of South Korea's ruling Democratic Party (DP) said he has been issued a U.S. visa for a trip to the U.S. Pacific Command, days after he said his application was rejected. Jin's initial visa rejection followed a similar case involving Rep. Jung Chung-rae, former chairman of the DP, earlier this month

https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/foreignaffa.body_zh: 华盛顿——美国国务卿马可·鲁比奥周六表示，如果朝鲜愿意讨论令华盛顿及其盟友关切的问题，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普仍愿与朝鲜领导人金正恩会谈，但目前尚未安排会面。鲁比奥是在亚特兰大举行的二十国集团外长会议结束后的新闻发布会上作出上述表态的。鲁比奥说：“我认为总统的态度是，如果朝鲜和金正恩准备就令我们以及韩国等盟友关切的问题与美国对话，他愿意进行会谈。目前没有任何安排。我今天在这方面没有什么可宣布的。”此前，外界一直猜测特朗普与金正恩可能重启外交接触。金正恩曾在特朗普首个总统任期内与他举行三次会面。这些表态此前还出现在鲁比奥与其韩国和日本 counterparts 周五于亚特兰大举行的三方会谈之后，三名最高外交官在会谈中重申了对朝鲜完全无核化的承诺。鲁比奥说：“总统不认为进行会谈或与某人见面是一种让步。我知道，在传统外交政策中，与某人见面或邀请某人参加某种活动，会被视为一种让步，仿佛这样就能赋予他们合法性。”当被问及美国近期拒绝或延迟向韩国议员发放签证的案件时，鲁比奥表示，两国将在双边基础上“妥善处理”这个问题。这名国务卿说：“我记得有一名特定的签证申请人，可能因行为方面的问题遭到拒签，那或许是几十年前的事了。但我们会在双边基础上妥善处理。”韩国执政党民主党议员 진成俊表示，他已获发赴美国太平洋司令部的美国签证；就在几天前，他曾称自己的签证申请遭到拒发。진成俊最初遭拒签之前，本月早些时候，该党前主席郑忠莱也遭遇了类似情况

Unlock these with Subscription The government on Saturday (October 31, 2026) slashed the export duty on petrol to nil while hiking the levy on export of diesel and aviation turbine fuel (ATF) by ₹3 per litre and 50 paise per litre respectively for the next 15-day period. There was no change in the existing excise duty rates for petrol and diesel for domestic consumption. Diesel exports would now draw a levy of ₹11.5 for every litre against ₹8.5 per litre it drew in the previous fortnight. ATF would be subject to an export levy of ₹11 for every litre against ₹10.5 for every litre as mandated for the previous fortnight. The revised levy on diesel assumes significance as India spiked its exports of the liquid vehicular fuel amid a global supply crunch, particularly in Europe. According to data from real-time analytics provider Kpler, India’s diesel exports stood at 700 kilo barrels per day in October, the highest since September 2025. The government has been conducting a fortnightly review of export levies since March 27, in the backdrop of the conflict in West Asia. These are done based on the average international benchmark prices of crude oil, petrol, diesel and ATF observed since the previous review. https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/foreignaffa.body: Foreign Minister Cho Hyun met separately with his German and Polish counterparts on the sidelines of a Group of 20 (G20) meeting in Atlanta to discuss ways to enhance bilateral cooperation, his office said Saturday. Cho met with German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul on Friday (U.S. time), expressing hope for deeper ties with the European nation in a wide range of areas, including defense, the economy and cutting-edge industries, according to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. In response, Wadephul thanked Seoul's foreign ministry for successfully preparing for German Chancellor Friedrich Merz's recent visit to Korea and expressed hope for expanded cooperation in bilateral trade and investment. Cho also met with his Polish counterpart, Radoslaw Sikorski, and called for continued discussions on cooperation in areas such as defense and batteries as a follow-up to Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk's visit to Korea in April, the ministry said. Sikorski also requested Korea's attention and support for Warsaw's efforts to join the G20, with Cho proposing continued consultations on the matter

https://leadership.ng/fg-tasks-nigerians.body: The Executive Vice Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of the National Agency for Science and Engineering Infrastructure (NASENI), Mr Khalil Suleiman Halilu, made the call during the distribution of solar home systems, clean cooking stoves and household support packs to 330 residents of Ondo State in Akure. Halilu said the initiative was designed to translate research and development into practical products that could improve living conditions and provide economic opportunities for Nigerians. He explained that the solar home systems would provide lighting for households, enable children to study at night and support small businesses, while the clean cooking stoves would offer more efficient cooking alternatives and reduce exposure to smoke when properly used. According to him, wider adoption of locally developed products would encourage domestic manufacturing and strengthen Nigeria’s capacity to develop solutions to its own challenges. He said “This is to promote locally produced items which brings about employment and also to have something good for our communities. He said the NASENI Sustainable Empowerment Programme had reached more than 10 states across the six geopolitical zones, with 330 men and women benefiting from the intervention in Ondo State. The NASENI chief executive added that the programme was intended to take technological innovations beyond research facilities and make them accessible to households and businesses. Also speaking, the Minister of Youth Development, Ayodele Olawande, said beneficiaries would receive additional financial support to enable them to establish or strengthen micro-businesses. Olawande said the intervention was not a political strategy but an effort to take technology-based solutions and economic opportunities to grassroots communities. In his remarks, gov. Yusuf commended Abejide for extending his empowerment programme beyond his constituency, urging other federal lawmakers to support Nigerians irrespective of their ethnic or religious backgrounds. https://leadership.ng/fg-tasks-nigerians.title_zh: 联邦政府敦促尼日利亚人使用本土制造的技术促进经济增长
https://leadership.ng/fg-tasks-nigerians.body_zh: 国家科学与工程基础设施局（NASENI）执行副主席兼首席执行官Khalil Suleiman Halilu先生，在阿库雷向奥 ND州330名居民分发太阳能家庭系统、清洁炊具和家居支持包时发出了这一号召。Halilu表示，该倡议旨在将研究与开发成果转化为实用产品，以改善生活条件，并为尼日利亚人提供经济机会。他解释说，太阳能家庭系统将为家庭提供照明，使儿童能够在夜间学习，并支持小型企业；正确使用时，清洁炊具可提供更高效的烹饪方式，并减少烟雾暴露。据他介绍，推广本地研发产品将鼓励国内制造，增强尼日利亚自主开发应对自身挑战解决方案的能力。他说：“这是为了推广本地生产的产品，既能带来就业，也能让我们的社区获得优质产品。”他说，NASENI可持续发展计划已覆盖全国六个地缘政治区域中的10多个州，其中330名男女在奥ND州受益于该项干预。NASENI首席执行官还表示，该计划旨在让技术创新走出研究机构，使家庭和企业都能获得这些成果。青年发展部长Ayodele Olawande也表示，受益者将获得额外财政支持，以便创办或强化微型企业。Olawande称，这项干预并非政治策略，而是旨在把基于技术的解决方案和经济机会带到基层社区。在发言中，州长Yusuf赞扬Abejide将其赋能计划延伸至选区之外，并敦促其他联邦议员不论尼日利亚人的族裔或宗教背景，都向其提供支持。他说，此类干预将促进国家团结、和平共处和经济发展。我们掌握独家优势。实时报道、突发独家新闻和独家视角将直接发送到您的手机。不要满足于过时新闻。加入LEADERSHIP NEWS WhatsApp频道，获取全天候最新动态 →

https://www.premiumtimesng.com/features-.body: For many residents of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), securing a roof over their heads can mean raising hundreds of thousands, and sometimes millions, of naira at once. Beyond the annual rent itself, prospective tenants often have to contend with agency, agreement and caution fees, while existing tenants face rent increases that can force them to move to less expensive and sometimes more distant communities. It is against this backdrop that the House of Representatives has begun consideration of a new bill seeking to regulate advance rent payments and protect tenants from what it describes as unlawful rental practices. The Federal Capital Territory Advance Rent Regulation and Tenants’ Protection Bill, 2026 (HB.2839), jointly sponsored by Paul Nnamchi (APC, Enugu) and Ahmed Doro (PDP, Katsina), passed first reading on Thursday, 22 October. But the proposal is not simply another attempt to tell landlords how much rent to collect. A closer look at the 17-page bill obtained by PREMIUM TIMES shows that it seeks to create an entire regulatory framework for tenancy in the FCT, covering advance payments, written agreements, agents, complaints, refunds, eviction practices, penalties and dispute resolution. The central provision is contained in Section 4 of the bill. Section 4(1) of the bill provides that a landlord, estate agent or property manager “shall not demand, receive or compel a tenant to pay more than twelve months’ rent in advance” as a condition for granting, renewing or continuing a tenancy. This simply prohibits the demanding, receiving or compelling of a tenant to pay more than one year’s rent in advance as a condition for obtaining, renewing or continuing a tenancy. That means the bill does not ban advance rent or make monthly rent compulsory. Instead, it establishes 12 months as the maximum amount that can be compulsorily demanded upfront. A landlord would still be able to collect one year’s rent in advance if that is the agreed arrangement. But demanding two or three years as a condition for granting or renewing a tenancy would become an offence if the bill becomes law. The bill also attempts to prevent landlords and agents from simply finding another way around the restriction. It specifically lists intermediaries, unexplained premiums, compulsory service charges, artificial renewal or re-grant of a tenancy, separate agreements and other arrangements designed to extract more than 12 months’ rent in advance as prohibited means of evasion. The proposed restriction has an exception. Section 4(4) states that a tenant may voluntarily pay more than 12 months’ rent in advance if “the tenant initiates the offer” and the payment is not imposed by the landlord and the tenant must not have been subjected to coercion, discrimination, threats or retaliation. The agreement must be recorded in writing, and the person receiving the payment bears the burden of proving compliance. This could become one of the contentious provisions during the legislative process. While the bill attempts to distinguish voluntary payments from compulsory demands, proving that a tenant genuinely volunteered to pay several years’ rent could be difficult where the landlord controls access to the property. The proposed law also seeks to formalise the relationship between landlords and tenants. Section 5 requires landlords or their authorised agents to provide written tenancy agreements stating the rent, payment schedule, duration of the tenancy, refundable deposits, fees and other charges, and the rights and obligations of both parties. Landlords and agents would also be required to disclose the nature, amount and legal basis of compulsory fees before a tenancy agreement is concluded and issue receipts or verifiable electronic acknowledgements for payments. The bill also prohibits retaliation against tenants who refuse to make unlawful payments or who complain about violations. A landlord or agent would not be allowed to threaten or unlawfully evict such a tenant, impose a punitive charge, withdraw a lawful benefit or otherwise retaliate against the tenant. The bill introduces a remedy that could significantly change the balance between tenants and landlords. Section 7 introduces a mechanism for recovering unlawfully collected rent. A tenant who has paid rent in violation of the proposed 12-month limit could apply to the proposed FCT Rent Regulation and Tenants’ Protection Authority for a refund. Where the proposed authority determines that a payment contravened the law, it may order the recipient to refund the unlawful amount within 30 days. The bill also allows an aggrieved party to appeal an order of the authority to the FCT High Court. “7(1) A tenant who has paid rent in contravention of section 4 may apply to the Authority for a refund order. (2) Where the Authority determines that a payment was received in contravention of section 4, it may order the recipient to refund the unlawful amount within thirty days after service of the order.” Under Section 8, the bill proposes the establishment of the Federal Capital Territory Rent Regulation and Tenants’ Protection Authority. The authority would receive and investigate complaints, monitor landlords, estate agents and property managers, issue compliance notices, facilitate mediation, order refunds and refer suspected criminal offences to relevant law-enforcement or prosecuting authorities. It would also establish complaint offices and electronic reporting channels throughout the FCT, including satellite towns, and publish periodic reports on rental practices and enforcement outcomes. Its governing board would include representatives of the FCT Administration, the federal ministry responsible for housing, the federal ministry responsible for justice, tenants, landlords or property owners and estate surveyors and valuers. The president will appoint the chairperson and members of the board, subject to Senate confirmation. The president will also appoint the director-general, subject to Senate confirmation. A person convicted of knowingly demanding or receiving unlawful advance rent would face a fine of between ₦500,000 and ₦5 million. A corporate body could face a fine of between ₦5 million and ₦20 million. The court could also order refunds, compensation for proven losses and payment of lawful costs. Failure to comply with a compliance notice issued by the proposed authority would also constitute an offence punishable by a fine of up to ₦1 million. Estate agents and property managers are expressly covered. Where an offence is committed through an intermediary, anyone who knowingly authorised, participated in or facilitated the offence could also be liable. The bill is not solely about the amount of money tenants pay. It also targets the methods some landlords may use to recover possession. It prohibits violence or threats, disconnecting essential services, removing or damaging a tenant’s property, changing locks without lawful authority and other forms of unlawful self-help. At the same time, it makes clear that tenants remain obliged to pay rent lawfully due and that landlords retain the right to recover rent and possession through due process. This is significant because the bill attempts to protect tenants without removing landlords’ existing property rights. This is perhaps the biggest question the lawmakers will have to confront. The bill regulates how much rent can be demanded upfront, but it does not regulate the actual amount landlords can charge as rent. There is no rent ceiling and no limit on how much rent can increase when a tenancy is renewed. A landlord who cannot demand two years’ rent upfront could still charge a high annual rent. The bill also does not address the shortage of affordable housing, construction costs, mortgage access or the wider factors driving rent increases. The proposed authority would have to monitor landlords and agents, investigate complaints and enforce its decisions across the FCT. The bill also provides for the authority to become operational within six months of the law taking effect. Despite its proposed restrictions on advance rent, the bill does not comprehensively regulate other charges tenants face when securing accommodation in Abuja, including agency fees, agreement fees and caution deposits. In Abuja, these charges are random and some tenants pay as high as 40 per cent of their rent for them. Although Section 5 requires landlords and agents to disclose the nature and amount of charges, it does not prescribe a maximum percentage or amount that can be demanded as agency or agreement fees. Neither does it establish a standard ceiling for caution deposits. The bill requires refundable deposits to be stated in tenancy agreements but does not clearly set out a standard formula for calculating them. This means tenants could have a clearer right to know what they are paying for without necessarily having protection against excessive charges. Section 4 prohibits landlords and agents from using charges that are not reasonably related to a service as a means of circumventing the 12-month advance rent restriction. However, this does not amount to a comprehensive regulation of legitimate agency fees or other letting costs. Consequently, tenants could still face substantial upfront expenses even if the bill becomes law. A landlord may no longer be able to compel a tenant to pay two years’ rent, but the tenant could still be required to pay agency, agreement and other charges, provided those charges comply with the law. Another major issue left unresolved is the payment arrangement for salary earners. Many Abuja residents earn monthly salaries but are expected to pay a full year’s rent upfront, with some landlords demanding two years’ rent from new tenants. For workers whose income comes in monthly, raising such a large sum at once can be difficult, even when they can afford the rent over the course of a year. The proposed law would prohibit landlords from compelling tenants to pay more than 12 months’ rent in advance. However, it does not require landlords to accept monthly or quarterly payments. A landlord could therefore still insist on a full year’s rent upfront, provided the demand does not exceed the proposed limit. This means the bill addresses the length of compulsory advance rent but does not fully address the financial difficulty created by the annual payment system. A tenant who cannot raise 12 months’ rent at once may therefore remain unable to secure accommodation, even if the landlord is no longer demanding two years’ payment. The latest proposal is part of a longer-running attempt by lawmakers to address rent practices in Abuja. In January 2022, the Senate introduced a bill sponsored by Smart Adeyemi, then representing Kogi West, seeking to regulate the payment of rent in the FCT. The bill passed second reading in February 2022. PREMIUM TIMES reported at the time that the proposal sought to reduce advance rent for new tenants from the prevailing one- or two-year payments to three months, followed by monthly payments. Mr Adeyemi argued that the existing system placed an excessive burden on low-income residents, particularly salaried workers who could not easily raise one or two years’ rent at once. While supporters argued that advance rent was placing unbearable pressure on residents, Chimaroke Nnamani, then the senator for Enugu East, opposed the proposal, arguing that rent payment was an economic matter that should be driven by market forces, including the availability of land, construction costs and income. He argued that the government should instead invest in housing schemes, mortgages and housing credit rather than regulate the business of private landlords. The Senate nevertheless voted overwhelmingly for the bill at second reading and referred it to the Committee on Housing and Urban Development for further consideration.
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/features-.title_zh: 关于阿布贾拟议房屋租金监管法案，你需要了解的一切
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/features-.body_zh: 对联邦首都 Territory（FCT）的许多居民来说，拥有一个遮风挡雨的家可能意味着一次性筹集数十万，有时甚至是数百万奈拉。除了全年租金本身外，准租户往往还要应对中介费、签约费押金和押金，而现有租户则面临租金上涨，这可能迫使他们搬往价格较低、有时距离更远的社区。正是在这一背景下，众议院开始审议一项新法案，旨在规范预付租金并保护租户免受其所称非法租赁行为的侵害。《2026年联邦首都预付租金监管与租户保护法案》（HB.2839）由保罗·纳姆奇（APC，埃努古州）和艾哈迈德·多罗（PDP，卡齐纳州）共同提案，于10月22日星期四通过一读。但该提案并非只是又一attempt试图规定房东应收取多少租金。PREMIUM TIMES获得的这份17页法案显示，它试图为FCT的租赁关系建立一套完整的监管框架，涵盖预付款、书面协议、中介、投诉、退款、驱逐程序、处罚和争议解决。法案的核心规定载于第4条。法案第4条第1款规定，房东、房地产中介或物业管理人不得将“要求、收取或迫使租户预付超过12个月租金”作为授予、续租或延续租赁关系的条件。这实际上禁止将要求、收取或迫使租户预付超过一年租金作为取得、续租或延续租赁关系的条件。这意味着，该法案并不禁止预付租金，也不强制要求按月付租。相反，它将12个月确立为可被强制要求一次性预付的最高金额。如果双方约定预付一年租金，房东仍可据此收取。但若法案成为法律，将两年或三年租金作为授予或续租租赁关系的条件将成为违法行为。法案还试图防止房东和中介另辟蹊径规避这一限制。法案明确将中介费、来路不明的额外费用、强制服务费、人为安排续租或重新授予租赁关系、另订协议以及其他旨在收取超过12个月预付租金的安排列为禁止的规避手段。拟议限制设有一项例外。第4条第4款规定，如果“租户主动提出”，且该付款并非房东强加，租户也未受到胁迫、歧视、威胁或报复，租户可以自愿预付超过12个月的租金。相关协议必须以书面形式记录，并由收取款项的一方承担证明合规的责任。这可能成为立法过程中的一项争议条款。尽管法案试图区分自愿付款与强制要求，但在房东掌控物业使用权的的情况下，要证明租户确实自愿支付数年租金可能十分困难。拟议法律还试图将房东与租户之间的关系正规化。第5条要求房东或其授权中介提供书面租赁协议，注明租金、付款时间表、租赁期限、可退还押金、各项费用及其他收费，以及双方的权利和义务。房东和中介还必须在租赁协议订立前披露强制收费的性质、金额和法律依据，并为付款出具收据或可核验的电子确认凭证。法案还禁止房东或中介报复拒绝支付非法款项或投诉违法行为的租户。房东或中介不得威胁或非法驱逐此类租户、施加惩罚性收费、收回合法利益或以其他方式报复租户。法案引入的一项救济措施可能显著改变租户与房东之间的力量平衡。第7条引入了追讨非法收取租金的机制。违反拟议12个月上限而支付了租金的租户，可以向拟议的FCT租金监管与租户保护管理局申请退款。若该管理局认定某笔付款违反法律，可以命令收款方在30天内退还非法收取的金额。法案还允许受侵害一方向FCT高等法院上诉管理局的命令。规定如下：“第7条（1）违反第4条支付租金的租户，可以向管理局申请退款命令。（2）管理局认定某笔付款系违反第4条收取的，可以命令收款方在命令送达后30天内退还非法金额。”根据第8条，法案提议成立联邦首都租金监管与租户保护管理局。该管理局将受理并调查投诉，监督房东、房地产中介和物业管理人，发出合规通知，促成调解，责令退款，并将涉嫌犯罪的案件移交相关执法或检察机关。它还将在FCT各地，包括各卫星城设立投诉办公室和电子举报渠道，并定期发布有关租赁实践和执法结果的报告。其董事会将包括FCT行政机关、负责住房事务的联邦部委、负责司法事务的联邦部委、租户、房东或物业所有者以及土地测量师和估价师的代表。总统将任命董事会主席和成员，但须经参议院确认。总统还将任命总干事，同样须经参议院确认。明知要求或收取非法预付租金的人一旦被定罪，将面临₦500,000至₦5 million的罚款。法人团体可能面临₦5 million至₦20 million的罚款。法院还可责令退款、赔偿经证实的损失并支付合法费用。不遵守拟议管理局发出的合规通知，也将构成犯罪，可处以最高₦1 million的罚款。房地产中介和物业管理人被明确纳入适用范围。若通过中介实施犯罪，任何明知并授权、参与或协助实施犯罪的人也可能承担责任。这部法案的意义不只在于租户支付多少钱。它还针对部分房东可能用来收回物业占有权的手段。法案禁止暴力或威胁、切断基本生活服务、搬走或损坏租户财物、未经合法授权更换门锁以及其他形式的非法自助行为。与此同时，法案明确规定，租户仍有义务依法支付应付租金，房东也仍有权通过正当程序收回租金和物业占有权。这一点十分重要，因为该法案试图在不剥夺房东现有财产权利的情况下保护租户。这或许是议员们必须面对的最大问题。法案对可预付租金的数额作出监管，但并未规定房东实际可收取的租金金额。法案没有设定租金上限，也没有限制续租时租金可以上涨多少。无法要求预付两年租金的房东，仍可收取较高的年租金。法案也未处理可负担住房短缺、建筑成本、按揭贷款可获得性以及推高租金的其他更广泛因素。拟议管理局将不得不监督房东和中介、调查投诉并在FCT各地执行决定。法案还规定，该管理局须在法律生效后六个月内开始运作。尽管该法案对预付租金提出限制，但它没有全面监管租户在阿布贾获取住房时面临的其他收费，包括中介费、签约费押金和押金。在阿布贾，这些收费随意收取，有些租户为此支付的金额高达租金的40%。尽管第5条要求房东和中介披露收费的性质和金额，但并未规定中介费或签约费可收取的最高百分比或金额，也没有为押金设定统一上限。法案要求在租赁协议中注明可退还押金，但未明确列出计算押金的标准公式。这意味着，租户或许能更清楚地了解自己支付的是什么，却未必能获得防止过高收费的保护。第4条禁止房东和中介利用与服务没有合理关联的费用，作为规避12个月预付租金限制的手段。但这并不等于对合法中介费或其他出租成本进行全面监管。因此，即使该法案成为法律，租户仍可能面临巨额前期费用。房东或许不能再强迫租户支付两年租金，但只要相关收费符合法律，租户仍可能被要求支付中介费、签约费和其他费用。另一个尚未解决的重要问题是工薪阶层租户的付款安排。许多阿布贾居民按月领取工资，却仍被要求一次性预付全年租金，一些房东还会向新租户索要两年租金。对按月取得收入的劳动者来说，即使其能够在一年过程中负担得起租金，一次筹集如此巨额资金仍很困难。拟议法律将禁止房东迫使租户预付超过12个月的租金，但并不要求房东接受按月或按季付款。因此，只要所要求的金额不超过拟议上限，房东仍可坚持要求一次性预付全年租金。这意味着，该法案处理了强制预付租金的期限问题，却未完全解决年度付款制度造成的经济困难。因此，无法一次筹集12个月租金的租户，可能仍无法获得住房，即便房东已不再索要两年预付款。这项最新提案是议员们为处理阿布贾租赁收费问题而进行的长期努力的一部分。2022年1月，参议院提出一项由时任代表科吉西部选区的斯马特·阿德耶米提案的法案，试图规范FCT的租金支付。该法案于2022年2月通过二读。PREMIUM TIMES当时报道称，该提案寻求将新租户预付租金从当时普遍存在的一年或两年改为三个月预付，此后按月支付。阿德耶米先生认为，现有制度给低收入居民，特别是难以一次筹集一年或两年租金的工薪阶层造成了过重负担。支持者认为预付租金给居民带来难以承受的压力，但时任恩努古东部选区参议员奇马罗克·纳马尼反对该提案，主张租金支付属于经济问题，应由土地供应、建筑成本和收入等市场力量决定。他认为，政府应转而投资住房计划、按揭贷款和住房信贷，而不是监管私人房东的经营。尽管如此，参议院仍在二读时以压倒性多数投票通过该法案，并将其提交住房与城市发展委员会进一步审议。

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/01/n.summary: •Threaten removal of illegal structures on transmission routes The House of Representatives’ Committee on Public Assets has threatened to demolish illegal structures erected on the federal government’s rights of way (ROW) for power transmission projects, warning that encroachment and vandalism were threatening investments in the electricity sector.
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/01/n.summary_zh: •威胁拆除输电线路上的违法建筑。众议院公共资产委员会威胁拆除联邦政府为输电项目预留的通行权（ROW）范围内搭建的违法建筑，并警告称，侵占和故意破坏正威胁电力行业 investments。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/01/n.body: •Threaten removal of illegal structures on transmission routes The House of Representatives’ Committee on Public Assets has threatened to demolish illegal structures erected on the federal government’s rights of way (ROW) for power transmission projects, warning that encroachment and vandalism were threatening investments in the electricity sector. The Chairman of the committee, Kuye Ademorin, gave the warning during inspection of the 132kV New Haven-Ninth Mile-Nsukka Double Circuit Transmission Line in Enugu State and the Egbu 330/132/33kV substation in Owerri, Imo State. The committee expressed concern that churches, hotels, private residences and even state government buildings had been erected along designated transmission routes, potentially delaying the completion of projects designed to improve electricity supply. Other lawmakers on the inspection tour, according to a statement by the NDPHC spokesperson, Nazo Agim, included Mark Obetta, Lanre Okunlola, Sani Rigo and Canice Nwachukwu. Ademorin questioned how state authorities could approve developments along corridors already designated as federal government rights of way, describing the situation as a threat to critical national infrastructure. He said the committee was impressed by the scale of the federal government’s investment in developing a sustainable electricity system but was disappointed that some communities were undermining the initiative through encroachment and vandalism. “We observed the magnitude of investment by the federal government in building a sustainable power system for the country, particularly in our states, to help them develop their industrial base through adequate power supply. “However, to our chagrin and disappointment, we saw a people who are not totally buying into the vision of a greater country for all of us,” he said. The lawmaker warned that the National Assembly would take appropriate measures to ensure that illegal structures were removed from the affected corridors. “It is not going to be business as usual. We are going to take drastic, appropriate steps to ensure that those structures are removed,” he said. The committee also called for stronger collaboration between federal and state governments to protect public assets and prevent further delays to electricity infrastructure projects. At the Egbu substation, the delegation acknowledged that the facility was about 85 per cent complete and, upon completion, would add approximately 250 megawatts to electricity supply in Imo State, significantly improving power delivery to the Orlu area. The project, which was first awarded in 2006, has received renewed attention under the leadership of NDPHC Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, Jennifer Adighije. Ademorin commended the quality of work at the substation and expressed optimism that its anticipated completion around March 2027 would stimulate industrial activities across the South-east. He, however, urged the federal government to ensure the timely completion of ongoing projects and prompt payment of contractors to avoid unnecessary delays. The committee chairman also emphasised the need for adequate and timely compensation for landowners whose properties were acquired for public infrastructure, noting that unresolved compensation issues could trigger disputes and litigation. He appealed to the governors of Enugu and Imo states to work with NDPHC to address encroachment, protect federal assets and accelerate the delivery of the projects. Ademorin further advised Nigerians to verify the ownership and status of land before purchasing properties, particularly around designated government rights of way, to avoid acquiring plots earmarked for public infrastructure. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/01/n.title_zh: 尼日利亚联邦电力委员会：联邦议员谴责电力项目遭侵占和破坏
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/01/n.body_zh: •威胁拆除输电线路沿线非法建筑 众议院公共资产委员会威胁拆除联邦政府输电项目用地范围内非法搭建的设施，并警告称，侵占和破坏行为正在威胁电力行业的投资。委员会主席Kuye Ademorin在检查恩古州132kV New Haven—Ninth Mile—Nsukka双回输电线路以及伊莫州奥韦里Egbu 330/132/33kV变电站时发出警告。委员会表示关切，称指定输电线路沿线已建有教堂、酒店、私人住宅，甚至州政府大楼，可能延误旨在改善电力供应的项目竣工。根据尼日利亚联邦电力控股公司发言人Nazo Agim发表的声明，参加此次检查的其他议员包括Mark Obetta、Lanre Okunlola、Sani Rigo和Canice Nwachukwu。Ademorin质疑州 authorities 如何能够批准在已被划定为联邦政府用地范围的走廊沿线开展开发，并称这一局面威胁到关键国家基础设施。他说，委员会对联邦政府为建设可持续电力体系所投入的大量资金印象深刻，但对一些社区通过侵占和破坏破坏该举措感到失望。他说：“我们看到联邦政府为建设可持续电力体系所投入的大量资金，特别是对我们所在各州的投资，旨在通过充足供电帮助它们发展工业基础。“然而，令我们懊恼和失望的是，我们看到一些民众并不完全认同建设一个属于所有人的更伟大国家这一愿景。”这名议员警告称，国民议会将采取适当措施，确保拆除受影响走廊内的非法建筑。他说：“一切照旧的日子不会继续。我们将采取严厉而适当的措施，确保拆除这些建筑。”委员会还呼吁联邦政府和州政府加强协作，保护公共资产，防止电力基础设施项目进一步延误。在Egbu变电站，代表团承认该设施已完成约85%，竣工后预计将向伊莫州新增约250兆瓦电力供应，显著改善奥鲁地区的供电。该项目于2006年首次中标，在尼日利亚联邦电力控股公司董事兼首席执行官Jennifer Adighije的领导下重新受到关注。Ademorin赞扬了变电站的工程质量，并乐观地表示，其预计于2027年3月左右竣工，将推动尼日利亚东南部各地工业活动。然而，他敦促联邦政府确保在建项目按时完工，并及时向承包商付款，以避免不必要的延误。委员会主席还强调，应向土地被征收用于公共基础设施的业主提供充分、及时的补偿，并指出，补偿问题未得到解决可能引发争端和诉讼。他呼吁恩古州和伊莫州州长与尼日利亚联邦电力控股公司合作，处理侵占问题、保护联邦资产并加快项目交付。Ademorin还建议尼日利亚人在购买房产前核实土地所有权和状态，尤其是在指定的政府用地范围周边，以避免购入 earmarked 用于公共基础设施的地块。THISDAY于1995年1月22日创办，由THISDAY NEWSPAPERS LTD.出版，地址为尼日利亚拉各斯阿帕帕Creek Road 35号，在尼日利亚36个州、联邦首都辖区以及世界各地设有办公室。它是尼日利亚最具权威性的新闻媒体，通过所有平台面向政治、商业、专业和外交精英以及更广泛的中产阶级，同时为有志者和千禧一代提供新思想、文化与技术的交汇点。该报秉持公共信托精神，追求真相与理性，报道范围涵盖突发新闻、政治、商业、金融市场、艺术、体育、社区，以及人与社会的交汇点。您可以发送邮件至：hello@thisdaylive.com，或访问我们的联系我们页面

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/01/h.summary: The Joint Health Sector Unions (JOHESU) have begun mobilising health workers nationwide for possible industrial action over the federal government’s failure to implement the Consolidated Health Salary Structure (CONHESS) adjustment. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/01/h.summary_zh: 联合卫生部门工会（JOHESU）已开始在全國動員醫護人員，可能因聯邦政府未能落實《綜合醫務人員薪資結構》（CONHESS）調整而發動 industrial action。該工會此前警告，將抵制任何企圖阻礙薪資調整的行為，並表示已不再準備容忍進一步延遲落實協議。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/01/h.body: The Joint Health Sector Unions (JOHESU) have begun mobilising health workers nationwide for possible industrial action over the federal government’s failure to implement the Consolidated Health Salary Structure (CONHESS) adjustment. This demand has remained unresolved for about 13 years. The union, which warned that it would resist any attempt to frustrate the salary adjustment, said it was no longer prepared to tolerate further delays in implementing the agreement. This was part of the resolutions reached at an emergency expanded National Executive Council (NEC) virtual meeting held on Thursday, October 29, 2026, attended by its affiliates and organs at federal and state levels. The union recalled that President Bola Tinubu had, on June 5, 2023, promised to actualise the adjustment while appealing to JOHESU to suspend its strike after assuming office. It also recalled that the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare had, on the same date, forwarded the 2021 High Level Body Technical Committee Report on the adjustment to the Budget Office of the Federation, the secretariat of the Presidential Committee on Salaries (PCS). However, JOHESU accused the government of allowing the process to stall because the PCS could not meet, warning that any further attempt to use the committee’s failure to act as an excuse would meet resistance. The union commended the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) and the Trade Union Congress of Nigeria (TUC) for taking decisive steps to secure the adjustment, describing it as the oldest demand in organised labour history. It also reminded the federal government of the provisions of the Trade Unions Act, Cap T14, LFN, 2004, which permits trade unions to negotiate benefit packages and collective bargaining agreements on behalf of their members. JOHESU consequently placed its members on alert and directed the commencement of mobilisation across health institutions nationwide for a possible industrial action and what it described as necessary but unparalleled resistance should the government yield to attempts to frustrate the demand. The union, however, urged members to remain peaceful while awaiting further directives from the NLC and TUC, following the ultimatum and timeline issued to the federal government. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/01/h.title_zh: 卫生工作者动员起来，准备与联邦政府就13年薪资调整延迟问题摊牌
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/01/h.body_zh: 联合卫生部门工会（JOHESU）已开始在全国范围内动员卫生工作者，可能因联邦政府未能落实《统一卫生工资结构》（CONHESS）调整而采取工业行动。这一诉求已悬而未决约13年。该工会曾警告，将抵制任何阻挠工资调整的企图，并表示已不再准备容忍协议落实继续拖延。这是工会于2026年10月29日星期四举行的全国执行委员会（NEC）紧急扩大虚拟会议所通过决议的一部分，其联邦和州级附属机构及组织派员出席了会议。工会回顾称，总统博拉·蒂努布曾于2023年6月5日承诺落实工资调整，同时在上任后敦促JOHESU暂停罢工。工会还指出，联邦卫生和社会福利部于同日向联邦预算办公室暨总统薪资委员会（PCS）秘书处转交了有关调整的2021年高层机构技术委员会报告。然而，JOHESU指责政府任由这一进程陷入停滞，因为PCS无法开会，并警告称，任何再次企图以委员会未采取行动作为拖延借口的做法都将遭到抵制。工会赞扬尼日利亚劳工大会（NLC）和尼日利亚工会大会（TUC）为促成工资调整采取果断措施，并称这是有组织劳工历史上持续时间最长的诉求。工会还提醒联邦政府遵守《2004年工会法》T14章《尼日利亚联邦法律汇编》的规定，该法允许工会代表成员谈判福利方案和集体谈判协议。因此，JOHESU已要求成员保持戒备，并指示在全国各医疗和卫生机构启动动员，为可能采取工业行动以及其所称必要但前所未有的抵制行动作准备，以防政府屈从于阻挠这一诉求的企图。不过，在等待NLC和TUC根据向联邦政府发出的最后通牒及时间表进一步下达指示期间，工会仍敦促成员保持和平。THISDAY于1995年1月22日创刊，由THISDAY NEWSPAPERS LTD.出版，地址为尼日利亚拉各斯阿帕帕克里克路35号，在尼日利亚36个州、联邦首都地区及世界各地设有办公室。作为尼日利亚最具权威性的新闻媒体，THISDAY通过所有平台服务政治、商业、专业和外交精英以及更广泛的中产阶级，同时为有志者、千禧一代提供新思想、文化和技术交汇的平台。该报秉持公共信托精神，致力于追求真相与理性，报道范围涵盖突发新闻、政治、商业、金融市场、艺术、体育和社区等议题，直至探索人与社会的交汇点。您可以发送邮件至：hello@thisdaylive.com，或访问我们的联系我们页面

https://www.yna.co.kr/view/akr2026110102.summary_zh: （首爾=聯合新聞社）記者申昌永=中國正快速擴大其市場版圖，不僅限於消費品和中間產品，在工業設備市場的布局也在加速。有觀點指出，韓國若要應對這一趨勢，就必須在先進市場突出供應可靠性，並在新兴市場鎖定生產工藝升級的需求。韓國貿易協會國際貿易通商研究員在1日發布的《中國工業設備出口的崛起與全球供應結構變化》報告中作出上述表述。
https://www.yna.co.kr/view/akr2026110102.body: (서울=연합뉴스) 신창용 기자 = 중국이 소비재와 중간재를 넘어 산업설비 시장에서도 영역을 빠르게 넓히고 있는 것으로 나타났다. 한국이 이에 대응하려면 선진 시장에서는 공급 신뢰성을 내세우고 신흥 시장에서는 생산공정 고도화 수요를 공략해야 한다는 지적이 나왔다. 한국무역협회 국제무역통상연구원은 1일 발표한 '중국 산업설비 수출의 부상과 글로벌 공급구조 변화' 보고서에서 이같이 밝혔다. 보고서에 따르면 중국의 산업설비 수출액은 2015년 1천42억달러에서 2025년 2천572억달러로 약 2.5배 급증했다. 이는 연평균 8.2% 증가한 수준으로, 같은 기간 소비재(1.8%)와 중간재(6.0%)의 성장세를 크게 웃도는 수치다. 중국의 역할이 소비재·중간재 공급자를 넘어 글로벌 제조업 생산 기반을 제공하는 설비 공급자로 확장되고 있는 셈이다. 한국과 중국의 산업설비 수출경합도(ESI)는 2015년 46에서 2025년 54로 상승했다. 독일(55→62)과 일본(44→47)도 중국과의 경합도가 동반 상승했다. 중국은 기존에 강점을 보였던 전력설비와 식품·섬유가공기계 외에도 물류·이송설비에서 독일을 제쳤다. 범용·기타 설비 부문에서는 독일과 공동 1위로 올라서는 등 범용성 높은 분야를 중심으로 글로벌 공급 영향력을 크게 넓혔다. 중국의 산업설비 점유율은 신흥 시장에서 2015년 21.1%에서 2024년 29.6%로 급등했으나 미국의 통상 제재 영향이 미친 선진 시장에서는 12.8%에서 14.0%로 소폭 상승하는 데 그쳤다. 보고서는 독일과 일본의 점유율이 동반 하락하는 사이 한국이 3.0%에서 3.3%로 안정적인 입지를 유지한 선진 시장에서는 공급 신뢰성과 현지 대응 역량을 바탕으로 입지를 넓힐 수 있다고 평가했다. 반면 중국의 저가 공세로 한국 점유율이 6.3%에서 4.1%로 하락한 신흥 시장에서는 생산기지 신규·증설 초기 단계부터 참여해 설비 조달 기회를 선점하고, 이후 자동화와 고정밀화, 설비 교체 수요까지 연계해야 한다고 제언했다. 허슬비 무역협회 연구원은 "중국이 가격경쟁력을 앞세워 산업설비 공급을 빠르게 늘리고 있는 만큼 우리 기업은 품질과 납기 신뢰성, 부품 공급·유지보수 역량으로 차별화해야 한다"며 "정부 차원에서도 현지 인증 대응과 수요기업 발굴 지원 등을 강화해 우리 기업의 해외 진출 부담을 낮춰야 한다"고 강조했다. 제보는 카카오톡 okjebo <저작권자(c) 연합뉴스, 무단 전재-재배포, AI 학습 및 활용 금지> 2026/11/01 11:29 송고 2026년11월01일 11시29분 송고
https://www.yna.co.kr/view/akr2026110102.title_zh: 中国工业设备出口激增……“韩国应以质量、交付和售后服务应对”
https://www.yna.co.kr/view/akr2026110102.body_zh:
（首尔=韩联社）记者申창용报道称，中国正在消费产品和中间产品之外，迅速扩大在工业设备市场的影响范围。有观点指出，韩国若要加以应对，就必须在发达市场突出供应可靠性，并在新兴市场开拓生产流程升级需求。韩国贸易协会国际贸易研究员1日发布的《中国工业设备出口的跃升与全球供应结构变化》报告称，工业设备出口额从2015年的1042亿美元增至2025年的2572亿美元，约为原来的2.5倍，年均增长率达到8.2%，远高于同期消费产品（1.8%）和中间产品（6.0%）的增长速度。这意味着，中国正从消费产品和中间产品供应国，扩展为为全球制造业生产基础提供设备的供应国。
韩国与中国工业设备出口竞争度（ESI）从2015年的46升至2025年的54。德国（55→62）和日本（44→47）与中国之间的竞争度也同步上升。除电力设备以及食品、纺织加工机械等原有优势领域外，中国在物流和输送设备方面也超过德国。在通用及其他设备领域，中国升至与德国并列第一，广泛扩大了在全球供应领域的影响力。
报告称，中国工业设备市场占有率在新兴市场从2015年的21.1%大幅升至2024年的29.6%；但在受美国贸易制裁影响的发达市场，仅从12.8%小幅升至14.0%。报告评价称，在德国和日本市场占有率同步下降的情况下，韩国在发达市场通过将占有率稳定在3.0%至3.3%，可以凭借供应可靠性和当地应对能力扩大市场影响力。
报告建议，在因中国低价攻势而使韩国市场占有率从6.3%降至4.1%的新兴市场，韩国企业应从生产基地新建和扩建初期就参与其中，先行获取设备采购机会，之后再将自动化、高精度化以及设备更新需求一并开发。
韩国贸易协会研究员具晓日（허슬비）强调：“中国凭借价格竞争力迅速扩大工业设备供应，因此我国企业应通过质量、交货期可靠性以及零部件供应和维护能力实现差异化。政府层面也应加强当地认证应对措施，并支持挖掘需求企业，以减轻我国企业出海面临的负担。”

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/01/h.body: The Zamfara State Police Command recently announced the arrest of a 22-year-old member of the Jama’atu Izalatil Bid’ah Wa’iqamatus Sunnah (JIBWIS), Umar Ibrahim Gandi Maradun for chanting incitements to religious violence in Nigeria. In a viral video, the accused was seen leading the chant: “Give Us Rifles to Kill Arna (infidels/Christians)….” in places like Enugu and Jos. According to the police, the suspect was located in Maradun. However, the police said the road from Gusau to Maradun was so bad that they had to contact JIBWIS in Maradun to bring the suspect to Gusau, in a motorcycle, popularly known as Okada. The matter became more disturbing considering the fact that the three former governors of the state since the enthronement of democracy almost came from nearly the affected area. For instance, Maradun is the home of the Minister of State for Defence, Bello Matawalle, who is also the immediate past governor of Zamfara State. The distance from Gusau to Maradun is officially between 91 to 100 kilometres. That should ordinarily take about 70 minutes on a modestly bad road. Now it takes over 180 minutes due mostly to the unmotorable nature of the road, and worsened by insecurity. Zamfara is also the home of Senator Abdulaziz Yari, the Director-General of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council mandated to oversee the re-election campaign of President Bola Tinubu. He is from Talata Mafara, which is separated from Maradun by less than 25 kilometres. Both communities are in the same Zamfara West Senatorial District currently represented in the Senate by Senate Yari, who was also governor of the state. According to media reports, the bad road continues to the village of Senator Yari, through to Talata Mafara Central Primary School where he graduated. Also from Zamfara West is Senator Sani Yerima, who comes from Anka, about 110 kilometres from Gusau. He was also Governor of the state for eight years until 2007 and senator thereafter for 12 years from 2007-2019. Reports claim there is also no road to his place. The state also witnessed the worst form of insecurity when the three were governors. These are the three men leading the charge to bring Renewed Hope to Nigerians. Charity, they say, begins at home. To many, the trio failed the people of the state. On the day of the deadly attack, the Taraba State Police Command said only 10 bodies were recovered, but the next day, it said the death toll had risen to 58, including 15 people who drowned while fleeing in an overloaded canoe.
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/01/t.summary_zh: 近期有报道证实，塔拉巴州卡里姆拉米多地方政府辖区比纳里社区遭武装分子袭击，造成80人死亡，相关消息不断令人痛心，也引发人们对联邦政府保护尼日利亚人生命能力削弱的担忧。致命袭击当天，塔拉巴州警察司令部表示仅发现10具遗体，但第二天又称死亡人数已升至58人，其中包括15人在乘坐超载独木舟逃离时溺亡。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/01/t.body: R ecent reports confirming the killing of 80 people in bandits’ attacks on the Binnari community in Karim Lamido Local Government Area of Taraba State have continued to break hearts, raising concerns about the federal government’s weakening capacity to protect the lives of Nigerians. The report recorded that the attack, which led to massive looting of shops and market stalls and setting of houses ablaze, occurred on Friday, October 23, the community’s weekly market day. The incident to place on a day when traders and buyers from surrounding settlements converged to exchange farm produce, food and other goods, just shortly after Juma’at prayers. Residents said the assailants stormed the community on motorcycles from neighbouring Plateau State, and carried out the four-hour reign of terror unchallenged. By the time the attackers withdrew, residents were searching nearby bushes and a river for their missing relatives, while burnt houses, damaged shops and abandoned belongings testified to the scale of the destruction. On the day of the deadly attack, the Taraba State Police Command said only 10 bodies were recovered, but the next day, it said the death toll had risen to 58, including 15 people who drowned while fleeing in an overloaded canoe. The police spokesperson, Victor Mshelizah, said search operations led to the recovery of additional bodies from surrounding bushes. By Tuesday, it was gathered that the death toll had further risen to 80. Beyond the loss of lives and property, the attack has renewed concerns about the ability of security agencies to protect isolated and vulnerable communities across the country. A trader identified only as Adamu said the assailants operated for hours without resistance. “We have no government in place,” he said, describing the duration of the attack and the destruction of goods during the market raid. Following the attack, the police announced the deployment of additional personnel, alongside the Nigerian Army and other security agencies. Residents were urged to remain calm, stay vigilant and provide credible information to security operatives. Condemning the killing, the global human rights organisation, Amnesty International, accused the federal government of failing to adequately protect vulnerable rural communities from repeated deadly attacks by gunmen and terrorists. The human rights organisation, in a statement, said the attack demonstrated a “disdain for the sanctity of life” and called for an impartial investigation, justice for the victims and adequate reparations for survivors. It said the incident reflected a wider pattern of violence against rural communities in parts of northern Nigeria, where armed groups have repeatedly attacked settlements, killed residents, destroyed property and abducted people. It further criticised the Nigerian authorities for what it described as their failure to prevent recurring atrocities and ensure that suspected perpetrators were brought to justice. The latest attack occurred despite Governor Agbu Kefas’ earlier intervention. Last January, he declared Karim-Lamido a special area of security concern through Executive Order No. 1 of 2026, citing recurring communal clashes, bandit-related attacks and violent herders’ attackers. The declaration was aimed at strengthening efforts to restore peace, protect residents and create conditions for normal economic and social activities. But violence has continued to threaten communities in the area. Observers feel that the Binnari killings are part of a wider pattern of insecurity in Taraba, where communal clashes, banditry, kidnapping and attacks on rural settlements have repeatedly threatened lives and livelihoods. The entire local government has featured prominently in the violence. Its location near the boundaries with Plateau, Bauchi and Gombe states added a cross-border dimension to security operations, particularly where armed groups can move through rural settlements and difficult terrain. In general, banditry has become a growing problem in North-west and North-central, with powerful gangs battling overstretched police and military across hard-to-reach, rural locations. Driven by money rather than ideology, the bandits in Nigeria target poorly policed rural areas, kidnapping for ransom and killing residents. The terror gangs raid villages and impose “taxes” on farmers and mining operations in areas with little state presence. The Armed Conflict Location and Event Data Project (ACLED), an independent, non-profit global research organisation and conflict monitor, recorded thousands of deaths (over 13,485 killed across North-Western states between 2010 and 2023, with a sharp surge of 2,742 casualties across 599 incidents in 2025 alone). Hundreds of thousands have been displaced. Bandits operate not as a single army, but as a loose “franchise” of over 120 armed groups led by regional commanders known as kachalas. Their tactics include mass motorcycle-borne raids, village destruction and looting, kidnap-for-ransom operations, cattle rustling, and imposing illegal “protection taxes” on farmers and miners. Originating from historical attacks on farmers and destruction of farmlands by herders, the crisis expanded due to climate change, shrinking grazing lands, poverty, gold-funded arms smuggling, and vast, unpoliced forested sanctuaries. The Nigerian military regularly launches air strikes and ground sweeps, yet they seem to be growing by the day. Local and state governments have occasionally attempted localised amnesties or peace talks, which critics and defence analysts argue fail because the gangs lack political ideology and repeatedly break truces. The primary responsibility of any government is securing the lives and property of its citizens, but the people hardly see this being demonstrated each time. As sad as the deaths were, there was not a single reaction or statement from the President Bola Tinubu and the Presidency, even as a succour to the community. Even though President Tinubu has repeatedly ordered troops to pursue suspected terrorists responsible for these mass killings of people across the country, Nigerians are yet to see any significant improvement, as people are still being killed almost daily. It was only the Senate that called for an urgent security offensive in border communities across Taraba, Plateau and Bauchi states. The lawmakers urged security agencies to establish additional security camps and intensify surveillance in the affected areas to prevent further attacks and protect vulnerable communities. The upper legislative chamber noted that the continued activities of armed bandits in rural communities undermined the government’s constitutional responsibility to protect lives and property. It warned that failure to address the recurring attacks could lead to further loss of lives, destruction of property, displacement of residents and worsening humanitarian challenges, and that no community should be left at the mercy of armed criminal groups. There is no country where the leaders truly value human lives that will not be jolted by the loss of 80 lives. In normal climes, the attack is enough to declare a state of emergency on insecurity in the state until the perpetrators are fished out and dealt with appropriately. But in Nigeria where the authorities and citizens are inundated with frequent news of massive killing, nothing bothers them anymore. Until authorities demonstrate that vulnerable communities such as Binnari are adequately protected, the killings will remain a grim reminder of the gap between official security commitments and the safety residents experience on the ground. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/01/t.title_zh: 塔拉巴州杀人案频发与治理危机
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/01/t.body_zh: 最新报道证实，武装劫匪袭击塔拉巴州卡里姆拉米多地方政府辖区宾纳里社区，造成80人死亡，消息不断令人痛心，也引发人们对联邦政府保护尼日利亚人生命安全能力削弱的担忧。报道称，袭击发生于10月23日星期五，即该社区每周一次的集市日。袭击导致大量商店和市场摊位遭洗劫，房屋被纵火焚毁。当天，附近聚居地的商贩和买家聚集在社区内 exchanged 农产品、食品及其他商品，事件就发生在他们刚刚结束主麻聚礼不久之后。居民称，袭击者从邻近的 Plateau 州骑摩托车冲入社区，并在无人抵抗的情况下持续了4小时的恐怖统治。袭击者撤离时，居民正在附近的灌木丛和河中寻找失踪的亲人，被焚毁的房屋、受损的商店和被遗弃的物品则见证了破坏的严重程度。致命袭击当天，塔拉巴州警察司令部表示仅发现10具遗体；但第二天又称，死亡人数已升至58人，其中包括15人在乘坐超载独木舟逃离时溺亡。警方发言人 Victor Mshelizah 表示，搜索行动从周边灌木丛中发现了更多遗体。到星期二，人们获悉死亡人数进一步升至80人。除了生命和财产损失外，此次袭击再次引发人们对安全机构保护全国偏远、脆弱社区能力的担忧。一名仅透露姓名为 Adamu 的商贩说，袭击者长达数小时未遇抵抗。他描述了袭击持续时间以及市场突袭中货物遭破坏的情况，并说：“我们这里没有政府。”袭击发生后，警方宣布增派人员，同时由尼日利亚陆军及其他安全机构配合行动。居民被敦促保持冷静、提高警惕，并向安全人员提供可靠信息。全球人权组织大赦国际谴责此次杀戮，指责联邦政府未能充分保护脆弱农村社区，使其免遭持枪犯罪分子和恐怖分子反复发动的致命袭击。该人权组织在一份声明中表示，此次袭击显示出对“生命神圣性”的蔑视，并呼吁开展公正调查，为受害者伸张正义，并给予幸存者充分赔偿。该组织称，这起事件反映了尼日利亚北部部分地区针对农村社区的更广泛暴力模式；武装团体一再袭击聚居地、杀害居民、破坏财产并绑架人口。该组织还批评尼日利亚当局未能阻止暴行再次发生，也未能确保将疑似犯罪者绳之以法。尽管州长 Agbu Kefas 此前采取了干预措施，最新袭击仍然发生。今年1月，他通过2026年第1号行政命令，将卡里姆拉米多列为特别安全关注地区，理由是当地社区冲突不断发生、武装劫匪袭击频仍，以及暴力牧民袭击事件。该声明旨在加强恢复和平、保护居民以及为正常经济和社会活动创造条件的工作。然而，暴力活动仍在威胁该地区社区。观察人士认为，宾纳里惨案是塔拉巴州更广泛安全局势恶化的一部分；当地社区冲突、匪患、绑架和针对农村聚居地的袭击一再威胁生命和生计。整个地方政府辖区在暴力事件中首当其冲。该地靠近 Plateau、Bauchi 和 Gombe 三州边界，为安全行动增加了跨境因素，尤其是在武装团体能够经由农村聚居地和崎岖地形流动的情况下。总体而言，武装匪患已成为尼日利亚西北部和中北部日益严重的问题，强大的犯罪团伙在难以抵达的偏远农村与警力不足、兵力吃紧的警察和军队抗衡。这些劫匪受金钱而非意识形态驱动，袭击治安薄弱的农村地区，通过绑架勒索赎金并杀害居民牟利。恐怖团伙突袭村庄，在国家力量鲜少介入的地区向农民和采矿活动征收“税费”。武装冲突地点与事件数据项目（ACLED）是一家独立、非营利的全球研究组织和冲突监测机构。该机构记录了数千人死亡：2010年至2023年期间，西北部各州共有超过13,485人死亡；仅2025年，599起事件便造成2,742人伤亡，增幅显著。数十万人被迫流离失所。武装劫匪并非作为单一军队行动，而是由120多个武装团体构成的松散“加盟网络”，由被称为 kachalas 的地区指挥官领导。他们惯用的手段包括大规模摩托车突袭、摧毁村庄、洗劫财物、绑架勒索、盗掠牲畜，以及向农民和矿工征收非法“保护费”。这场危机起源于牧民对农民的历史性袭击和农地破坏，随后因气候变化、牧场萎缩、贫困、由黄金资金支持的武器走私，以及大片缺乏治安管理的森林避难所而扩大。尼日利亚军方经常发动空袭和地面清剿，但袭击似乎仍在与日俱增。地方政府和州政府偶尔会尝试局部特赦或和平谈判，但批评者和国防分析人士认为，这些努力无法奏效，因为这些团伙缺乏政治理念，并且屡次违背停火协议。任何政府的首要责任都是保障公民生命和财产安全，但民众几乎看不到这一点在每一次事件中得到体现。死亡人数令人悲痛，但总统 Bola Tinubu 和总统府对此次袭击没有作出任何反应或声明，也没有向社区提供任何慰问。尽管 Tinubu 总统已多次命令部队追捕涉嫌制造全国多地大规模杀戮的恐怖分子，尼日利亚人仍未看到局势有显著改善，几乎每天仍有人丧生。只有参议院呼吁在塔拉巴州、Plateau 州和 Bauchi 州的边境社区紧急开展安全攻势。议员敦促安全机构设立更多安全营地，并加强受影响地区的监视，以防止进一步袭击并保护脆弱社区。参议院指出，武装劫匪持续在 rural 社区活动，削弱了政府保护生命和财产的宪法责任。参议院警告，若不处理反复发生的袭击，可能造成更多人员死亡、财产破坏、居民流离失所和人道主义挑战加剧，任何社区都不应落入武装犯罪集团的魔掌。80条生命的丧失足以震动任何真正珍视人生命的国家。在正常情况下，此次袭击已足以促使该州就安全问题宣布紧急状态，直至抓获肇事者并依法处置。但在尼日利亚，当局和公民不断看到大规模杀戮的消息，已经不会再为此感到不安。在当局证明已对宾纳里等脆弱社区提供充分保护之前，这些杀戮仍将是官方安全承诺与居民实际安全之间巨大落差的冷酷提醒。THISDAY https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/01/o.body: Former Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, sparked widespread outrage recently after issuing a stern warning that anyone caught manipulating the 2027 elections would be killed. Speaking at a political event in his constituency, Omo-Agege warned that anyone who attempted to rig or manipulate votes in the upcoming polls would face severe consequences. Addressing supporters and party faithful in Delta Central, Omo-Agege declared that the era of political actors subverting the popular mandate was over. Omo-Agege, who is seeking election to the Delta Central senatorial seat under the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), emphasised that voters were prepared to defend their votes at polling units nationwide. “I want to make the news again. Anybody who rigs the election on that day, we will kill him! If you don’t value your life, come and rig the election. They’re rigging your future. They’re rigging the future of your children. We’re waiting for them. Let them try it. It is rig-and- die. We’re going to give them aura for aura. There’s no court this time. We’re going to fight,” he was quoted as saying. Omo-Agege declared his intention to contest for the Delta Central senatorial seat in the 2027 elections in May. He resigned his membership of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in a letter dated May and addressed to the chairman of the party’s Orogun Ward 2 in Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State. Omo-Agege’s comment was not only unfortunate but unguarded and totally condemnable. He should know that it is inappropriate for a man of his calibre to advocate for jungle justice. As a lawyer and a former lawmaker, he should know that the best way to treat anybody arrested for a crime, is to be handed over to the police for prosecution. The police should invite him for questioning, and if possible, to write an undertaking that he will not encourage the killing of anyone during the 2027 general election. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/01/o.body_zh: 参议院前副议长、参议员奥维·奥莫-阿格吉近日因严厉警告称，任何操纵2027年选举的人都会被杀，引发广泛愤慨。奥莫-阿格吉在其选区的一场政治活动上警告称，任何企图在即将举行的选举中舞弊或操纵选票的人都将面临严重后果。他在向中三角洲州的支持者和党内人士发表讲话时宣称，政治人物颠覆民意的时代已经结束。奥莫-阿格吉正以尼日利亚民主党（NDC）候选人身份角逐中三角洲州联邦参议院席位，他强调，选民已准备好在全国各地的投票站捍卫自己的选票。据报道，他说：“我要再次成为新闻人物。任何人在那一天操纵选举，我们就会杀了他！如果你不珍惜自己的生命，就来操纵选举吧。他们正在操纵你的未来，操纵你孩子的未来。我们正等着他们。让他们试试看。那就是舞弊和死亡。我们将以同样的手段回敬他们。这次没有法庭。我们将抗争到底。”奥莫-阿格吉于5月宣布 intends 参加2027年中三角洲州联邦参议院席位选举。他在5月写给尼日利亚三角洲州乌盖利北地方政府辖区该党奥罗贡第2选区主席的一封信中，辞去了全尼日利亚进步大会党（APC）的党籍。奥莫-阿格吉的言论不仅不幸，而且缺乏审慎，完全应受谴责。他应当知道，像他这样资历的人鼓吹丛林司法并不合适。作为一名律师和前立法者，他理应懂得，对任何因犯罪被捕的人，最恰当的处理方式是将其移交警方起诉。警方应邀请他接受询问，并尽可能要求他签署承诺书，保证在2027年大选期间不鼓励杀害任何人。THISDAY创刊于1995年1月22日，由THISDAY NEWSPAPERS LTD.出版，社址位于尼日利亚拉各斯阿帕帕克里克路35号，在尼日利亚36个州、联邦首都辖区及世界各地设有办公室。作为尼日利亚最权威的新闻媒体，该报通过所有平台为政治、商业、专业和外交精英以及更广泛的中产阶层提供服务，同时充当抱负者和千禧一代探索新思想、文化与技术的交汇点。该报是一项公共信托，致力于追求真理与理性，报道范围涵盖突发新闻、政治、商业、金融市场、艺术、体育和社区等议题，直面个人与社会之间的 crossroads。您可以发送邮件至：hello@thisdaylive.com，或访问我们的联系我们页面

https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/us-c.body: ABUJA –The United States District Court for the District of Columbia has denied a motion by Aaron Greenspan seeking limited discovery from Nigerian President Bola Tinubu and DCI Group in ongoing litigation under the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA). “The Court’s decision makes clear that this Freedom of Information Act proceeding cannot be used to pursue discovery unrelated to the legal questions before it,” said attorney Christopher W. Carmichael. According to him, the Court also denied a separate motion by nonparty Karl Von Batten seeking permission to file an amicus curiae (friend-of-the-court) brief, as well as Greenspan’s related request for judicial notice. Additionally, the Court denied Greenspan’s motion for summary judgment. “The Court also denied the plaintiff’s motion for summary judgment and rejected a separate request to introduce an amicus brief,” said Attorney Oluwole Afolabi. Carmichael表示：“法院的裁决明确表明，这起依据《信息自由法》提起的诉讼不能被用于寻求与法院目前审理的法律问题无关的证据。”据他介绍，法院还驳回了非诉讼当事人Karl Von Batten提出的另一项动议。该动议请求法院准许其提交法庭之友意见书，同时法院也驳回了Greenspan关于司法认知的相关请求。此外，法院还驳回了Greenspan提出的简易判决动议。律师Oluwole Afolabi表示：“法院还驳回了原告要求简易判决的动议，并拒绝了提交法庭之友意见书的另一项请求。”此处发表的评论不代表Vanguard报纸及其任何员工的观点

https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new.summary_zh: 铁路部长阿什瓦尼·瓦伊什瑙周六表示，印度总理纳伦德拉·莫迪已批准子弹头列车项目的北线走廊。该走廊将连接德里、阿格拉、坎普尔、勒克瑙、阿约提亚、瓦拉纳西、普拉亚格拉杰、巴特那和西里古里，线路还将延伸至古瓦哈提。走廊将大幅缩短出行时间，预计从德里到瓦拉纳西的旅程仅需3小时35分钟。
https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new.body: Railway minister Ashwini Vaishnaw on Saturday said Prime Minister Narendra Modi has approved the North Corridor of the bullet train project, connecting Delhi, Agra, Kanpur, Lucknow, Ayodhya, Varanasi, Prayagraj, Patna and Siliguri, with the route extending to Guwahati. The corridor will significantly reduce travel time, with the journey between Delhi and Varanasi expected to take three hours and 35 minutes. The proposed travel times include 59 minutes between Delhi and Agra, one hour and 45 minutes to Kanpur, and two hours and 12 minutes to Lucknow. The Lucknow-Varanasi journey is expected to take one hour and 21 minutes. Vaishnaw emphasised that the project would be built under the Make in India initiative. “The construction is progressing rapidly. It will be fully ‘Make in India’, built by the youth and welders of India.” Chief minister Yogi Adityanath said an action plan had been prepared to operate a bullet train between Delhi and Varanasi which will reduce travel time to three-and-a-half hours. https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/fg-d.summary: The Federal Government has deployed a specialised technical team to Ogun State to investigate recurring subsurface gas emissions that have triggered health concerns and disrupted academic activities in secondary schools across the Ijebu axis. The intervention, coordinated by the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC), is aimed at establishing the geological source of the emissions and recommending lasting solutions to the recurring incidents affecting schools and surrounding communities.
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/fg-d.summary_zh: 联邦政府已派出专业技术团队前往奥贡州，调查地下气体反复逸散问题。这些气体逸散已引发健康担忧，并扰乱伊杰布地区沿线多所中学的教学活动。此次行动由尼日利亚上游石油监管委员会（NUPRC）协调，旨在确定气体逸散的地质来源，并提出持久解决方案，以应对影响学校及周边社区的反复事件。
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/fg-d.body: The Federal Government has deployed a specialised technical team to Ogun State to investigate recurring subsurface gas emissions that have triggered health concerns and disrupted academic activities in secondary schools across the Ijebu axis. The intervention, coordinated by the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC), is aimed at establishing the geological source of the emissions and recommending lasting solutions to the recurring incidents affecting schools and surrounding communities. The deployment followed reports of localised gas seepages suspected to have caused oxygen depletion and breathing difficulties among students and other residents in the affected communities. Speaking during a joint press briefing and commencement of a site assessment in Ijebu Ode on Saturday, the Federal Government’s Ad-hoc Committee said preliminary indications suggested that the emissions could be associated with natural subsurface geological processes rather than leaks from petroleum pipelines. The team, however, stressed the need for further technical investigations to establish the actual source and nature of the emissions. Speaking at the briefing, the team leader and Assistant Director at the NUPRC, Prosper Okonedo, said the Commission had constituted the committee following an initial assessment conducted by the Ogun State Government. Okonedo explained that the Commission’s Chief Executive, Mrs Oritsemeyawa Eyesan, directed the deployment of experts from its Lagos regional office to collaborate with the state government and investigate the situation. According to him, “about two weeks ago, the Commission Chief Executive of NUPRC, Mrs. Oritsemeyawa Eyesan, advised that we set up an ad-hoc committee from the Lagos regional office to come to the state because the state government had conducted an initial assessment and submitted their report.” He disclosed that the Commission had also been investigating similar incidents in other parts of the country, including communities in Rivers and Delta states. “Presently, we have a study group known as the Epe Study Group. They are looking into similar issues in a village community in Rivers State, and there is one right now in Delta State where we have established that gas seepage is emanating from the subsurface. “However, for this state, we cannot really say what it is right now. That is why we are here, and we are going to deploy to the site to see the situation for ourselves, even though the state government had reported seepages of gas affecting certain secondary schools in some communities,” he said. Okonedo said the federal government was committed to working with the Ogun State government to address the situation and safeguard residents. “The government is there to ensure the welfare and well-being of the Nigerian people. If that is the paramount role of government, that is why we as a Commission have come to work with the state government to proffer solutions to whatever problem exists in this community. “My team and I will do an assessment and come up with a report that will work well for the Nigerian people,” he added. Also speaking, the Ogun State Commissioner for Environment, Mr Ola Oresanya, described the recurring emissions as an emerging environmental challenge that requires coordinated intervention and technical expertise at the national level. Oresanya said similar incidents had been reported in Rivers, Delta and Osun states, suggesting that the problem might extend beyond isolated communities in Ogun. “We have similar problems going on right now in Rivers, Delta, Osun, and here in Ogun State. Coincidentally for us in Ogun State, this is happening around schools. But we need to establish that what is happening around the region is similar to what we are witnessing here; it is not just a local problem,” he said. The commissioner appealed to residents to remain calm while investigations continued, assuring them that the state government was working with relevant experts to determine the cause of the emissions. “All I want to say is that we don’t have any reason to panic. All we need to do is stay concerned, but please don’t panic. What we know and what we are bringing to the table is that the gas affecting our people is subsurface gas. We’ve proved that over and over. “There is no gas pipeline at Owode in Ikenne, and there is no gas pipeline around Ijebu-Omu where these things are happening. It is coming from the upper crust. It is a natural occurrence, and what triggers it will be established,” Oresanya stated. He also ruled out any immediate plan to relocate residents of the affected communities, noting that the government was consulting global practices and examining appropriate public health management measures. Meanwhile, Professor Philip Ikhiane, a Professor of Sedimentary Petroleum Geochemistry at Olabisi Onabanjo University (OOU), Ago-Iwoye, and leader of the Ogun State Technical Investigating Team, disclosed that preliminary geological investigations had identified underground structural features that could be linked to the gas emissions. Ikhiane explained that geological surveys and remote sensing operations had revealed subsurface lineaments, which could represent faults, fractures or joints beneath the affected areas. According to him, these geological structures could provide pathways through which naturally occurring gases migrate from underground formations to the surface. He said further investigations would be required to establish the relationship between the identified geological features and the reported emissions. The latest intervention comes amid growing concerns following repeated incidents in which more than 100 students from secondary schools in Ijebu-Ode, Ago-Iwoye and Ijebu-Igbo were reportedly hospitalised after inhaling an offensive gaseous substance. The affected students were taken to the State Hospital, Ijebu-Ode, General Hospital, Ijebu-Igbo, and other healthcare facilities for medical attention. Among the schools reportedly worst affected are Ijebu-Igbo Girls Grammar School, Anglican Girls Grammar School, Ijebu-Ode, and Itamerin Comprehensive High School, Ago-Iwoye. A video circulating on social media showed some students collapsing and being rushed to hospitals following the suspected exposure. The Ogun State Government had earlier identified the substance as methane, although the Federal Government’s latest investigation is expected to establish the precise source, composition and geological pathway of the emissions. A teacher in one of the affected schools, who spoke on condition of anonymity, described the incident as frightening, saying students and members of staff suddenly developed breathing difficulties. “The incident happened at about 10 am. The students and the staff started inhaling this gas and began to have difficulty in breathing and were fainting, after which they were rushed to the hospitals,” the teacher said. The first reported incident occurred in April, affecting about 40 students. In May, more than 120 students were reportedly hospitalised following another exposure, while a further 69 students were taken to hospitals on June 1 after another occurrence. The recurring incidents have raised concerns about the safety of students and staff in the affected schools, as well as the possible long-term environmental and public health implications for surrounding communities. With the deployment of the NUPRC technical team, residents and other stakeholders are expecting a comprehensive investigation that will identify the source of the emissions, establish appropriate safety measures and prevent further exposure, particularly in schools.
