联邦政府已派遣一支专业技术团队前往奥贡州，调查该州伊杰布地区反复出现的地下气体排放事件。这些事件引发健康担忧，并导致当地中学的教学活动中断。此次行动由尼日利亚上游石油监管委员会（NUPRC）协调，旨在查明气体排放的地质来源，并提出持久解决方案，以应对影响学校及周边社区的反复事件。

此次部署源于多起局部气体渗漏报告。有关方面怀疑，这些气体渗漏导致受影响社区的学生及其他居民出现缺氧和呼吸困难。联邦政府特设委员会星期六在伊杰布奥德举行联合新闻简报会并启动现场评估时表示，初步迹象显示，气体排放可能与地下自然地质过程有关，而非石油管道泄漏。不过，团队强调仍需进一步开展技术调查，以确定气体排放的实际来源和性质。

NUPRC助理司长兼团队负责人Prosper Okonedo在简报会上说，奥贡州政府完成初步评估后，委员会便组建了该委员会。Okonedo解释说，委员会首席执行官Oritsemeyawa Eyesan女士指示其拉各斯区域办事处派遣专家，与州政府合作调查此事。他说：“大约两周前，NUPRC委员会首席执行官Oritsemeyawa Eyesan女士建议我们从拉各斯区域办事处成立一个特设委员会，前来该州，因为州政府已经进行了初步评估并提交了报告。”他透露，委员会还在调查该国其他地区发生的类似事件，包括 Rivers州和Delta州的社区。

他说：“目前，我们有一个名为Epe Study Group的研究小组。他们正在调查Rivers州一个村庄社区的类似问题；Delta州目前也出现了类似情况，我们已确认那里的气体渗漏来自地下。不过，就奥贡州而言，我们目前确实无法判断具体情况。这就是我们来到这里的原因，我们将前往现场亲自了解情况，尽管州政府已报告说，一些社区的特定中学受到气体渗漏影响。”

Okonedo表示，联邦政府致力于与奥贡州政府合作处理此事，保障居民安全。他说：“政府的职责是确保尼日利亚人民的福祉和安康。如果这是政府的首要职责，那么我们委员会前来与州政府合作，就是为这个社区存在的任何问题提出解决方案。我的团队和我将开展评估，并形成一份有利于尼日利亚人民的报告。”

奥贡州环境专员Ola Oresanya先生也在会上发言，将反复出现的气体排放描述为一项新出现的环境挑战，需要国家级协调干预和技术专长。Oresanya说，Rivers州、Delta州和Osun州也报告过类似事件，表明问题可能不仅限于奥贡州的个别社区。

他说：“目前，Rivers州、Delta州、Osun州以及我们奥贡州都出现了类似问题。恰好在奥贡州，这些情况发生在学校周边。但我们必须确认，该地区发生的情况是否与我们在这里目睹的相同；这不只是一个局部问题。”

该专员呼吁居民在调查继续进行期间保持冷静，并保证州政府正与相关专家合作，确定气体排放的原因。他说：“我想说的只是，我们没有理由恐慌。我们需要做的只是保持关注，但请不要恐慌。我们所了解并带到会议上的情况是，影响我们民众的气体是地下气体。我们已经一次又一次地证实了这一点。

“Ikenne的Owode没有天然气管道，Ijebu-Omu这些事发地点周边也没有天然气管道。气体来自上部地壳。这是一种自然现象，至于触发因素，将予查明。”

他还排除了近期立即迁移受影响社区居民的计划，称政府正在参考全球实践，并研究适当的公共卫生管理措施。

与此同时，奥拉比西·奥纳班乔大学（OOU）Ago-Iwoye校区沉积石油地球化学教授、奥贡州技术调查团队负责人Philip Ikhiane教授透露，初步地质调查发现了一些可能与气体排放有关的地下构造特征。Ikhiane解释说，地质测绘和遥感作业揭示了地下线性构造，这些构造可能是受影响区域下方的断层、裂隙或节理。他说，这些地质构造可能为自然产生的气体从地下地层向地表迁移提供通道。进一步调查将用于确定已发现的地质特征与所报告气体排放之间的关系。

此次最新干预行动出台之际，公众对反复发生事件的担忧日益加剧。据报道，Ijebu-Ode、Ago-Iwoye和Ijebu-Igbo地区的中学已有超过100名学生因吸入刺鼻气体而住院。

受影响学生被送往Ijebu-Ode州医院、Ijebu-Igbo综合医院及其他医疗机构接受救治。据报道，受影响最严重的学校包括Ijebu-Igbo女子文法学校、Ijebu-Ode圣公会女子文法学校，以及Ago-Iwoye的Itamerin综合高中。社交媒体上传播的一段视频显示，一些学生疑似接触气体后倒下，并被紧急送往医院。

奥贡州政府此前已认定该物质为甲烷，但预计联邦政府最新调查将确定气体排放的确切来源、成分和地质通道。一名受影响学校的教师在匿名前提下 Describes the incident as frightening, saying students and members of staff suddenly developed breathing difficulties。该教师说：“事件大约发生在上午10点。学生和教职员工开始吸入这种气体，随后出现呼吸困难并昏厥，之后便被送往医院。”

首次报告的事件发生在4月，影响约40名学生。5月，据报道又有超过120名学生因再次接触气体而住院；6月1日另一次事件发生后，又有69名学生被送往医院。

反复发生的事件引发了人们对受影响学校学生和教职员工安全的担忧，也引发了对周边社区可能面临的长期环境和公共卫生影响的关注。随着NUPRC技术团队部署到位，居民及其他利益相关方期待开展全面调查，确定气体排放来源，制定适当安全措施，并防止进一步接触气体，尤其是在学校内。

https://www.myjoyonline.com/galamsey-wer.body: An Associate Professor at the University of Ghana School of Law, Prof Kwadwo Appiagyei-Tuah, has praised the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) for its role in mobilising gold to support the economy and stabilise the Cedi but warned that the gains are being undermined by the country’s continued struggle against illegal mining. He said Ghana appeared to be making progress on the economic front through gold mobilisation, but the environmental damage caused by galamsey remained a major concern. “We agree that GoldBod is doing well in getting the gold to support the economy and stabilise the Ghanaian cedi. It appears we are winning the financial war but are losing the environmental war,” he said. Prof Appiagyei-Tuah’s comments highlight the tension between the economic benefits of Ghana’s gold trade and the environmental consequences of illegal mining, particularly the pollution of water bodies and destruction of forest reserves. He had earlier acknowledged that some progress had been made in the fight against galamsey but questioned the evidence behind some of the figures being presented to support claims of success. “Definitely, some progress has been made, but there are some figures that have been thrown about without evidence,” he said. He added that although some available information suggested the government was making progress, other figures did not support that assessment, with data still indicating that illegal mining remained alarming. The comments were made on JoyNews’ Newsfile programme on Saturday, October 31, amid renewed public debate over the effectiveness of government interventions against illegal mining
https://www.myjoyonline.com/galamsey-wer.title_zh: 非法采矿：我们正在赢得经济战，却在环境战中失利
https://www.myjoyonline.com/galamsey-wer.body_zh: 加纳大学法学院副教授夸德沃·阿皮亚吉-图阿教授赞扬了加纳黄金局（GoldBod），称其在调动黄金以支持经济、稳定塞地方面发挥了积极作用，但警告称，该国持续打击非法采矿的斗争正削弱这些成果。他说，加纳似乎正通过调动黄金在经济方面取得进展，但非法采矿造成的环境破坏仍是重大关切。他说：“我们认同GoldBod在调动黄金、支持经济以及稳定加纳塞地方面表现良好。看来我们正在赢得经济战，却在环境战中失利。”阿皮亚吉-图阿教授的评论凸显了加纳黄金贸易带来的经济利益与非法采矿造成的环境后果之间的矛盾，尤其是水体污染和森林保护区遭破坏。他此前曾表示，打击非法采矿已经取得一些进展，但质疑了一些用于支持成功说法的数据背后的证据。他说：“毫无疑问，已经取得了一些进展，但有些数据是在没有证据的情况下随意抛出的。”他补充说，尽管现有部分信息显示政府正在取得进展，但其他数据并不支持这一评估，相关数据仍显示非法采矿形势依然令人担忧。这些评论是在10月31日星期六播出的JoyNews《新闻档案》节目中发表的，当时公众再次就政府打击非法采矿的干预措施是否有效展开讨论。

https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/2027.body: The National President of the Miyetti Allah Cattle Breeders Association of Nigeria (MACBAN), Baba Othman Ngelzarma, has declared support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027, citing the establishment of the Federal Ministry of Livestock Development as a major step towards addressing decades of neglect of the livestock sector. Ngelzarma said pastoralists, cattle breeders and other livestock stakeholders across the country were prepared to support Tinubu for a second term in appreciation of his administration’s recognition of the economic importance of the sector. He spoke at a rally organised in Kaduna by the Fulbe APC Forum and Tinubu Yeso-Yeso Political Forum (TYPF), in collaboration with the Coalition of Pastoralists and Traders Associations and the Amalgamated Union of Livestock Dealers, Butchers and other stakeholders. The rally, held under the theme, “United for Inclusion, Representation and Prosperity,” attracted Fulani organisations, pastoralists, cattle breeders, livestock dealers, butchers, processors and political stakeholders from different parts of the country. Ngelzarma said the creation of the livestock ministry in July 2024 had fulfilled a longstanding demand by pastoralists and livestock operators, who had campaigned for a dedicated government institution to address challenges in the industry for several decades. “We are here today to extend our appreciation and support to the administration of President Tinubu. “The creation of the livestock ministry is something we have been advocating for and looking forward to for decades,” he said. He noted that the initiative had also encouraged some state governments to establish similar institutions to coordinate livestock development, describing it as an opportunity to address longstanding challenges confronting pastoralists and other operators in the industry. The Minister of Livestock Development, Idi Mukhtar Maiha, urged pastoralists, livestock farmers and other stakeholders to take advantage of the ministry’s programmes to improve productivity, expand their businesses and enhance their livelihoods. Maiha identified inadequate veterinary services, limited access to pasture and water, high feed costs, poor market infrastructure and low productivity as some of the factors that had hindered the growth of Nigeria’s livestock industry over the years. He said Nigeria had an estimated 58 million cattle, 124 million goats, 70 million sheep, 9.3 million pigs, 3.2 million donkeys, 700,000 camels and 300 million birds, describing the figures as enormous economic opportunities that could be harnessed through deliberate investments and improved management. The minister disclosed that seven veterinary hospitals had been completed and equipped under a World Bank-supported programme, while additional facilities were at various stages of completion. He said the Federal Government planned to expand veterinary services across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory, with primary veterinary facilities also envisaged for the 774 local government areas. Maiha challenged livestock associations to work with the ministry and state governments within three months to identify the challenges confronting their members and develop practical proposals for investment and improved service delivery. He said the government was also working to strengthen Nigeria’s participation in regional and international livestock trade through improved animal health standards, traceability systems and market infrastructure. On the recurring tensions between farmers and pastoralists, the minister stressed the need for peaceful coexistence, dialogue and responsible management of land and water resources, noting that sustainable livestock development depended on harmonious relationships between farming and pastoral communities. He also urged young Nigerians to embrace livestock production as a viable business capable of generating employment and wealth, rather than viewing it merely as a traditional occupation. In his remarks, Kaduna State Governor Uba Sani, represented by the Commissioner for Agriculture, Murtala Dabo, said the state government was complementing the Federal Government’s initiative through investments in livestock infrastructure and services. Dabo disclosed that Kaduna State’s budgetary allocation to livestock development had increased from N1.48 billion in 2023 to more than N100 billion in 2026. He said the state government had provided solar-powered water facilities in pastoralist communities, expanded livestock vaccination programmes and introduced artificial insemination services to improve animal productivity. According to him, improved feeding and breeding practices had increased milk production among some cattle from about 1.5 litres to between three and four litres. He added that the government was also upgrading slaughter facilities and improving infrastructure across the livestock value chain to boost production, processing and marketing. https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/2027.title_zh: 2027年：米耶蒂·阿拉支持蒂努布连任，并提及牲畜部
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/2027.body_zh: 尼日利亚米耶蒂阿拉牛育种者协会（MACBAN）全国主席Baba Othman Ngelzarma宣布支持总统Bola Tinubu竞选连任，表示联邦政府设立畜牧业发展部，是解决该行业数十年来遭忽视问题的重要一步。Ngelzarma表示，为感谢 Tinubu政府认可畜牧业的经济重要性，全国各地的牧民、牛育种者及其他畜牧业利益相关方都准备支持 Tinubu争取第二任期。他是在 Kaduna由Fulbe APC Forum和Tinubu Yeso-Yeso Political Forum（TYPF）联合牧民及贸易商协会联盟、牲畜经销商、屠宰商及其他利益相关方举办的一场集会上发表上述言论的。大会以“团结实现包容、代表与繁荣”为主题，吸引了来自全国各地的富拉尼组织、牧民、牛育种者、牲畜经销商、屠宰商、加工商和政治利益相关方。Ngelzarma表示，2024年7月设立畜牧业部实现了牧民和畜牧业经营者长期以来的诉求；数十年来，他们一直呼吁设立专门的政府机构，以应对该行业面临的挑战。“我们今天齐聚于此，向 Tinubar总统政府表达感谢和支持。设立畜牧业部是我们倡导并期待了数十年的事情，”他说。他指出，这项举措还促使一些州政府设立类似机构，以协调畜牧业发展，并称这是解决牧民和该行业其他经营者长期面临挑战的机会。畜牧业发展部长Idi Mukhtar Maiha敦促牧民、畜牧农场主及其他利益相关方利用该部的各项计划，提高生产率、扩大业务并改善生计。Maiha列举了阻碍尼日利亚畜牧业多年来发展的若干因素，包括兽医服务不足、牧场和水源获取受限、饲料成本高、市场基础设施落后以及生产率低下。他说，尼日利亚估计拥有5,800万头牛、1.24亿只山羊、7,000万只绵羊、930万头猪、320万头驴、70万头骆驼和3亿只家禽；这些数字蕴含巨大的经济机会，可通过有针对性的投资和改善管理加以利用。部长透露，在世界银行支持的项目下，已有7家兽医院建成并配备设备，另有更多设施正处于不同的建设阶段。他说，联邦政府计划在36个州和联邦首都辖区扩大兽医服务覆盖范围，并计划在774个地方政府辖区设立初级兽医机构。Maiha要求各畜牧业协会在三个月内与该部及州政府合作，找出成员面临的挑战，并制定促进投资和改善服务交付的切实方案。他说，政府还在通过提升动物健康标准、完善可追溯性系统和加强市场基础设施，加强尼日利亚参与区域和国际畜牧业贸易的能力。谈及农民与牧民之间反复出现的紧张关系时，部长强调各方需要和平共处、对话，并负责任地管理土地和水资源，同时指出，可持续的畜牧业发展有赖于农业社区与牧民社区之间保持和谐关系。他还敦促尼日利亚年轻人把畜牧生产视为一种能够创造就业和财富的可行商业模式，而不要仅仅将其视为传统职业。在讲话中，由农业委员Murtala Dabo代表出席的Kaduna州州长Uba Sani表示，州政府正通过投资畜牧业基础设施和服务，配合联邦政府的举措。Dabo透露，Kaduna州用于畜牧业发展的预算拨款已从2023年的14.8亿奈拉增至2026年的逾1,000亿奈拉。他说，州政府已在牧民社区提供太阳能供水设施，扩大牲畜疫苗接种项目，并引入人工授精服务，以提高动物生产率。据他介绍，改进饲养和繁育做法后，部分奶牛的产奶量已从约1.5升增加到3至4升。他补充说，政府还在升级屠宰设施，并改善整个畜牧业价值链的基础设施，以促进生产、加工和营销。此处发表的意见不代表Vanguard报纸或其任何员工的观点

Unlock these with Subscription Aimed at strengthening Delhi’s firefighting and emergency rescue services, Chief Minister Rekha Gupta has approved the creation of 2,345 additional posts across various categories in the Delhi Fire Services (DFS), the CM’s Office (CMO) said on Saturday. The Chief Minister said it was essential to strengthen the fire service in line with the city’s growing needs to ensure the safety of Delhi’s residents and save lives. Under the restructuring, the number of posts will be increased across various ranks and categories, including Deputy Chief Fire Officer, Divisional Officer, Assistant Divisional Officer, Station Officer, Sub-Officer, Leading Fireman, Fire Operator, Peon and Gardener, as per the CMO. “This will increase the availability of personnel at every level, from senior supervisory positions to frontline staff engaged in firefighting and rescue operations. It will also help streamline the department’s organisational structure, ensure better discharge of responsibilities at different levels and improve its efficiency during emergencies,” the CMO said in a statement. The Chief Minister said that Delhi’s rapidly growing population, expanding urban areas, densely populated settlements, high-rise buildings, industrial establishments and complex infrastructure were creating new challenges for firefighting and emergency services. “Every minute matters in the event of a fire or any other disaster. Adequately trained manpower, a strong leadership structure and the ability to respond quickly play a decisive role in protecting people and their property,” she said. At a seminar titled "Vietnam-China Businesses: Connecting Manufacturing, Logistics, and Global Value Chains" on Oct. 29, speakers called for closer economic integration beyond traditional trade. The event was part of the 2026 Autumn Economic Forum in Ho Chi Minh City. Xu Shou, acting consul general of China in HCMC, said the two economies had complementary industrial structures and supply chains. "Cooperation between Chinese and Vietnamese businesses has moved beyond traditional trade in goods into a new phase of supply chain coordination, technology exchange, and knowledge sharing," he said. Chinese companies have experience in smart manufacturing, modern logistics and innovation and are ready to deepen cooperation with Vietnamese partners, Xu said. He called for stronger links between suppliers and downstream businesses, as well as collaboration in technology transfer, process management, quality control and workforce training. China is Vietnam's largest trading partner, with bilateral trade exceeding US$256 billion in 2025. Trade reached more than $253 billion in the first nine months of 2026, up 37.6% year-on-year. During the same period, investors from China, including Hong Kong, received licenses for 1,104 new projects in Vietnam, with registered capital of $4.5 billion, up 31.35%. China ranked fourth among Vietnam's investment partners, with manufacturing accounting for about 80.61% of registered capital. Yang Wen Bin, acting chairman of the HCMC Chapter of the Chinese Business Association in Vietnam, said the figures reflected Vietnam's investment appeal and the potential for greater cooperation in manufacturing, logistics and supply chains. Yang Wen Bin, Acting Chairman of the HCMC Chapter of the Chinese Business Association in Vietnam, speaks at the 2026 Autumn Economic Forum in HCMC on Oct. 29, 2026. Photo courtesy of AEF 2026 Yang urged businesses to expand cooperation in advanced manufacturing, electronics, information technology, green energy and supporting industries, alongside technology exchanges, workforce training and investment partnerships. He said deeper integration could help Vietnamese businesses participate more extensively in regional and global production networks. Jesse Choi, CEO of Sunwah Group in Southeast Asia and Sunwah Innovations, and chairman of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area Entrepreneurs Alliance in Vietnam, said closer manufacturing and supply chain ties could support cooperation in technology, logistics, finance and human resource development. Sunwah established Sunwah Innovations in 2020. Its innovation spaces in HCMC, Hanoi and Da Nang connect businesses, startups, universities and investors with partners in China and other markets. Through exchange programs, business networking and technology partnerships, the initiative helps commercialize research, connect technology solutions with domestic demand and give Vietnamese businesses access to international opportunities, Choi said. Speakers also called for stronger road, waterway and railway connections, smart border gates, digital supply chains, information sharing and harmonized technical standards. Xu urged both countries to pursue joint ventures in areas including urban railways, innovative trade platforms and cross-border finance to deepen their participation in global value chains. At a meeting with a delegation from the Research Office of China's State Council on Oct. 27, Vietnamese Deputy Minister of Finance Nguyen Thi Bich Ngoc outlined five pillars for bilateral cooperation. She called for stronger manufacturing supply chain links, technology cooperation and research and development, as well as strategic infrastructure development, particularly the Lao Cai-Hanoi-Hai Phong railway. Ngoc also proposed closer logistics links, smart border gates and customs cooperation to reduce trade costs, and encouraged Chinese financial institutions to participate in Vietnam's international financial center

官员和商界领袖表示，越南和中国应扩大制造业、技术和物流领域的合作，以加强两国在全球供应链中的作用。10月29日，在一场题为“越南—中国企业：连接制造业、物流与全球价值链”的研讨会上，与会者呼吁加强超越传统贸易的经济融合。此次活动是胡志明市2026年秋季经济论坛的一部分。
中国驻胡志明市总领事徐守说，中越两国的产业结构具有互补性，供应链也相互配套。
他说：“中越企业之间的合作已经超越传统货物贸易，进入供应链协调、技术交流和知识共享的新阶段。”
徐表示，中国企业在智能制造、现代物流和创新方面拥有经验，并准备与越南伙伴深化合作。他呼吁加强供应商与下游企业之间的联系，同时推动技术转让、工艺管理、质量控制和劳动力培训等领域的协作。
中国是越南最大的贸易伙伴，2025年双边贸易额超过2560亿美元。2026年前9个月，双边贸易额超过2530亿美元，同比增长37.6%。
同期，包括来自香港的中国投资者获得了越南1104个新项目的许可，注册资本为45亿美元，同比增长31.35%。中国在越南投资伙伴中排名第四，制造业约占注册资本的80.61%。
在越南中国商会胡志明市分会代理主席杨文彬表示，这些数字反映了越南对投资的吸引力，以及双方在制造业、物流和供应链领域扩大合作的潜力。杨文彬在2026年秋季经济论坛上讲话。2026年10月29日于胡志明市举行。图片由AEF 2026提供。
杨呼吁企业在先进制造、电子、信息科技、绿色能源和配套产业扩大合作，同时加强技术交流、劳动力培训和投资伙伴关系。他说，更深入的融合能够帮助越南企业更广泛地参与区域和全球生产网络。
Sunwah Group东南亚及Sunwah Innovations首席执行官、粤港澳大湾区企业家联盟越南主席Jesse Choi表示，加强制造业和供应链联系可以支持技术、物流、金融和人力资源开发等领域的合作。
Sunwah于2020年成立Sunwah Innovations。该公司在胡志明市、河内和岘港的创新空间将企业、初创公司、大学和投资者与中国及其他市场的伙伴连接起来。Choi表示，通过交流项目、商业 networking 和技术伙伴关系，该计划帮助研究成果实现商业化，将技术解决方案与国内需求对接，并让越南企业获得国际机会。
与会的发言者还呼吁加强公路、水路和铁路连接，建设智慧口岸，推进数字供应链、信息共享和技术标准协调统一。
徐敦促两国在城际铁路、创新贸易平台和跨境金融等领域开展合资合作，以深化参与全球价值链。
10月27日，在与中国国务院研究室代表团举行会谈时，越南财政部副部长阮氏碧玉提出了双边合作的五大支柱。她呼吁加强制造业供应链联系、技术合作与研发，以及战略基础设施建设，尤其是老街—河内—海阳铁路。
阮氏碧玉还提议加强物流联系、智慧口岸建设和海关合作，以降低贸易成本，并鼓励中国金融机构参与越南国际金融中心

https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.body: Caring Africa has urged the federal and state governments to begin implementing Nigeria’s newly approved National Care Policy and Implementation Plan, 2026-2030. The organisation, which served as a technical partner to the Federal Ministry of Women Affairs and Social Development in developing the policy, said its approval is only the beginning of efforts to establish a national system for childcare, elderly care and other forms of paid and unpaid care. The Federal Executive Council, presided over by President Bola Tinubu, approved the policy on Wednesday alongside the National Action Plan on Ending Violence Against Children and the National Policy on Menstrual Health and Hygiene Management, 2026-2030. The Minister of Women Affairs and Social Development, Imaan Sulaiman-Ibrahim, announced the approvals at a press briefing in Abuja on Thursday to mark the 26th anniversary of United Nations Security Council Resolution 1325 on Women, Peace and Security. According to the ministry, the National Care Policy recognises unpaid care work, promotes regulated childcare and elderly care services, sets minimum standards for care centres and provides for a National Care Fund. Blessing Adesiyan, founder and Chief Care Officer of Caring Africa, said the next stage should be to domesticate the policy across Nigeria. Ms Adesiyan said care services such as health, education and social welfare are delivered substantially at state level, making adoption of the policy by the 36 states important to its implementation. “A federal policy that stays in Abuja will not change anything for a woman looking for childcare in Oshodi or caring for her mother in Sokoto,” she said. Ms Adesiyan called for the policy to be taken across the six geopolitical zones and adopted by the states. Nigeria joins countries that have adopted national care policies. Brazil enacted its National Care Policy in 2024, followed by a funded national plan, while Chile signed its Chile Cuida care system into law in 2026. Kenya has also launched a national care policy and is implementing it at county level, while UN Women supports more than 50 countries in developing national care systems. The policy is built around 11 pillars covering unpaid care work, care infrastructure, maternal and newborn care, childcare, ageing and elderly care, disability care, the care workforce, regulation of the care economy, care financing and employer-supported care. Under the childcare component, the framework provides for a tiered licensing system for childcare facilities, minimum standards on space, staff ratios, safety, hygiene and nutrition, as well as a national register for childcare workers. It also proposes a pathway for informal crèches to meet regulatory requirements rather than simply being excluded from the system. For care workers, the policy proposes defining care work as a formal occupation under Nigerian labour law, with training and certification pathways and a national caregiver database. It also proposes a minimum wage floor for care workers, health insurance and pension access. The framework also proposes a dedicated care line in the federal budget and a National Care Fund to pool public, corporate and development financing for care services. Caring Africa cited data showing that women and girls perform about 80 per cent of unpaid care work in Nigeria, including childcare, cooking, cleaning and caring for sick or elderly relatives. The organisation also cited estimates that Nigerian women spend about 4.3 hours a day on unpaid care work, compared with 1.12 hours for men. It said only about five per cent of Nigerian children aged zero to two are enrolled in licensed childcare. The National Bureau of Statistics estimates that formalising the care economy could create 17 million jobs, while research by Economist Impact indicates that accessible and quality childcare could enable 1.7 million more Nigerian mothers to enter the workforce by 2030. Ms Adesiyan said the policy would also provide a framework for employers to support workers with caregiving responsibilities through measures such as paid leave and employer-supported care. She said the policy’s provisions on maternal and newborn care would extend support into the postpartum period, while its broader framework covers ageing, disability and care within households. “The stress of sustained caregiving carries a real physical health cost, which we rarely count. This policy is the first instrument we have that touches it,” she noted
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.title_zh: 921762人关爱非洲，敦促在全国落实国家关怀政策
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.body_zh: Caring Africa敦促联邦政府和州政府开始落实尼日利亚新近获批的《国家照护政策及实施计划（2026—2030年）》。该组织曾担任联邦妇女事务和社会发展部制定该政策的技术合作伙伴，并表示，政策获批只是建立全国儿童照护、老年照护以及其他有偿和无偿照护体系的开端。由总统Bola Tinubu主持的联邦执行委员会于周三批准了该政策，同时批准的还有《终结针对儿童暴力国家行动计划》和《月经健康与卫生管理国家政策（2026—2030年）》。妇女事务和社会发展部长Imaan Sulaiman-Ibrahim周四在阿布贾举行的新闻发布会上宣布了这些批准事项，以纪念联合国安理会第1325号《关于妇女、和平与安全》决议通过26周年。该部表示，《国家照护政策》承认无偿照护劳动，推动规范化的儿童照护和老年照护服务，规定照护中心的最低标准，并设立国家照护基金。Caring Africa创始人兼首席照护官Blessing Adesiyan表示，下一阶段应是在尼日利亚各地落实该政策。Adesiyan女士说，医疗、教育和社会福利等照护服务主要由州一级政府提供，因此让36个州采纳该政策对落实而言至关重要。她说：“一项停留在阿布贾的联邦政策，对于在Oshodi寻找儿童照护服务或在家照顾索科托母亲的女性而言，不会带来任何改变。”Adesiyan女士呼吁将该政策推广至全国六个地缘政治区域，并由各州采纳。尼日利亚由此加入已采纳国家照护政策的国家行列。巴西于2024年实施其《国家照护政策》，随后出台了一项有资金支持的国家计划；智利则在2026年将Chile Cuida照护体系签署为法律。肯尼亚也已启动国家照护政策，并在郡一级予以实施；联合国妇女署则支持50多个国家制定国家照护体系。该政策围绕11项支柱构建，涵盖无偿照护劳动、照护基础设施、孕产妇和新生儿照护、儿童照护、老龄化和老年照护、残障人士照护、照护劳动力、照护经济监管、照护融资以及雇主支持的照护。在儿童照护部分，该框架规定对儿童照护机构实行分级许可制度，确立空间、人员配置比例、安全、卫生和营养等方面的最低标准，并建立全国照护工作者登记表。政策还为非正式托儿点满足监管要求提供路径，而不是将其直接排除在体系之外。在照护工作者方面，政策提议依据尼日利亚劳动法将照护工作界定为正式职业，建立培训和认证路径，并设立全国照护人员数据库。政策还提议为照护工作者设定最低工资底线，并提供医疗保险和养老金保障。框架还建议在联邦预算中设立专门的照护支出项目，并设立国家照护基金，集中公共、企业和发展融资，用于照护服务。Caring Africa援引数据称，在尼日利亚，女性和女童承担约80%的无偿照护劳动，包括照看孩子、做饭、清洁以及照顾患病或年迈亲属。该组织还援引估算称，尼日利亚女性每天花费约4.3小时从事无偿照护劳动，而男性仅为1.12小时。尼日利亚仅约5%的0至2岁儿童登记在持牌儿童照护机构中。尼日利亚国家统计局估计，将照护经济正规化可创造1700万个就业岗位；Economist Impact的研究则表明，到2030年，便捷且高质量的儿童照护可让另外170万名尼日利亚母亲进入劳动力市场。Adesiyan女士表示，该政策还将为雇主支持承担照护责任的员工提供框架，包括带薪休假和雇主支持的照护等措施。她说，政策关于孕产妇和新生儿照护的规定将把支持延伸至产后阶段，而其更广泛的框架还涵盖老龄化、残障人士照护以及家庭内部照护。她指出：“持续承担照护责任的压力会对身体健康造成真实代价，而我们很少计算这些代价。这项政策是我们第一份真正触及这一问题的工具。”

Unlock these with Subscription Crude oil procurement remained volatile during the September quarter, with Indian Oil Corporation (IOC) sourcing supplies at discounts of up to $5 per barrel and premiums of as much as $12, Anuj Jain, Director (Finance), told investors during a post-results call on Saturday. The Delhi-headquartered refiner’s net profit more than doubled year-on-year to ₹21,630 crore in the second quarter, supported by improved refining margins and a brief decline in benchmark crude oil prices. Mr. Jain said LPG under-recoveries stood at ₹184 per cylinder in September before rising to ₹229 in October. These are projected to increase further to ₹309 in November and ₹370 in December. Explaining the volatility in procurement costs, he said crude purchases during the quarter ranged from a discount of $5 per barrel to a premium of $12 against prevailing benchmark prices. In the first quarter, the range was from zero discount or premium to a premium of $18 per barrel. Effective procurement prices depend on several factors, including whether supplies are contracted on a free-on-board (FOB) or delivered-at-place (DAP) basis, freight costs and the grade of crude. Russian crude accounted for around 55% of IOC’s crude basket during the first half of the fiscal, followed by supplies from the Middle East, primarily Saudi Arabia and Dubai, at 24%. Africa, including Angola and Nigeria, contributed about 10%, while Brazil accounted for 7%. Supplies from the U.S. and Venezuela made up the remaining 2-5% and 3-4%, respectively. Around 87% of the company’s crude procurement during the period came through spot sourcing. Mr. Jain said. Responding to a question on whether spot purchases entailed higher costs, he said such sourcing did not necessarily mean paying a premium, as prices varied across region/geography. “Now, within spot you have Russian crude. Sometimes, we are getting a high discount, sometimes we are paying a premium as well,” Mr. Jain said. “In the few months, we have seen huge, discounted crude coming in from Iraq. So, the moment it is available, we are buying huge quantities from Iraq also. That used to be our staple diet before the [West Asia] crisis as well.” He added that procurement economics were also influenced by effective negotiations, which played an important role in determining the final price. https://www.thehindu.com/business/econom.body_zh: 订阅可享受高级新闻、社论、观点等更多内容。解锁这些内容需订阅。9月季度，原油采购成本持续波动。Indian Oil Corporation（IOC）以每桶最高折价5美元、最高溢价12美元的价格采购原油。财务总监Anuj Jain周六在业绩公布后的电话会上告诉投资者，这家总部位于德里的炼油企业受益于炼油利润率改善以及基准原油价格短暂下跌，第二财季净利润同比翻了一番以上，达到₹21,630 crore。Jain先生表示，液化石油气的未回收成本9月为每瓶₹184，10月升至每瓶₹229，预计11月将进一步升至每瓶₹309，12月升至每瓶₹370。他解释采购成本的波动时说，该季度原油采购价格相对于当时的基准价格介于每桶折价5美元至溢价12美元之间。第一季度的价格区间为无折价或溢价至每桶溢价18美元。实际采购价格取决于多个因素，包括供应合同采用船上交货（FOB）还是指定地点交货（DAP）条款、运费以及原油品级。在本财年上半年，IOC原油采购组合中，俄罗斯原油约占55%，随后是来自中东的原油，主要为沙特阿拉伯和Dubai原油，占24%。包括安哥拉和尼日利亚在内的非洲占约10%，巴西占7%。来自美国和委内瑞拉的供应分别占其余份额中的2%至5%和3%至4%。Jain先生表示，该期间公司约87%的原油采购通过现货渠道完成。在回答现货采购是否意味着成本更高的问题时，他说，这种采购方式并不一定意味着支付溢价，因为各地区的价格有所不同。Jain先生说：“如今，现货原油中有俄罗斯原油。有时我们能获得较高折价，有时也会支付溢价。在最近几个月里，我们看到大量打折原油从伊拉克运来。因此，一旦有货，我们也会从伊拉克大量采购。在[西亚]危机之前，这一直都是我们的主要原料来源。”他还表示，采购经济性也受到有效谈判的影响，而谈判在确定最终价格方面发挥着重要作用。评论必须使用英文，并以完整句子表述。评论不得包含辱骂性或针对个人的内容。发布评论时请遵守我们的社区准则。我们已迁移至新的评论平台。如果你已经是The Hindu的注册用户并已登录，可以继续参与我们的文章讨论。如果你没有账户，请注册并登录后发表评论。用户登录自己的账户后，可以在Vuukle查看过去的评论

https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/business/co.body: WASHINGTON — Korean Ambassador to the United States Kang Kyung-wha has pledged to strengthen cooperation with U.S. authorities to support bilateral investment, describing Hyundai Motor Group's latest investment in Alabama as an example of the expanding economic partnership between the two countries. Kang made the remarks Wednesday while attending a ceremony announcing Hyundai Motor Manufacturing Alabama's plan to invest about $450 million in its Montgomery plant, according to the Korean Embassy in Washington. The ambassador highlighted Hyundai's presence in the U.S. as an "outstanding example" of how the Korea-U.S. alliance has evolved over more than seven decades, expanding beyond its security foundations into cooperation in economic security and advanced technology. Kang also said the investment would combine Korea's advanced manufacturing capabilities with America's innovation and market competitiveness, allowing the two countries to "shape the future of the automotive industry together," according to the embassy. https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.body: WASHINGTON — Hanwha Defense USA (HDUSA), a subsidiary of South Korea's Hanwha Aerospace Co., has secured a $269 million contract to build a medium landing ship (LSM) for the U.S. Navy and Marine Corps, marking its first U.S. Navy shipbuilding contract, according to the company. The company said Thursday it was selected by U.S. maritime services firm Tote Services to build one LSM at Hanwha Philly Shipyard in Philadelphia, with options to construct three additional vessels. The selection was made through a competitive bidding process under Tote Services' vessel construction management program, which oversees shipbuilding contracts for the U.S. Navy and Marine Corps. "Since acquiring Philly Shipyard in 2024, Hanwha has made significant investments in its workforce and technology to pave the way to build ships for the U.S. Navy and other federal customers," HDUSA President and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Michael Coulter said. Construction is scheduled to begin in the fourth quarter of 2027. Tote Services' $2.2 billion vessel construction manager contract supports the Navy and Marine Corps' planned 35-ship LSM fleet. The program's first vessel is expected to be delivered in 2030. The announcement comes as HDUSA is moving to acquire a controlling stake in Hanwha Philly Shipyard, which Hanwha purchased in 2024, as the South Korean defense group seeks to expand its presence in the U.S. shipbuilding industry

https://www.premiumtimesng.com/opinion/9.summary: Following Federal Executive Council approval, the Federal Government announced in May 2026 plans to establish the National Research and Innovation Development Fund (NRIDF), with an annual funding target of up to $500 million, approximately ₦673 billion at the current official exchange rate. https://www.premiumtimesng.com/opinion/9.summary_zh: 联邦执行委员会批准后，联邦政府于2026年5月宣布计划设立国家研究与创新发展基金（NRIDF），年度资金目标最高为5亿美元，按当前官方汇率约合₦6730亿。然而，政府所承诺的事项与政府实际承诺拨付的资金之间仍有差距。
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/opinion/9.body: In March, I visited the University of Michigan in Ann Arbor, where my daughter is currently a pre-med student. The university, often described as one of America’s Public Ivies because of its academic reputation and standing among leading public universities, has Professor Omolade Adunbi, a Nigerian on its faculty as its Director of the African Studies Center. I have maintained a relationship with Professor Adunbi for nearly two decades, and he joined my daughter in welcoming me to campus. During our conversation, I asked him about innovative ways American universities finance their programmes and what Nigeria and other African economies could learn. He introduced me to what I would call the Michigan template. One of the things he drew my attention to include the commercial value of university research as a source of funding. The University of Michigan has an extensive research-commercialisation ecosystem, connecting faculty research with corporations, foundations, investors and entrepreneurs through its innovation partnerships office. At Michigan, research output creates opportunities for corporations to sponsor research, enter partnerships with academics, license intellectual property and commercialise discoveries. Professor Adunbi mentioned Google co-founder Larry Page as an illustration of the relationship between university education, research and entrepreneurship. Page graduated from Michigan before proceeding to Stanford, where he and Sergey Brin developed PageRank, the technology that became foundational to Google. The research that produced Google was conducted at Stanford, but the example illustrates the wider value of university education and innovation. As Nigeria continues to approve licences for more universities, the value of these institutions must extend beyond the degrees they award. It should also be measured by their capacity to produce people, ideas and discoveries that create economic value. In fiscal year 2025, Michigan recorded $2.16 billion in research expenditures, attracted $170.6 million in corporate-sponsored research awards and supported the creation of 31 startups. Its experience demonstrates what becomes possible when academic research, government investment and private-sector participation reinforce one another. For Nigeria, this raises a fundamental policy question, which is my burning question for this edition. Why should Nigerian universities remain so heavily dependent on government allocations and tuition when their research capabilities could also attract corporate investment, generate intellectual property and support new businesses? This requires more than asking companies to fund universities. It requires institutions capable of producing credible research, protecting intellectual property and negotiating commercial partnerships. In connection, On 10 October, the London-based global charity, Wellcome, published a report that draws on interviews with more than 140,000 people across 140 countries. Its findings show that public trust in science has declined globally since the COVID-19 pandemic and fallen below its 2018 level. Nigeria’s experience reflects this worrying trend. In 2018, 26 per cent of Nigerians said they trusted science a lot. By 2020, that figure had fallen to 13 per cent. It recovered modestly to 15 per cent in 2025. Although the recovery is welcome, Nigeria remains 11 percentage points below its pre-pandemic level. Overall, 57 per cent of Nigerians reported at least some trust in science. The survey’s findings on vaccination make the challenge more concrete. Asked whether they would take a vaccine recommended by a doctor or nurse, 35 per cent of Nigerian respondents said they would take it immediately. Another 36 per cent preferred time to think about it, while 24 per cent said they did not take vaccines at all. Someone who wants time to consider a vaccine is not necessarily opposed to vaccination. Such concerns should not automatically be dismissed as ignorance. The more important question is whether people can obtain clear, credible answers that allow them to make informed decisions. The pandemic provides an important context. Scientific recommendations sometimes change because the evidence has changed. That is not a weakness of science; it is how science works. But when authorities communicate uncertainty poorly, subsequent changes can be interpreted as evidence of incompetence or dishonesty. Nigeria must nevertheless resist the temptation to explain its figures entirely through COVID-19. For many Nigerians, the most immediate encounter with science is not a laboratory or research institution, but a hospital, clinic, pharmacy or conversation with a health professional. As it is, the Wellcome report identifies an important relationship between confidence in healthcare institutions and trust in science. Globally, 43 per cent of people expressing a lot of confidence in their country’s hospitals and clinics also reported a lot of trust in science, compared with 26 per cent across the survey population. Economic insecurity adds another dimension. Globally, 39 per cent of people living comfortably reported a lot of trust in science in 2025, compared with 20 per cent of those finding it difficult to get by financially. Families preoccupied with food, rent, school fees and medical bills may have fewer resources to seek reliable information or act on professional advice. When institutions appear disconnected from those struggles, their pronouncements may carry less weight. To be fair, the Nigerian government has announced an initiative that could address some of these challenges. Following Federal Executive Council approval, the Federal Government announced in May 2026 plans to establish the National Research and Innovation Development Fund (NRIDF), with an annual funding target of up to $500 million, approximately ₦673 billion at the current official exchange rate. The fund is intended to support competitive research grants, strengthen innovation infrastructure and commercialise research findings. However, there is a difference between what a government promises and what it commits to funding. The $500 million figure was announced as an estimated annual target. On October 8, the Minister of Innovation, Science and Technology, Kingsley Udeh, clarified that the exact amount could not yet be determined because the proposed funding mechanism would draw on different sources calculated as percentages on a year-by-year basis. He also confirmed that the enabling bill had been forwarded to the National Assembly. In other words, the government has secured executive approval for the initiative, but the legislative and funding arrangements are not yet fully established. An announcement is not an appropriation, and an appropriation is not necessarily a disbursement. The government must therefore demonstrate that the fund will be backed by a sustainable revenue framework, independently governed, transparently administered and accessible to credible researchers. I have not found a specific public response from the Nigerian government to the Wellcome report since its 10 October publication. But to turn discoveries into commercially viable solutions, Nigeria needs research that addresses local priorities and stronger university-industry partnerships
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/opinion/9.title_zh: 政府资金为何无法独自解决尼日利亚的教育危机，作者：Adeola Akinremi
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/opinion/9.body_zh: 3月，我到访了位于安娜堡的密歇根大学，我的女儿目前在那里攻读医学预科。该大学凭借其学术声誉以及在顶尖公立大学中的地位，常常被称为美国“公立常春藤”之一；尼日利亚人教授Omolade Adunbi在该校任教，担任非洲研究中心主任。我与Adunbi教授保持联系已近20年，这次他与我的女儿一同欢迎我来到校园。交谈中，我询问他美国大学为各项计划提供资金的方式有哪些创新，以及尼日利亚和其他非洲经济体可以从中汲取哪些经验。他向我介绍了我会称之为“密歇根模式”的做法。他提请我关注的事项之一，是大学研究的商业价值可作为资金来源。密歇根大学拥有完善的研究成果商业化生态系统，通过其创新合作办公室将教师研究与企业、基金会、投资者和创业者连接起来。在密歇根大学，研究成果为企业赞助研究、与学术界建立合作、获得知识产权许可以及将研究发现商业化创造了机会。Adunbi教授以Google联合创始人Larry Page为例，说明大学教育、研究与创业之间的关系。Page从密歇根大学毕业后前往Stanford，在那里他与Sergey Brin开发了PageRank，这项技术后来成为Google的基础。催生Google的研究是在Stanford开展的，但这个例子说明了大学教育与创新的更广泛价值。随着尼日利亚继续批准增设大学，这些机构的价值不能仅限于它们颁发的学位，还应当衡量它们能否培养人才、产生思想并作出能够创造经济价值的发现。2025财年，密歇根大学录得$2.16 billion研究支出，吸引了$170.6 million企业赞助研究奖励，并支持成立了31家初创企业。其经验表明，当学术研究、政府投资和私营部门参与彼此促进时，便能产生更大的可能性。对尼日利亚而言，这提出了一个根本性的政策问题，也是本期我最迫切想要探讨的问题。尼日利亚大学的研究能力既可以吸引企业投资、产生知识产权并支持新业务，为何还要如此严重地依赖政府拨款和学费？这不能仅仅停留在要求企业资助大学的层面，而需要大学具备开展可信研究、保护知识产权以及谈判商业合作的能力。与此同时，总部设在伦敦的全球慈善机构Wellcome于10月10日发布了一份报告，报告借鉴了对140个国家逾140,000人的访谈。其调查结果显示，自COVID-19疫情爆发以来，全球公众对科学的信任有所下降，并已低于2018年的水平。尼日利亚的情况印证了这一令人担忧的趋势。2018年，26%的尼日利亚人表示非常信任科学；到2020年，这一比例降至13%，2025年小幅回升至15%。尽管这一回升值得欢迎，但尼日利亚仍比疫情前低11个百分点。总体而言，57%的尼日利亚人表示至少在一定程度上信任科学。调查关于疫苗接种的发现，使这一挑战更加具体。被问及是否愿意接种医生或护士推荐的疫苗时，35%的尼日利亚受访者表示会立即接种；另有36%希望有 time考虑，24%则表示自己完全不接种疫苗。希望有时间考虑疫苗接种的人，并不一定反对疫苗接种，不应自动将这类顾虑斥为无知。更为重要的问题是，人们能否获得清晰、可信的答案，从而作出知情决定。疫情为此提供了重要背景。当证据发生变化时，科学建议有时也会随之改变。这不是科学的弱点，而是科学运行的方式。然而，如果当局沟通不确定性时处理不当，后续变化可能会被解读为无能或不诚实的证据。尽管如此，尼日利亚仍须抵制将所有数据变化完全归因于COVID-19的诱惑。对许多尼日利亚人而言，他们接触科学最直接的场所并非实验室或研究机构，而是医院、诊所、药房，或与卫生专业人员进行交流的谈话。Wellcome报告由此发现，对医疗机构的信心与对科学的信任之间存在重要关系。在全球范围内，对本国医院和诊所非常有信心的受访者中，43%也表示非常信任科学，而全体受访者中的这一比例为26%。经济不security又增加了另一个维度。2025年，全球生活宽裕的人群中有39%表示非常信任科学，而经济拮据、难以维持生活的人中，这一比例为20%。那些忙于应对食物、房租、学费和医疗账单的家庭，可能没有更多资源去寻求可靠信息或依照专业建议采取行动。当各类机构显得与这些困境脱节时，它们的声明也就可能缺乏分量。公平地说，尼日利亚政府已经宣布了一项可能缓解部分 challenges 的倡议。经联邦执行委员会批准，联邦政府于2026年5月宣布计划设立国家研究与创新发展基金（NRIDF），年度资金目标最高为$500 million，按当前官方汇率约为₦673 billion。该基金拟用于支持竞争性研究补助、加强创新基础设施以及推动研究成果商业化。然而，政府作出的承诺与政府实际承诺拨款之间仍有差别。$500 million这一数字公布时只是预估的年度目标。10月8日，创新、科技部部长Kingsley Udeh澄清说，由于拟议资金机制将按年度从不同来源、以不同百分比计算出资，确切金额目前尚无法确定。他还确认，相关的授权法案已提交国民议会。换言之，政府已经为这项倡议取得行政批准，但立法和资金安排尚未完全确立。宣布资金并不等于拨付预算，而拨付预算也不等于实际支付。因此，政府必须证明，该基金将建立在可持续的财政框架基础上，由独立机构治理、透明管理，并向可信研究人员开放。自Wellcome报告于10月10日发布以来，我尚未发现尼日利亚政府针对该报告作出的具体公开回应。但是，若要将研究发现转化为具有商业可行性的解决方案，尼日利亚需要开展关注本地优先事项的研究，并加强大学与产业之间的合作伙伴关系

https://www.myjoyonline.com/mahama-must-.body: The Third National Vice Chairman of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Nana Akomea, has asked President John Dramani Mahama to apologise to former President Nana Akufo-Addo for his past comments criticising the conferment of honorary degrees on serving presidents. Mr Akomea says the President’s acceptance of another honorary doctorate from a university in Russia exposes what he considers an inconsistency in the position Mr Mahama previously held on the matter. In a Facebook post on Thursday, Mr Akomea recalled that when Mr Akufo-Addo received honorary awards during his presidency, Mr Mahama questioned the appropriateness of such recognition while a person was still in office. He said the then-opposition leader had argued that Mr Akufo-Addo should have waited until after his presidency to allow for a proper assessment of his record before receiving honorary doctorates. Mr Akomea also recalled Mr Mahama’s suggestion that the former president was using the influence of his office to secure such honours from universities. However, Mr Akomea noted that President Mahama, who has been in office for less than two years, had himself received three or four honorary doctorates, including the latest recognition in Russia. Expressing mixed feelings about the latest award, he said he was happy for President Mahama but considered his acceptance of the honour inconsistent with the criticism he had directed at his predecessor. “For the sake of his Integrity, President Mahama owes President Akufo-Addo an unqualified apology on this matter of honorary awards,” he wrote
https://www.myjoyonline.com/mahama-must-.title_zh: Mahama必须就授予荣誉博士学位一事向Akufo-Addo道歉
https://www.myjoyonline.com/mahama-must-.body_zh: 新爱国党（NPP）第三全国副主席 Nana Akomea 要求总统 John Dramani Mahama 就其过去批评向在任总统授予荣誉学位的言论，向前总统 Nana Akufo-Addo 道歉。Akomea 先生表示，总统接受俄罗斯一所大学授予的另一项荣誉博士头衔，暴露了他认为 Mahama 先生此前在这一问题上的立场前后矛盾。周四，Akomea 先生在 Facebook 的一则帖子中回忆称，Akufo-Addo 先生在任总统期间获得荣誉奖项时，Mahama 先生质疑在任者接受此类荣誉是否恰当。他说，这位当时的反对党领袖认为，Akufo-Addo 先生应等到卸任后再接受荣誉博士学位，以便对其任内政绩作出适当评价。Akomea 先生还提到，Mahama 先生曾暗示前总统正利用职位影响力从各大学获取此类荣誉。然而，Akomea 先生指出，任职不足两年的 Mahama 总统自己也获得了三到四个荣誉博士学位，其中包括俄罗斯授予的最近一项荣誉。他对最新奖项表达了复杂感受，称自己为 Mahama 总统感到高兴，但认为他接受这一荣誉与此前对前任的批评不一致。他写道：“为了维护他的诚信，Mahama 总统在荣誉奖项一事上，应当无条件地向 Akufo-Addo 总统道歉。”

https://leadership.ng/2027-n50000-cash-r.summary_zh: 非洲民主大会（ADC）批评联邦政府宣布每月向民众发放50,000奈拉现金救济，称此举是选举噱头，据称源于博拉·艾哈迈德·蒂努巴总统在2027年大选前的绝望。该反对党指控蒂努巴政府通过政策让尼日利亚民众遭受严重经济困难后，又企图用现金补贴重新赢得好感。
https://leadership.ng/2027-n50000-cash-r.body: The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has criticised the Federal Government’s announcement of a N50,000 monthly cash relief payment, describing it as an election gimmick allegedly driven by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s desperation ahead of the 2027 general election. The opposition party accused the Tinubu administration of attempting to regain public goodwill through cash handouts after subjecting Nigerians to severe economic hardship through its policies. In a statement signed by its National Publicity Secretary, Mallam Bolaji Abdullahi, the ADC questioned the timing of the announcement, alleging that the intervention was a reaction to the party’s promise to reduce the cost of living and make life more affordable if elected into power in 2027. According to the party, the government has recently announced several intervention programmes without delivering meaningful relief to Nigerians. “President Tinubu is in full panic mode now. Since the ADC and our Presidential Candidate, Atiku Abubakar, have made affordability and reducing the cost of living the cardinal focus of our campaign, the government has been announcing one desperate intervention or another,” Abdullahi said. The party recalled the August announcement of a $1 billion Renewed Hope Social Intervention Fund, a proposed 30-day fuel discount, cheaper transportation across states from October 1, and a N70,000 transportation allowance for workers. It alleged that these announcements had failed to translate into meaningful improvements in the living conditions of Nigerians. The ADC also questioned the purchasing power of the proposed N50,000 payment, asking what meaningful assistance the amount could provide to households struggling with rising food, transportation, fuel and healthcare costs. “What exactly is N50,000 supposed to buy in Tinubu’s Nigeria today? How much food can a family purchase with that amount? How much transport can it cover? And for how long?” the statement queried. The party argued that petrol prices had increased significantly, with food and transportation costs also rising, making the proposed intervention inadequate to address the financial difficulties facing ordinary Nigerians. It further accused the Federal Government of failing to anticipate the hardship associated with its economic reforms, insisting that vulnerable citizens should not have to wait until an election season to receive financial assistance. According to the ADC, the government should have incorporated adequate social protection measures into its economic reform plans from the beginning rather than introducing cash relief programmes after years of economic difficulties. The party also raised concerns about transparency and accountability in the implementation of government intervention programmes, warning that the latest initiative could create another avenue for the diversion of public funds. It referenced findings attributed to the Auditor-General concerning previous cash transfer programmes, questioning whether billions of naira allocated to earlier interventions had been properly accounted for. “What has happened to the findings of the Auditor-General concerning the billions of naira in previous cash transfers that could not be properly accounted for? Have those responsible been held accountable?” the party asked. The ADC further questioned how Nigerians could be expected to trust another intervention programme when concerns surrounding previous government-funded initiatives had allegedly not been adequately addressed. It warned that the N50,000 payment could either be an election-season publicity exercise intended to influence public perception or another programme vulnerable to financial mismanagement. “At best, this is an election gimmick designed to deceive Nigerians into believing that a government which has neglected them for more than three years suddenly cares about their welfare. At worst, it could become another scheme to siphon public funds under the convenient cover of poverty alleviation,” the statement added. The opposition party maintained that sustainable solutions to Nigeria’s cost-of-living crisis must go beyond temporary cash transfers. It called for policies aimed at restoring citizens’ purchasing power and reducing the cost of essential commodities, particularly food, energy and transportation. The ADC insisted that meaningful economic relief would require addressing the underlying causes of rising living costs rather than relying on periodic financial interventions. The statement was signed by Mallam Bolaji Abdullahi, National Publicity Secretary of the African Democratic Congress. We’ve got the edge. https://leadership.ng/2027-n50000-cash-r.title_zh: 2027年：5万奈拉现金救济反映Tinubu在选举前的绝望心态
https://leadership.ng/2027-n50000-cash-r.body_zh: 非洲民主大会（ADC）批评联邦政府宣布每月向民众发放₦50,000现金救济金，称此举是选举把戏，并指其源于总统博拉·艾哈迈德·蒂努布在2027年大选前的急切心理。这个反对党指责蒂努布政府通过政策使尼日利亚人遭受严重经济困境后，又企图借助发放现金争取公众好感。在由全国宣传秘书马利姆·博拉吉·阿卜杜拉希签署的一份声明中，ADC对宣布救济金的时间提出质疑，称政府的干预是因为该党承诺若在2027年赢得执政权，将降低生活成本、让生活更加负担得起。该党表示，政府近期宣布了多项干预计划，但并未给尼日利亚人带来实质性救济。阿卜杜拉希说：“蒂努布总统现在已陷入彻底恐慌。自ADC及我们的总统候选人阿蒂库·阿布巴卡尔将生活可负担性和降低生活成本作为竞选活动的核心重点以来，政府便不断推出一个又一个急迫的干预措施。”该党回顾了政府8月宣布的10亿美元“重燃希望社会干预基金”、拟议的30天燃油折扣、10月1日起实施的各州交通降价措施，以及向工作者提供₦70,000交通津贴。该党声称，这些措施并未切实改善尼日利亚人的生活状况。ADC还质疑拟议中的₦50,000补助金所能产生的购买力，询问这笔钱能为面临食品、交通、燃油和医疗费用上涨的家庭提供何种实际帮助。声明质问道：“在今天的蒂努布治下尼日利亚，₦50,000究竟能买到什么？一个家庭能用这笔钱购买多少食品？能够支付多少交通费？又能够维持多久？”该党认为，汽油价格已大幅上涨，食品和交通成本也在攀升，因此拟议中的干预措施不足以解决普通尼日利亚人面临的经济困难。该党进一步指责联邦政府未能预先估计经济改革带来的困难，坚持认为弱势公民不应非要等到选举季才获得经济援助。ADC表示，政府本应从一开始就将军充分的社会保障措施纳入经济改革计划，而不是在经历多年经济困难后才推出现金救济计划。该党还对政府干预计划执行过程中的透明度和问责提出担忧，警告最新举措可能为挪用公共资金提供新的渠道。声明援引了审计长对以往现金转移计划的调查结果，质问此前用于干预措施的数十亿奈拉是否已得到妥善核算。阿卜杜拉希所在的ADC问道：“审计长对以往数十亿奈拉现金转移无法妥善核算的调查结论如今如何？相关责任人是否已被追究？”ADC还进一步质疑，在围绕以往政府资助举措的疑虑据称尚未得到充分解决的情况下，尼日利亚人如何被期望信任另一项干预计划。该党警告称，₦50,000补助金要么是一场意在影响公众观感的选举季宣传活动，要么又是一个容易发生财务管理的计划。声明补充道：“往好里说，这是一场选举把戏，目的是欺骗尼日利亚人，让他们相信一个忽视他们三年多的政府突然关心起他们的福祉。往坏里说，它可能成为又一个打着扶贫便利旗号侵吞公共资金的阴谋。”这个反对党坚持认为，解决尼日利亚生活成本危机的可持续方案必须超越临时现金转移。该党呼吁制定旨在恢复公民购买力、降低基本商品成本的政策，尤其应降低食品、能源和交通成本。ADC坚持认为，真正有意义的经济救济需要解决生活成本上涨的根本原因，而不能依赖间歇性的经济干预。声明由非洲民主大会全国宣传秘书马利姆·博拉吉·阿卜杜拉希签署。我们掌握独家优势。实时报道、独家内幕和独家视角将直接推送到您的手机。不要满足于陈旧新闻。加入LEADERSHIP NEWS的WhatsApp，随时获取全天候最新消息 →

https://www.premiumtimesng.com/business/.summary_zh: 专注尼日利亚市场的数字金融服务公司OPay于周五撤回原计划进行的3.04亿美元美国首次公开发行，原因是某个未具名的外国司法管辖区启动了监管调查。该公司原计划以股票代码“OPay”在纽约证券交易所上市。OPay于周五晚些时候撤回了原定的美国首次公开发行，但未说明监管机构身份及调查性质。
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/business/.body: OPay, a Nigeria-focused digital financial services company, has withdrawn its planned $304 million US initial public offering on Friday over a regulatory inquiry by a foreign jurisdiction it did not identify. The SoftBank-backed digital-payments company described the inquiry as relating to a jurisdiction immaterial to its core operations, Reuters reported. The company had earlier disclosed that it was raising $304 million in its initial public offering (IPO) and aimed to secure a market capitalisation of more than $4 billion. The company had planned to list on the NYSE under the ticker symbol “OPay.” OPay withdrew its planned US initial public offering later on Friday, but it did not identify the regulator or the nature of the inquiry. OPay said it expected the matter to be resolved satisfactorily in the near future and that the probe should not be misconstrued as a reflection of the company’s business performance, financial condition, operational integrity or regulatory standing. It explained that the inquiry would not affect its operations, regulatory standing or customer service in Nigeria or its other markets. Founded in 2018, OPay provides digital financial services across emerging markets, including Nigeria and Indonesia. Its app offers payments, money transfers, savings and loans in economies where limited access to traditional banking can make everyday transactions difficult. The company had reached a $1 billion revenue run rate in the second quarter of 2026, recording 137 per cent year-on-year growth and a 19 per cent net margin in the first six months of the year. The fintech company raised $400 million in 2021 at a valuation of $2 billion. It had about 50 million monthly active users as of 31 July, according to its IPO prospectus. Citigroup, Deutsche Bank, Standard Bank, and CICC were among the underwriters
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/business/.title_zh: OPay因海外监管调查撤回原计划进行的3.04亿美元美国IPO
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/business/.body_zh: OPay是一家专注于尼日利亚市场的数字金融 services 公司。由于一个未指明名称的外国司法管辖区发起监管调查，该公司于周五撤回了原计划规模为3.04亿美元的美国首次公开发行。路透社报道，这家获得软银支持的数字支付公司称，相关调查涉及一个与其核心业务无关紧要司法管辖区。该公司此前披露，计划通过首次公开发行募集3.04亿美元，并争取实现超过40亿美元的市值。公司原计划以股票代码“OPay”在纽约证券交易所上市。OPay于周五晚些时候撤回了原计划进行的美国首次公开发行，但没有透露监管机构身份或调查的具体性质。OPay表示，预计此事将在近期得到令人满意的解决，并称不应将调查误解为公司经营业绩、财务状况、运营完整性或监管地位的反映。公司解释道，此次调查不会影响其在尼日利亚及其他市场的业务运营、监管地位或客户服务。OPay成立于2018年，在包括尼日利亚和印度尼西亚在内的新兴市场提供数字金融服务。其应用提供支付、转账、储蓄和贷款服务；在传统银行服务覆盖有限、日常交易可能面临困难的经济体中，这些服务尤为重要。根据该公司的首次公开发行招股说明书，截至2026年7月31日，公司约有5000万月活跃用户。该金融科技公司在2026年第二季度实现了10亿美元的年化收入，较上年同期增长137%，今年前六个月净利润率为19%。这家金融科技公司于2021年融资4亿美元，估值达到20亿美元。花旗集团、德意志银行、标准银行和中金公司是承销商之一。

https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/otti.body: Gov. Alex Otti of Abia has said his administration chose Electric Vehicles (EVs) over Compressed Natural Gas (CNG)-powered buses because EVs represent an upgrade in transportation technology. Otti explained that it was for that reason that the government opted for electric buses for its public transportation system. He offered the explanation during the October edition of his monthly media chat held at the Michael Okpara Auditorium, Umuahia, on Friday night. He said that despite the preference for EVs, the State Government still encouraged the establishment of additional CNG stations in the state. “We are not opposed to CNG, but we chose electric vehicles for our public transportation system,” the governor said. He said that both petrol and CNG vehicles operate on internal combustion engines, while EVs require a different propulsion system. He further said that some companies had expressed interest in establishing additional CNG stations in the state, adding that agreements had been reached with them. He explained that the proposed stations would cater to privately owned vehicles and other consumers, rather than the state’s public transportation system. Otti said that CNG was cheaper to use than petrol and expressed optimism that the conversion of petrol and diesel vehicles to CNG would gain more traction in the country. He also said that there are Nigerian companies that specialised in converting internal combustion engine vehicles to CNG. Otti also responded to the purported complaints about the continued existence of street trading at the Umuahia city centre, popularly called Isi-Gate. According to him, street trading cannot be totally eliminated; hence, it still operates in other developed parts of the world, including London. He promised that traders that might suffer displacement by the state’s urban renewal efforts would be compensated. Otti said that the state government was working to restore order in the capital city, particularly tackling the challenges associated with street trading. He said the relocation of traders from Isi-Gate would be gradual, considering that many petty traders on the street depended on the income for their livelihoods. He said that the government was still exploring alternative locations for traders that would be affected to avoid pushing them into activities that could further undermine public order. “We are a government that is compassionate. So, if we move you out of your shop, we will pay you compensation. We will ensure that,” he said. Otti argued that displacing traders without considering their economic circumstances would defeat the purpose of the government’s urban renewal programme. “It doesn’t make sense to drive everybody away. Who are you even sanitising the place for? “So, it is a balancing act. We are handling it step by step,” he said. https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/otti.title_zh: Otti解释阿比亚州为何偏爱电动巴士而非压缩天然气巴士
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/otti.body_zh: Abia州长Alex Otti表示，他的政府选择电动汽车（EVs），而不是压缩天然气（CNG）驱动巴士，是因为电动汽车代表着交通技术的升级。Otti解释说，正因如此，政府才为公共公交系统选择电动巴士。他在10月举行的月度媒体交流活动上作出上述解释。活动于周五晚上在Umuahia的Michael Okpara Auditorium举行。他说，尽管州政府优先选择EVs，但仍在鼓励该州增设更多CNG加气站。Otti说：“我们并不反对CNG，但我们的公共公交系统选择了电动汽车。”他说，汽油车和CNG车辆都采用内燃机，而EVs需要另一套推进系统。他还表示，一些公司有意在该州增设更多CNG加气站，目前已与这些公司达成协议。他解释说，计划增设的加气站将服务私人拥有的车辆和其他消费者，而不是州政府的公共公交系统。Otti表示，CNG的使用成本低于汽油，并乐观预计，将汽油车和柴油车改装为使用CNG将在全国得到更广泛推广。他还说，尼日利亚有一些公司专门从事将内燃机汽车改装为CNG车辆。Otti还回应了有关Umuahia市中心俗称Isi-Gate的区域仍然存在街头摆卖活动的所谓投诉。据他所说，街头摆卖无法彻底消除，因此世界上其他发达地区，包括London，也依然存在这种活动。他承诺，可能因州政府推进城市更新而被迫迁离的商贩将获得补偿。Otti表示，州政府正努力恢复这座首府城市的秩序，尤其着力解决街头摆卖带来的问题。他说，考虑到许多街头小贩依靠这项收入维持生计，将商贩迁出Isi-Gate的工作将逐步推进。他还表示，政府仍在为受影响的商贩寻找其他安置地点，以免迫使他们从事可能进一步破坏公共秩序的活动。他说：“我们是一个富有同情心的政府。因此，如果我们将你们从店铺迁出，就会向你们支付补偿。我们会确保这一点。”Otti认为，不考虑商贩的经济状况就迫使他们迁离，将使政府的城市更新计划适得其反。他说：“把所有人都赶走是说不通的。你们究竟是为了谁才整治这个地方？所以，这需要权衡取舍。我们正逐步处理此事。”（ NAN ）此处发表的意见不代表《Vanguard》报社及其任何员工的观点。

https://leadership.ng/lagos-intensifies-.body: The state government, during the exercise led by the wife of Lagos State Governor, Dr Ibijoke Sanwo-Olu, in the Ajina area of Ikorodu Local Government, and the Head of Service, Mr Bode Agoro, in the Ikeja area of the state, warned that the practice undermines sanitation efforts and increases the risk of flooding. The wife of the Lagos State Governor, Dr Ibijoke Sanwo-Olu, disclosed this while monitoring the monthly environmental sanitation exercise in Ikorodu. The governor’s wife urged residents of Ikorodu to sustain the exercise beyond the last Saturday of every month and work towards emerging as the cleanest Local Government Area in the state. She emphasised that continuous public sensitisation remains essential for promoting environmental cleanliness, despite the challenges of behavioural change. Mrs Sanwo-Olu encouraged residents to embrace proper sanitation practices in their homes, schools, markets and communities, stressing that keeping Lagos clean is a collective responsibility. She commended the active participation of residents, particularly children, youths, market traders and environmental sanitation workers, who turned out early to clean their surroundings. In the same vein, Agoro said the exercise was the seventh since March, calling on local government chairpersons and their executives to mobilise residents to improve environmental cleanliness. He stressed that sanitation must be a continuous responsibility, noting that government officials observed residents dumping refuse into canals during the exercise. According to him, the Ministry of the Environment has been notified to clear affected canals, while plans are also underway to reconstruct a canal in the area in consultation with the relevant drainage authorities. Agoro, however, cautioned that clearing the canals would achieve little if residents continued to dispose of waste indiscriminately. We’ve got the edge. https://leadership.ng/cbn-appoints-8-pre.summary_zh: 这份通告依据《1996年第10号进口装运前检验法》印发，发给获授权的经销商银行、尼日利亚海关总署、尼日利亚上游石油监管委员会（NUPRC）、尼日利亚国家石油有限公司、尼日利亚中游和下游石油监管局、码头运营商、石油天然气公司及公众。
https://leadership.ng/cbn-appoints-8-pre.body: The appointments take effect from October 2, 2026, under the Nigerian Export Supervision Scheme. They were contained in a circular dated October 29, 2026 (ref: TED/FEM/FPC/PUB/001/005), signed by Aderinola Shonekan, Director of the Trade and Exchange Department. The circular, issued in line with the Pre-shipment Inspection of Imports Act No. 10 of 1996, is addressed to authorised dealer banks, the Nigeria Customs Service, the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC), the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited, the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority, terminal operators, oil and gas companies and the public. It directs all of them to ensure compliance. Arlington Securitas Nigeria Ltd will monitor Dakee Engineering and Construction Ltd, Trobell International Nigeria Ltd, Robinson International Energy Ltd and Integrated Shipping Services Nigeria Ltd. The latest move follows several adjustments to the scheme. In May 2024, the CBN appointed 11 agents: nine pre-shipment inspection agents and two monitoring and evaluation agents. Dakee Engineering and Construction and Arlington Securitas were on that list. The allocation of terminals was reviewed in March 2025. In July 2026, the bank named Candid Oil Services Ltd as inspection agent for the Taurus Oil and Gas Depot. The new circular changes the companies responsible for inspecting export cargoes and the terminals each one covers. The appointments come as gas export earnings grow. According to CBN data, Nigeria earned $2.53 billion from gas exports in the first quarter of 2026. We’ve got the edge. https://punchng.com/aiyedatiwa-plans-cal.body: The Ondo State Government plans to establish a youth call centre, to be known as the Ondo State Youth Call Centre, as a channel of communication between the government and young people. The initiative is designed to provide a direct and accessible communication channel between the government and youths across the state’s 18 Local Government Areas. This was contained in a statement issued on Saturday by the Special Assistant to Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa on Youth and Social Inclusion, Comrade Henry Okunomo. According to the statement, the centre will serve as a central platform where young people can “make enquiries, seek information about employment and empowerment opportunities, report challenges, submit complaints, access relevant government interventions and communicate their concerns directly to the appropriate authorities.” The statement read, “The initiative will also promote youth participation in governance, strengthen social inclusion, facilitate access to educational and entrepreneurial opportunities and ensure that the voices of young people, particularly those in underserved and riverine communities, are heard and appropriately addressed. Ondo bizman commits suicide, family cries foul play N70,000 allowance: Labour turns heat on govs My sister fears losing Air Force home after husband’s death — Sister-in-law “Through this platform, the Office of the Special Assistant to the Governor on Youth and Social Inclusion seeks to bridge the communication gap between government and young people while establishing a more structured mechanism for identifying, documenting and responding to youth-related concerns. “The centre will also facilitate referrals to relevant Ministries, Departments and Agencies, ensuring that enquiries and complaints receive appropriate attention.” The statement added that the initiative reflected an approach to youth engagement that recognised young people not merely as beneficiaries of government policies but as important stakeholders in governance, development and social transformation. “The youth call centre meets the 21st century rapid response and synergy required for youth and social inclusion. The official launch, operational arrangements and communication channels will be made public in due course,” the statement concluded. Peter Dada
https://punchng.com/aiyedatiwa-plans-cal.title_zh: Aiyedatiwa计划设立呼叫中心，与奥多州青年沟通
https://punchng.com/aiyedatiwa-plans-cal.body_zh: 奥多州政府计划设立一个青年呼叫中心，名为“奥多州青年呼叫中心”，作为政府与年轻人沟通的渠道。该举措旨在为政府与全州18个地方政府辖区的青年建立直接且便捷的沟通渠道。州长Lucky Aiyedatiwa青年与社会包容事务特别助理Henry Okunomo同志于星期六发布的声明中提到了这一点。声明称，该中心将作为统一平台，让年轻人可以“查询情况、了解就业和赋权机会、报告难题、提交投诉、获取相关政府援助，并直接向主管机关反映诉求”。声明写道：“该举措还将促进青年参与治理，加强社会包容，便利青年获取教育与创业机会，并确保年轻人的声音，尤其是服务不足地区和河流社区青年的声音得到倾听和妥善处理。奥多州商人自杀，家人质疑存在他杀N70,000津贴：劳工加强对政府的施压 我的姐姐担心丈夫去世后失去空军家属住宅——嫂子‘通过这一平台，州长青年与社会包容事务特别助理办公室力求弥合政府与年轻人之间的沟通鸿沟，同时建立一套更有条理的机制，用于识别、记录和回应与青年有关的问题。‘该中心还将协助向相关部委、部门和机构转介事项，确保咨询和投诉得到妥善处理。’声明补充称，该举措体现了一种青年参与方针，即承认年轻人不仅是政府政策的受益者，也是治理、发展和社会转型的重要利益相关者。‘青年呼叫中心满足了青年与社会包容工作对21世纪快速响应和协同配合的要求。正式启动、运营安排和沟通渠道将在适当时候公布。’声明最后说道。Peter Dada

https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/more.summary_zh: 总统博拉·蒂努布欢迎Airtel Nigeria启动“开放网络”计划，称这是迈向提高透明度、保护消费者权益和改善尼日利亚电信服务的一项积极举措。蒂努布总统表示，该计划契合其政府鼓励私营部门投资、扩大数字基础设施，并确保尼日利亚民众享受到更加可靠和便捷电信服务的承诺。
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/more.body: President Bola Tinubu has welcomed the launch of Airtel Nigeria’s Open Network initiative, describing it as a positive step towards greater transparency, consumer protection and improved telecommunications services in Nigeria. President Tinubu said the initiative aligns with his administration’s commitment to encouraging private-sector investment, expanding digital infrastructure, and ensuring Nigerians benefit from more reliable and accessible telecommunications services. He welcomed the growing emphasis on transparency in the sector, including the NCC’s public network coverage maps, performance information and consumer satisfaction surveys, which help Nigerians better understand the services available to them and hold operators accountable. The president also highlighted the federal government’s recent Zero-Rated Access to Educational Platforms and Content Initiative, implemented through the NCC in collaboration with the Federal Ministry of Education and telecommunications operators. The programme, designed to provide eligible students with up to 100MB of free daily data to access approved educational websites and learning resources, reflects his administration’s determination to make digital opportunities more accessible, particularly to young Nigerians. He welcomed Airtel Nigeria’s continued investment in network expansion, which has seen its infrastructure grow from approximately 15,000 sites two years ago to more than 17,000 nationwide. The expansion includes more than 1,050 network sites added during the company’s 2025/26 financial year, including 657 5G sites. President Tinubu said sustained investment in telecommunications infrastructure is essential to expanding broadband access, improving network capacity, and supporting businesses, education, and economic opportunities across Nigeria. He commended the NCC, under the leadership of Dr Maida, for its continued efforts to strengthen regulatory oversight, promote transparency and protect telecommunications consumers. The president urged operators to sustain investment in network expansion, particularly in underserved communities, and ensure that customer complaints receive timely attention. He emphasised that the success of telecommunications investment and innovation must ultimately be measured by the experience of Nigerians who depend on these services for their livelihoods, businesses and everyday communication. President Tinubu reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to maintaining a business environment that encourages responsible investment and innovation while ensuring that consumer interests remain central to telecommunications development. He called on operators to translate their investments into better network coverage, fewer service disruptions and more responsive customer service for Nigerians
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/more.body_zh: 总统博拉·蒂努布对Airtel Nigeria启动开放网络倡议表示欢迎，称这是迈向加强尼日利亚网络透明度、消费者保护和改善电信服务的一步积极举措。蒂努布总统表示，该倡议契合其政府鼓励私营部门投资、扩大数字基础设施并确保尼日利亚民众受益于更可靠、更易获取的电信服务的承诺。他欢迎电信行业日益重视透明度，包括NCC发布的公共网络覆盖地图、绩效信息和消费者满意度调查，这些举措有助于尼日利亚民众更好地了解可获得的各项服务，并督促运营商履行职责。总统还强调，联邦政府近期推出了“教育平台与内容零费率接入倡议”，由NCC与联邦教育部及电信运营商协作实施。该计划旨在向符合条件的用户提供每天最多100MB的免费流量，以便访问获批的教育网站和学习资源，体现了其政府决心让数字机会更加普及，尤其是惠及尼日利亚年轻人。他欢迎Airtel Nigeria持续投资扩大网络覆盖，其基础设施已从两年前的约15,000个站点增至全国超过17,000个站点。公司在2025/26财年新增了超过1,050个网络站点，其中包括657个5G站点。蒂努布总统表示，持续投资电信基础设施对于扩大宽带接入、提升网络容量以及支持尼日利亚各地的企业、教育和经济机会至关重要。他赞扬NCC在Maida博士领导下持续努力加强监管、促进透明度并保护电信消费者。总统敦促运营商持续投资扩大网络覆盖，尤其是服务不足的社区，并确保客户投诉得到及时处理。他强调，电信投资与创新的成效最终必须以尼日利亚民众的实际体验来衡量，因为民众依靠这些服务维持生计、经营业务和日常通信。蒂努布总统重申，其政府致力于维护鼓励负责任投资与创新的营商环境，同时确保消费者利益始终是电信发展的核心。他呼吁运营商将投资转化为更好的网络覆盖、更少的服务中断以及为尼日利亚民众提供更迅速响应的客户服务。

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/31/t.body: President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has approved the appointment of Professor Murtala Muhammad Ahmad as the seventh substantive Chief Medical Director (CMD) of the Usmanu Danfodiyo University Teaching Hospital (UDUTH), Sokoto. In a statement by the Head, Public Affairs, UDUTH, Mansur Wadata, the appointment is for an initial term of four years with effect from October 20, 2026, and was conveyed in a letter signed by the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Muhammad Ali Pate. Professor Ahmad succeeds Professor Anas Ahmad Sabir, who successfully completed his two-term tenure in May this year. The statement further stated that while congratulating him on the appointment, Professor Pate reminded him of the heavy responsibilities of his new office and the yearnings of Nigerians for an effective and responsive healthcare delivery system. He urged the new CMD to justify the confidence reposed in him by Mr. President by working collaboratively with all stakeholders to ensure that the hospital continues to deliver quality healthcare services to Nigerians. Professor Ahmad becomes the second alumnus of the Usmanu Danfodiyo University to lead the Teaching Hospital as Chief Medical Director, marking a historic milestone for the institution. With over two decades of experience in Paediatrics and Child Health, Professor Ahmad brings a robust blend of clinical expertise, university teaching, and hospital administration to his new role. He earned his Bachelor of Medicine and Bachelor of Surgery (MBBS) degree from the Usmanu Danfodiyo University, followed by a Fellowship of the West African College of Physicians (FWACP) in Paediatrics and a Professional Diploma in Education from Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria. He also holds specialized certifications in paediatric electroencephalography, health leadership, management, and public administration from the University of Cape Town, University of Washington and Administrative Staff College of Nigeria (ASCON) respectively. Before his elevation, Professor Ahmad built an impressive administrative track record within both the university and the teaching hospital, steadily climbing the academic ladder from Lecturer I to Senior Lecturer, Reader, and ultimately Professor of Paediatrics. He previously served as Deputy Chairman of the Medical Advisory Committee (Training) at UDUTH for four years, where he brought impactful transformation to the administration of residency and training in the hospital. He also held key roles as Deputy Director of the Institute of Child Health and Faculty Examinations Officer in the Faculty of Clinical Sciences, alongside representing the faculty on the University Senate, and stepped in as Acting Chairman of the Medical Advisory Committee and Acting Chief Medical Director on multiple occasions. Beyond institutional management, Professor Ahmad has been at the forefront of public health service and specialised medical research in Sokoto State and across Nigeria, with active involvement in maternal and perinatal death surveillance and response, and as a national trainer on the management of severe acute malnutrition. As a prolific researcher, he has published widely in peer-reviewed journals focusing on child health, child neurology, epilepsy, and broader paediatric health concerns, while actively mentoring the next generation of medical professionals and postgraduate students. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/31/t.title_zh: Tinubu任命Ahmad教授为UDUTH首席医疗官
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/31/t.body_zh: 总统Bola Ahmed Tinubu已批准任命Murtala Muhammad Ahmad教授为位于Sokoto的Usmanu Danfodiyo University Teaching Hospital（UDUTH）第七任正式首席医务主任（CMD）。UDUTH公共事务负责人Mansur Wadata在一份声明中表示，此次任命的首个任期为4年，自2026年10月20日起生效，任命通知由卫生与社会保障协调部长Muhammad Ali Pate教授签署的函件传达。Pate教授在声明中进一步表示，他祝贺Ahmad教授获得任命，同时提醒他将承担新职位赋予的重任，以及尼日利亚人民对高效且能及时回应的医疗服务体系的期待。他敦促新任CMD通过与所有利益相关方协作，不辜负总统先生对他的信任，确保医院继续为尼日利亚人民提供优质医疗服务。Ahmad教授成为第二位以首席医务主任身份领导该教学医院的Usmanu Danfodiyo University校友，标志该校迎来历史性里程碑。Ahmad教授拥有20多年的儿科和儿童健康经验，将丰富的临床专业能力、大学教学经验和医院管理经验融入新职位。他从Usmanu Danfodiyo University取得医学学士与外科学士（MBBS）学位，随后取得西非内科医师学院（FWACP）儿科专业进修资格，并从Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria取得教育专业文凭。他还从University of Cape Town取得儿科脑电图和健康领导力认证，从University of Washington取得管理认证，并从Administrative Staff College of Nigeria（ASCON）取得公共行政认证。在此次晋升之前，Ahmad教授在大学和教学医院都取得了出色的行政管理成绩，并逐步晋升学术职级，先后担任一级讲师、高级讲师、Reader，最终成为儿科教授。他此前在UDUTH担任医学咨询委员会（培训）副主席4年，期间推动医院住院医师培训及培训管理工作的 impactful 转型。他还曾担任儿童健康研究所副所长、临床科学学院考试事务官等重要职务，代表学院参加大学评议会，并多次代理医学咨询委员会主席和首席医务主任职务。除机构管理外，Ahmad教授还一直处于Sokoto州及尼日利亚各地公共卫生服务和专业医疗研究的前沿，积极参与孕产妇和围产期死亡监测与应对工作，并担任重度急性营养不良管理领域的全国培训师。作为成果丰硕的研究者，他在同行评审期刊上广泛发表研究论文，重点关注儿童健康、儿童神经病学、癫痫以及更广泛的儿科健康问题，同时积极指导下一代医疗专业人员和研究生。THISDAY于1995年1月22日创办，由THISDAY NEWSPAPERS LTD.出版，地址为35 Creek Road Apapa, Lagos, Nigeria，并在尼日利亚36个州、联邦首都辖区及世界各地设有办公室。该报是面向政治、商业、专业和外交精英以及更广泛中产阶层的尼日利亚最具权威性的全平台新闻媒体，同时为有抱负者和千禧一代提供汇聚新思想、文化与技术的交汇点。该报秉持公共信托精神，致力于追求真相与理性，报道范围从突发新闻、政治、商业、金融市场、艺术、体育和社区延伸至人与社会的交汇点。您可以发送电子邮件至hello@thisdaylive.com或访问我们的联系我们页面

https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/poli.body: Layer 1 The Zamfara Commissioner of Police, CP Muhammad Bello, has confirmed the rescue of three of the six Islamic Clerics (Imam) kidnapped on September 12, while travelling to Talata Mafara, Zamfara. Bello gave the confirmation in an interview with some select reporters on Friday in Gusau. He said the rescue followed a multi-agency collaboration and seamless synergy between the Office of the National Security Adviser (ONSA), the Department of State Services (DSS) and police operatives. The CP said security tactical operations remained ongoing in full force, leveraging real-time intelligence supplied by local community members to track down the remaining armed bandits and ensure the safe rescue of the three clerics still in captivity. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the ONSA, in a high-stakes intelligence-driven collaboration with the DSS and the Nigeria Police Force (NPF), rescued the three Islamic clerics kidnapped while en route to a special prayer session for President Bola Tinubu in Talata Mafara, Zamfara. NAN also reports that the victims were part of a group of six Islamic clerics abducted on Sept. 12, when heavily armed bandits intercepted them around 11:30 a.m. on the Dakko-Damri feeder road near Sububu Forest in Bakura Local Government Area. The clerics, identified as Imam Yahuza, Magawata Abdullahi, Malam Shehu Dakko, Imam Bala Fagon and Na’ibi Tasi’u, were travelling to Talata Mafara to attend a special prayer gathering to seek divine favour for Tinubu’s administration. Their abductors had reportedly demanded N30 million ransom for their release. A senior security operative involved in the extraction also confirmed that the three clerics were rescued unhurt following meticulous, intelligence-led manoeuvres. NAN learnt that the clerics are said to be in stable condition after receiving medical evaluation and expert debriefing. The security operatives confirmed that the three clerics were slated for formal handover to the Zamfara Government to reunite them with their families. The Police command assured that operational leads would continue, urging the public to maintain a vigilant flow of timely, actionable information to help flush out terrorist elements across the region. https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/poli.body_zh: 第1层 扎姆法拉州警察局长穆罕默德·贝洛确认，6名于9月12日在前往扎姆法拉州塔拉塔马法拉途中遭绑架的伊斯兰教clerics（伊玛目）中，已有3人获救。贝洛周五在古绍接受部分记者采访时证实了這一消息。他说，此次营救行动由国家安全顾问办公室（ONSA）、国家情报局（DSS）和警察人员多方协作、密切配合完成。警察局长表示，安全部门仍在全力开展战术行动，利用当地社区居民提供的实时情报追查其余武装劫匪，并确保仍被拘押的3名clerics安全获救。尼日利亚通讯社（NAN）报道，ONSA与DSS及尼日利亚警察部队（NPF）在情报主导的高风险协作行动中，救出了3名在前往扎姆法拉州塔拉塔马法拉参加总统博拉·蒂努布特别祈祷会途中遭绑架的伊斯兰教clerics。NAN还报道，遇害者属于9月12日一起绑架案的6名伊斯兰教clerics。当天上午11时30分左右，重武装劫匪在巴库拉地方政府辖区苏布武森林附近的达克奥—达姆里支线公路上拦截了他们。这些clerics被确认为伊玛目亚胡扎、马加瓦塔·阿卜杜拉希、马拉姆谢胡·达克奥、伊玛目巴拉·法贡和奈比·塔西乌，他们当时正前往塔拉塔马法拉，参加一场特别祈祷集会，为蒂努布政府祈求神的眷顾。据报道，绑架者要求支付3000万奈拉赎金后才肯放人。参与营救行动的一名高级安全官员也证实，经过周密筹划、以情报为导向的行动，3名clerics已安全获救，毫发无损。NAN获悉，这些clerics在接受医学检查和专家询问后状况稳定。安全行动人员证实，这3名clerics将正式移交给扎姆法拉州政府，以便与家人团聚。警方指挥部保证将继续追查行动线索，并敦促公众保持警惕，及时提供切实可行的情报，协助清除该地区各地的恐怖分子。此处发表的意见不代表《Vanguard》报及其任何员工的观点

He, however, stressed the need for effective communication of government policies at both federal and state levels to help citizens understand their objectives, implementation and expected benefits.

https://dailytrust.com/government-reform.body: Vice-President Kashim Shettima has defended the federal government’s economic reforms, saying they are designed to create an enabling environment for investment, strengthen businesses and improve the country’s productive capacity. He, however, stressed the need for effective communication of government policies at both federal and state levels to help citizens understand their objectives, implementation and expected benefits. Shettima spoke in Abuja at the Dukes Masterclass on Penetrative Leadership, where he highlighted the importance of effective communication in governance and the digital economy. “The reforms undertaken by this administration, including the fuel subsidy removal, foreign exchange market liberalisation, fiscal restructuring and revenue mobilisation, represent important steps towards building a more productive, competitive and resilient economy. “These decisions require courage, but beyond the decisions themselves, they are intended to create an environment in which investments can grow, businesses can plan with greater confidence, public resources can be deployed more effectively, and the productive capacity of our people can be better harnessed,” he said. He said the government must communicate its policies clearly, provide credible evidence of progress and listen to citizens’ experiences to build public confidence in its programmes. In his opening address, Otunba Bimbo Ashiru, speaking on the theme, ‘Penetrative Leadership: Definitive Strategies in Robust Crisis and Reputational Management in an Increasingly Chaotic World Order’, also underscored the importance of effective policy communication by leaders and government officials. https://dailytrust.com/government-reform.title_zh: 政府实施旨在吸引投资的改革
https://dailytrust.com/government-reform.body_zh: 副总统卡希姆·谢蒂马为联邦政府的经济改革辩护，称这些改革旨在营造有利于投资的环境、强化企业竞争力并提升国家的生产能力。但他强调，联邦和州两级政府都必须有效沟通政策，帮助公民了解政策的目标、执行方式及预期收益。谢蒂马在阿布贾举行的Dukes Masterclass“深入领导力”论坛上发言，重点指出有效沟通在治理和数字经济中的重要性。他说：“本届政府推出的改革，包括取消燃油补贴、外汇市场自由化、财政结构调整和增加财政收入，都是建设更具生产力、竞争力和韧性的经济的重要步骤。这些决定需要勇气，但这些决定本身不仅旨在投资能够增长、企业能够更有信心地制定规划、公共资源得到更有效的调配，而且还要让我们人民的生产能力得到更充分的发挥。”他说，政府必须清楚传达政策，提供可信的进展证据，并倾听公民的亲身体验，以增强公众对其各项计划的信心。在开幕致辞中，Otunba Bimbo Ashiru围绕“深入领导力：在日益混乱的世界秩序中稳健应对危机与维护声誉的明确策略”这一主题，也强调了领导人和政府官员有效沟通政策的重要性。加入《每日信任报》WhatsApp群，方便快速获取身边的新闻和动态

https://dailytrust.com/nasu-issues-ultim.summary: The Yobe State Council of the Non-Academic Staff Union of Educational and Associated Institutions (NASU) has issued a 14-day ultimatum to the state government to address three key welfare demands or risk industrial action. The ultimatum, which took effect on October 28, 2026, expires at midnight on November 11.
https://dailytrust.com/nasu-issues-ultim.summary_zh: 约贝州教育及相关机构非学术人员工会（NASU）州委员会已向州政府发出最后通牒，要求其在14天内处理三项关键的福利诉求，否则将面临工业行动。最后通牒于2026年10月28日生效，将于11月11日午夜到期。
https://dailytrust.com/nasu-issues-ultim.body: The Yobe State Council of the Non-Academic Staff Union of Educational and Associated Institutions (NASU) has issued a 14-day ultimatum to the state government to address three key welfare demands or risk industrial action. The ultimatum, which took effect on October 28, 2026, expires at midnight on November 11. The union’s position was contained in a statement signed by its state chairman, Comrade Ali Usman. Among its demands is the implementation of the 65-year retirement age for non-academic staff in state-owned tertiary institutions. The union is also demanding the immediate implementation of the reviewed 2024 salary table under the Consolidated Tertiary Institutions Salary Structure (CONTEDISS), as well as the approval and implementation of the Consolidated Non-Teaching Tools Allowance (CONTTA) and applicable Earned Allowance (EA). While acknowledging the contributions of lecturers to the development of tertiary institutions, the union said non-academic staff also played critical roles in the administrative, technical and operational activities necessary for the effective running of the institutions. It argued that the failure to give non-academic staff equal consideration could undermine institutional efficiency and harmonious industrial relations. The statement added that the prolonged delay in addressing the demands had generated widespread dissatisfaction among members and negatively affected staff morale across the affected institutions. The union urged the state government to use the 14-day ultimatum to take concrete steps towards resolving the issues, warning that failure to meet the demands by November 11 would prompt its leadership to reconvene on November 12 to determine the next line of action in accordance with labour laws. It appealed to Governor Mai Mala Buni and other relevant government stakeholders to intervene and address the demands to avert industrial unrest and possible disruption of academic and administrative activities in the state’s tertiary institutions.
